> *Example (non-normative): a player with two Fireballs in the battle region casts one; both go on the stack. A Fireball the same player has in another region is not cast (illustrative).* <sub>test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.casting.spell-tokens.burst — both battle-region Fireballs are cast together and one in another region is not</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 2 tests run · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.4; Rulebook 2023 p.4; Rulebook 2023 p.4 · Rulings: R309 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.casting.spell-tokens.burst</sub>

<a id="r702.8"></a>**702.8.** A card or ability that needs targets can be played only if every target it requires can be chosen at the same time, each one legal and different from the others. See rule 110.

> *Example (non-normative): Fight cannot be played unless the region holds an ally and another unit.* <sub>test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ target requirements: Fight cannot be played without an ally and another unit in the region</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Tidal Reversion cannot be played while one player has no unit to recall.* <sub>test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ target requirements: Tidal Reversion is not playable while one player has no unit to recall</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 3 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1410252965276684418#0; RAQ 1410252965276684418#1; RAQ 1410252965276684418#3 · Rulings: R323 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts, 401-raq-fix-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.casting.targets-required</sub>

<a id="r702.8a"></a>**702.8a** A card that targets nothing has no target requirement.

> *Example (non-normative): Rebalance can be played by a player with no unit.* <sub>test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::Rebalance is playable with no unit of your own</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1454169054402314362#1 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Key: effects.casting.targets-required.untargeted</sub>

<a id="r702.8b"></a>**702.8b** A triggered graft composite whose targeted part has no legal target is not put on the stack at all, and its untargeted parts do not happen either. See rules 722, 706. *(Engine differs, see F-U14-1.)*

> *Example (non-normative): Megadeath grafted with Resurrect, and no unit of cost 2 or less in the bin: no Poison 5 is made.* <sub>test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ target requirements: a graft trigger with a required target and none available makes nothing at all</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1410252965276684418#2 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.casting.targets-required.graft-trigger</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U14-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r703"></a>
### 703. The Stack and Priority

<a id="r703.1"></a>**703.1.** The stack is "first in, last out". A new effect is put on top of the effects already there. When it is time to resolve, the top effect resolves first, so the effect put on last resolves first.

> *Example (non-normative): Mycelial Mentor is played with Bloomcaster out. Bloomcaster's trigger goes on the stack above the Mentor, so its 1/1 is made before the Mentor arrives and the Mentor never sees it.* <sub>test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Bloomcaster: its 1/1 resolves before the Mycelial Mentor it was played with arrives</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.14; Rulebook 2023 p.14 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Key: effects.priority.stack</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U01-12 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r703.1a"></a>**703.1a** An effect put on the stack does not resolve immediately. This gives the other players in the region a chance to respond to it.

> *Example (non-normative): Luminous Arc is cast at a unit; the unit is undamaged while the Arc waits on the stack, and the other player may respond.* <sub>test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.priority.stack.not-immediate — a cast Luminous Arc waits on the stack, its target untouched, while the other player may respond</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.28; Manual p.28 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.priority.stack.not-immediate</sub>

<a id="r703.1b"></a>**703.1b** New effects can be added on top of the stack after it has started resolving, between the resolutions of the effects on it.

> *Example (non-normative): two Luminous Arcs are on the stack; after the top one resolves, a third Arc is cast and resolves before the one still waiting.* <sub>test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.priority.stack.add-while-resolving — after the top of a two-item stack resolves, a new spell goes on above the remaining item and resolves first</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.14; Manual p.28 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.priority.stack.add-while-resolving</sub>

<a id="r703.1c"></a>**703.1c** A triggered ability put on the stack can be responded to like any other effect. See rule 706.

> *Example (non-normative): Xenopod Progenitor's trigger is negated on the stack, and its controller is never asked to pay its [1].* <sub>test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ Xenopod: negated on the stack, it never asks for the [1]</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: Manual p.28 · Designer: RAQ 1397189214352703590#1 · Rulings: R250 (the owner's §3 statement that all triggers are respondable) · Replaces: R250 (its §3 conclusion that combat-damage triggers are not respondable was reversed by R261; its deployment half was amended by R286) · Tests: 229-cosmic-and-control.test.ts, 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.priority.stack.triggers-respondable</sub>

<a id="r703.2"></a>**703.2.** Priority is the ability to take game actions such as playing cards or activating abilities. A player with priority can take such actions; a player without priority cannot.

> *Example (non-normative): in the attack window only the initiative player, who holds priority, is offered a card; the other player’s play is refused.* <sub>test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.priority.priority — only the player with priority may play a card</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.30; Manual p.30 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.priority.priority</sub>

<a id="r703.2a"></a>**703.2a** A player who uses priority to take an action may keep priority and take further actions. Each action goes on the stack as an effect; none of them happens immediately. *(Engine differs, see F-U14-2.) (Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.30; Manual p.30 · Key: effects.priority.priority.hold</sub>

<a id="r703.2b"></a>**703.2b** When a player passes priority after taking one or more actions, each other player receives priority, so that they can respond. This continues until all players pass priority in succession.

> *Example (non-normative): after a cast the other player receives priority and responds; the first player then receives priority again, and the top item resolves only after both pass in succession.* <sub>test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.priority.priority.pass — after an action the other player receives priority, and the item resolves only once both pass in succession</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.30; Manual p.30 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.priority.priority.pass</sub>

<a id="r703.2c"></a>**703.2c** A player cannot respond to another player passing priority. A player who passes may not get another chance to act.

> *Example (non-normative): the defender passes on an Arc and the attacker passes; the Arc resolves at once, with no further chance for the defender.* <sub>test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.priority.priority.no-response-to-pass — after one player passes, the other passing resolves the item with no further chance for the first</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.13 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.priority.priority.no-response-to-pass</sub>

<a id="r703.2d"></a>**703.2d** All players on a team share priority and can act in whichever order they choose among themselves. Teams pass and receive priority as one. See rule 904. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.30; Manual p.30 · Key: effects.priority.priority.teams</sub>

<a id="r703.3"></a>**703.3.** A priority window is a sequence in which the players (or teams) each receive priority in order.

> *Example (non-normative): in an empty attack window the initiative player receives priority, then the other player; when both have passed the step ends.* <sub>test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.priority.window — in an empty attack window each player receives priority in turn, initiative first, and then the step moves on</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.30; Manual p.30 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.priority.window</sub>

<a id="r703.3a"></a>**703.3a** In a priority window the initiative player receives priority first. If they decline to act, priority passes clockwise to the next non-initiative player in the region. If the initiative player is not in the region, priority begins with the player nearest to the initiative player, clockwise. See rules 508, 903.

> *Example (non-normative): the defender casts a spell, which resolves; the new window opens with the initiative player, not the caster.* <sub>test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.priority.window.order — a new window opens with the initiative player even when the other player cast the item that just resolved</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.30; Manual p.30; Manual p.30 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.priority.window.order</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U14-8 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r703.3b"></a>**703.3b** In each region, the attack step, the block step and the after combat step each have a priority window. The combat damage step has a priority window only between its sub-steps, and only when Swift or Sluggish units split it (rule 608). See rules 604, 605, 607, 608, 609.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: Manual p.30 · Designer: RAQ 1363298910528864318#0 · Tests: 297-damage-substeps-are-steps.test.ts · Key: effects.priority.window.steps</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U14-1 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r703.3c"></a>**703.3c** When all players pass priority in succession with an effect on the stack, the top effect resolves. All players then receive priority in order again, which is a new priority window. When all players pass priority with the stack empty, the game moves to the next step.

> *Example (non-normative): two passes resolve Luminous Arc; a new window opens in the same step with the initiative player; two passes on the empty stack end the step.* <sub>test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.priority.window.resolve — two passes resolve the top item, a new window opens, and two passes on the empty stack end the step</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.30; Manual p.30; Rulebook 2023 p.13 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.priority.window.resolve</sub>

<a id="r703.4"></a>**703.4.** When several effects are put on the stack at the same time, each player chooses the order of their own. The initiative player puts all of theirs on first, then the non-initiative player, so the non-initiative player's effects resolve first. See rule 706.

> *Example (non-normative): with one trigger per player, the initiative player's trigger is at the bottom of the stack.* <sub>test: 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts::R261 RAQ STACK ORDER</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.43; Manual p.43 · Designer: RAQ 1540678747953569832#1 · Rulings: R2 · Tests: 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts · Key: effects.priority.simultaneous</sub>

<a id="r703.4a"></a>**703.4a** Cards played by one effect at the same time are separate effects, put on the stack at the same time in an order their controller chooses.

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1396955380000755795#4 · Tests: 169-mid-resolution-window.test.ts · Key: effects.priority.simultaneous.same-effect</sub>

<a id="r703.4b"></a>**703.4b** A Burst group of spell tokens goes on the stack all at once. Its caster chooses the order, one token at a time, and aims each; the token chosen first resolves first. The other players receive priority only when the whole group is on the stack. See rule 803.

> *Example (non-normative): the first Fireball picked ends on top of the stack.* <sub>test: 358-burst-order.test.ts::R309: the caster picks each Fireball in RESOLVE order and aims it</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Rulings: R309, R309 · Tests: 358-burst-order.test.ts · Key: effects.priority.simultaneous.burst</sub>

<a id="r703.5"></a>**703.5.** A card played during another effect's resolution waits on the stack until that resolution has finished. Only then do players receive priority, and they may respond to the played card before it resolves. See rule 701.4. *(Engine differs, see F-U14-3.)*

> *Example (non-normative): a card Tides of the Cosmos plays for free can be answered on the stack.* <sub>test: 169-mid-resolution-window.test.ts::a free play is still a play, so it can be answered on the stack</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1396955380000755795#4 · Rulings: R198 · Tests: 169-mid-resolution-window.test.ts · Key: effects.priority.mid-resolution</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U14-5 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r703.6"></a>**703.6.** Once an effect has begun to resolve, no player can respond to it. It can no longer be targeted, negated or augmented.

> *Example (non-normative): while Premonition is resolving, the other player is offered nothing, it is not a legal target, and a negation or a Virus aimed at it is refused.* <sub>test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.priority.resolving — while Premonition is resolving it cannot be targeted, negated, augmented or responded to</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Rulings: R78, R79 (its stack-virus half) · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.priority.resolving</sub>

<a id="r703.7"></a>**703.7.** Deployment uses the stack, but each player has a stack of their own there. Only that player sees it and holds priority over it; no other player can respond to it or is made to wait on it. See rule 507.

> *Example (non-normative): a deploy-timing spell played in deployment is a real stack item, so Earthbound Replicator can copy it.* <sub>test: 138-spell-copy.test.ts::R286/CT-176: a deploy-timing play names a REAL stack item</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R286, R286 · Replaces: R144 (its half (a) (deployment triggers on one shared stack) was amended by R286); R250 (its §3 deployment half (no priority in deployment) was amended by R286) · Tests: 138-spell-copy.test.ts · Key: effects.priority.deployment</sub>

<a id="r703.8"></a>**703.8.** There is no priority in the haste step. Haste cards are played there as special actions. See rule 504.

> *Example (non-normative): Molten Upheaval played in the haste step makes its Fireball at once; no one has priority and nothing waits on a stack.* <sub>test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.priority.haste-step — in the haste step nobody has priority and a haste card resolves at once with no stack</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.13 · Rulings: R97 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.priority.haste-step</sub>

<a id="r704"></a>
### 704. Resolution and Fizzling

<a id="r704.1"></a>**704.1.** When an effect resolves, its instructions are carried out in the order printed, and a later instruction sees the results of an earlier one. The exception is target legality: it is judged once, as the effect begins to resolve (rule 704.5), so an earlier instruction cannot make a later instruction's target illegal. See rule 704.5.

> *Example (non-normative): Finality ("Negate all other effects. Erase all cards in bins.") erases the cards it has just negated, because they are in bins by its second sentence.* <sub>test: 61-negation.test.ts::Finality erases the very cards it just negated</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: partial, round 3, 1 test run · Rulings: R68 (its Finality ordering note), R324 · Engine: markIllegalTargets · Tests: 61-negation.test.ts · Key: effects.resolution.order</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U14-10, D-U14-13 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r704.1a"></a>**704.1a** Choices an effect makes that are not targets (how to divide damage among a player's units, which card to discard, whether to pay an optional amount inside the effect) are made while it resolves. See rule 702.5.

> *Example (non-normative): Xenopod Progenitor's trigger goes on the stack with no payment asked; its [1] is asked as it resolves.* <sub>test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ Xenopod: the trigger goes on the stack with no payment asked</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1397189214352703590#0 · Rulings: R67 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.resolution.order.choices</sub>

<a id="r704.1b"></a>**704.1b** No priority window opens around a payment or choice made while an effect resolves.

> *Example (non-normative): while Premonition asks its controller which card to cache, the other player has no action; the choice made, Premonition finishes without any pass.* <sub>test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.resolution.order.no-window — the choice Premonition asks while resolving opens no priority window, and the item finishes as soon as it is made</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Rulings: R6 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.resolution.order.no-window</sub>

<a id="r704.2"></a>**704.2.** When a spell resolves it goes to its controller's bin. When a spell unit resolves it enters play as a unit instead. See rule 405.

> *Example (non-normative): a resolved Luminous Arc is in its controller’s bin; a resolved Jelly is in play as a unit.* <sub>test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.resolution.destination — a resolved spell goes to its controller bin, and a resolved spell unit enters play</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.13; Manual p.13 · Rulings: R250 (§4, zones follow control) · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.resolution.destination</sub>

<a id="r704.2a"></a>**704.2a** A card that goes to a bin from the stack is not trashed. See rule 801.

> *Example (non-normative): two Luminous Arcs reach the bin from the stack, one resolved and one fizzled; neither is trashed.* <sub>test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.resolution.destination.not-trashed — a spell that resolves into the bin and one that fizzles into it fire no trashed event</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Rulings: R68 (its removal-and-destination half) · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.resolution.destination.not-trashed</sub>

<a id="r704.2b"></a>**704.2b** A spell token never goes to a bin; it is erased. See rule 304.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.4; Rulebook 2023 p.4 · Rulings: R68 (its removal-and-destination half) · Tests: 61-negation.test.ts · Key: effects.resolution.destination.token</sub>

<a id="r704.2c"></a>**704.2c** A spell that is Unstable, or that carries a Virus applied to it on the stack, is erased instead of going to a bin, whether it resolves, fizzles or is negated. See rule 723.

> *Example (non-normative): a spell played from the bin under Abyssal Evocation is Unstable, so it is erased and not put back in the bin.* <sub>test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::Abyssal Evocation: a bin-played spell is {Unstable}</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): a spell played from the bin under Abyssal Evocation that fizzles is erased too.* <sub>test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.resolution.destination.unstable — a spell played from the bin under Abyssal Evocation that fizzles is erased, not binned</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R79 (its stack-virus half), R96 · Replaces: R68 (its bin destination for a negated card is narrowed by R79: an Unstable one is erased) · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts, 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.resolution.destination.unstable</sub>

<a id="r704.2d"></a>**704.2d** A copy of a spell has no card. When it resolves or leaves the stack, nothing goes to a bin. See rule 710.

> *Example (non-normative): a resolved copy of Suspend bins nothing, and its "Erase me." erases nothing.* <sub>test: 138-spell-copy.test.ts::a resolved copy bins nothing</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R164 · Tests: 138-spell-copy.test.ts · Key: effects.resolution.destination.copy</sub>

<a id="r704.3"></a>**704.3.** A spell unit's spell effect happens first; if it resolves, the unit then enters play. If the spell unit is prevented from resolving (negated, or with its targets made invalid), the unit does not enter play and the card goes to the bin. See rule 303.

> *Example (non-normative): a spell unit played through Hooba-Pon has its spell part happen, then spawns into the formation.* <sub>test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Hooba-Pon spell unit: the spell part happens, then the unit spawns into the formation</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.13 · Designer: RAQ 1461450216874967235#1 · Rulings: R97 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Key: effects.resolution.spell-unit</sub>

<a id="r704.4"></a>**704.4.** A negated effect is removed from the stack at once, when the effect that negates it resolves. It does not resolve.

> *Example (non-normative): one mass negate removes all its victims from the stack together, with no extra priority rounds.* <sub>test: 61-negation.test.ts::R68: a mass negate empties the stack of its victims AT ONCE</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R68 (its removal-and-destination half) · Tests: 61-negation.test.ts · Key: effects.resolution.negation</sub>

<a id="r704.4a"></a>**704.4a** A negated spell, spell unit, unit, ambush or Virus goes to its controller's bin, and a negated Virus cannot be used as a Virus again. A negated spell token is erased. A negated triggered or activated ability just leaves the stack, because it has no card of its own.

> *Example (non-normative): a negated spell token is erased, never binned.* <sub>test: 61-negation.test.ts::R68: a negated spell TOKEN is erased, never binned</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.34; Manual p.34 · Rulings: R68 (its removal-and-destination half), R68 (its removal-and-destination half) · Replaces: R68 (narrowed by R79: a negated card that is Unstable is erased instead of binned) · Tests: 61-negation.test.ts · Key: effects.resolution.negation.destination</sub>

<a id="r704.4b"></a>**704.4b** A negated unit or spell unit never enters play.

> *Example (non-normative): negating a unit on the stack: it never arrives, and its card goes to the bin.* <sub>test: 118-stack-effect.test.ts::R128: negating a unit on the stack</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1461450216874967235#1 · Rulings: R128 · Tests: 118-stack-effect.test.ts, 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Key: effects.resolution.negation.no-arrival</sub>

<a id="r704.5"></a>**704.5.** As an effect begins to resolve, each target it declared is checked again by the rule it was chosen under: its kind, its printed restriction, its region, and being different from the other targets. A target that fails the check is lost, exactly like a target that has left play. See rule 110.

> *Example (non-normative): an Ambush whose ally was stolen in response recalls nothing.* <sub>test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ valid targets: an Ambush whose ally changed sides before it resolves recalls nothing</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1355466429788328066#1; RAQ 1355466429788328066#2 · Rulings: R324, R324, R56 · Replaces: R64 (its statement that a printed restriction is not re-asked at resolution was amended by R324); R256 (its remark that a restriction is never re-asked was amended by R324) · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.resolution.recheck</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U03-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r704.5a"></a>**704.5a** The check is made once, as the effect begins to resolve. An earlier part of the effect cannot make a later part's target illegal in the middle of its resolution. *(Engine differs, see F-U14-9.) (Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Rulings: R324 · Key: effects.resolution.recheck.once</sub>

<a id="r704.5b"></a>**704.5b** A target remains the same object while it stays where it is. A target that changes zone (to a hand, a bin, and so on) is gone, and the effect does not follow it to a new object. A target that stays put is still a legal target even if another effect also targets it. See rule 410.

> *Example (non-normative): Organic Exchange may target two of its controller's own units, and another spell aimed at one of them still resolves.* <sub>test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::Organic Exchange may target two of your own units</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.40 · Designer: RAQ 1454169054402314362#2 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Key: effects.resolution.recheck.same-object</sub>

<a id="r704.5c"></a>**704.5c** Several effects may target the same unit, even if together they would do more than destroying it takes. If an earlier one removes it, the later ones lose that target.

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R144 (its half (b)), R144 (its half (b)) · Key: effects.resolution.recheck.shared-target</sub>

<a id="r704.5d"></a>**704.5d** Changing an effect's targets before it resolves can save it from fizzling. See rule 110.

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1354013430805434389#2 · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts · Key: effects.resolution.recheck.retarget</sub>

<a id="r704.6"></a>**704.6.** An effect fizzles if, as it resolves, it has lost all of its targets. A fizzled effect does nothing, and a fizzled spell goes to the bin. See rule 110.

> *Example (non-normative): Arc Lightning’s only target dies before it resolves; Arc Lightning fizzles, deals no damage and goes to the bin.* <sub>test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.resolution.fizzle — Arc Lightning whose only target died fizzles, does nothing, and goes to the bin</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.43 · Designer: RAQ 1354013430805434389#0 · Rulings: R86 · Tests: 78-round17-core.test.ts, 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.resolution.fizzle</sub>

<a id="r704.6a"></a>**704.6a** When an effect fizzles, none of it happens, including parts of it that had no target.

> *Example (non-normative): a graft composite that loses its only target fizzles whole; its untargeted grafts make no Poison.* <sub>test: 78-round17-core.test.ts::R86: a graft composite that loses its ONLY target fizzles whole</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1354013430805434389#0 · Rulings: R86 · Tests: 78-round17-core.test.ts · Key: effects.resolution.fizzle.whole</sub>

<a id="r704.6b"></a>**704.6b** If an effect has lost some but not all of its targets, it resolves as best it can against those that remain, untargeted parts included.

> *Example (non-normative): an effect with two targets and an untargeted draw loses one target before it resolves; it acts on the remaining target and the draw still happens (illustrative).*

> *Example (non-normative): Tidal Reversion still recalls the other unit when one of its targets is removed.* <sub>test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ target requirements: Tidal Reversion still recalls the other unit when one target is removed</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): a graft composite whose one target survives also carries out its untargeted grafts.* <sub>test: 78-round17-core.test.ts::R86: one surviving target carries the untargeted grafts through</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Twin Flame loses one of its two targets before it resolves; the remaining target still takes its 2 damage.* <sub>test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.resolution.fizzle.partial — Twin Flame with one of two targets gone still damages the other</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): a graft composite with two targeted grafts loses one of the targets; the untargeted grafts still make their Poison tokens.* <sub>test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.resolution.fizzle.partial — a graft composite with two targets losing one still runs its untargeted part</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 3, 3 tests run · Printed: Manual p.43 · Designer: RAQ 1410252965276684418#4; RAQ 1354013430805434389#0 · Rulings: R86 · Tests: 78-round17-core.test.ts, 390-raq-stack.test.ts, 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.resolution.fizzle.partial</sub>

<a id="r704.6c"></a>**704.6c** An effect that needs two of its targets together (a fight or an exchange) does nothing if it loses one of them. It does not fizzle.

> *Example (non-normative): Fight that loses one of its two targets does nothing to the survivor.* <sub>test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ fizzles: Fight that loses one of its two targets does nothing to the survivor</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Organic Exchange that loses one of its two targets exchanges nothing; the survivor stays with its controller.* <sub>test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.resolution.fizzle.pair — Organic Exchange that loses one target exchanges nothing</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.43 · Designer: RAQ 1354013430805434389#1 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts, 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.resolution.fizzle.pair</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U14-2 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r704.6d"></a>**704.6d** An effect that has no targeting part anywhere cannot fizzle. Nor can a part whose target was optional ("up to") and was left empty: declaring no target was a legal choice, and the rest of the effect still happens. See rule 704.6g.

> *Example (non-normative): an item with no targeting part anywhere never fizzles.* <sub>test: 78-round17-core.test.ts::R86: an item that declares NO target anywhere never fizzles</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 2 tests run · Rulings: R86, R86, R86 · Tests: 78-round17-core.test.ts · Key: effects.resolution.fizzle.untargeted</sub>

<a id="r704.6e"></a>**704.6e** An ambush is a targeted effect. If its target is removed, the ambush fizzles and the ambushing unit is put into the bin. See rule 803.

> *Example (non-normative): the ally targeted by Lurking Slimebeast’s ambush dies; the ambush fizzles and Slimebeast goes to the bin.* <sub>test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.resolution.fizzle.ambush — Lurking Slimebeast whose ambush target died fizzles and goes to the bin</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.40; Manual p.40 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.resolution.fizzle.ambush</sub>

<a id="r704.6f"></a>**704.6f** A Virus whose target has become invalid when it resolves is put into the bin, and cannot be used as a Virus again. See rule 723.

> *Example (non-normative): a Virus’s host dies before the Virus resolves; the Virus goes to the bin and is not offered as a Virus from there.* <sub>test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.resolution.fizzle.virus — a virus whose host died before it resolved goes to the bin and is not offered as a virus again</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.34; Manual p.34 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.resolution.fizzle.virus</sub>

<a id="r704.6g"></a>**704.6g** An effect with a required target that never had a legal candidate fizzles, although it declared no target. See rule 704.6d.

> *Example (non-normative): an item whose required target had no legal candidate when it was cast fizzles.* <sub>test: 78-round17-core.test.ts::R86: a required target with no legal candidate at cast still fizzles</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Rulings: R86 · Tests: 78-round17-core.test.ts · Key: effects.resolution.fizzle.never-had-target</sub>

<a id="r704.7"></a>**704.7.** An effect stays on the stack, and still resolves, if its source leaves play. See rule 714.

> *Example (non-normative): an effect stays on the stack when its unit dies, and still resolves.* <sub>test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ dead unit: an effect stays on the stack when its unit dies and still resolves</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1353895783266516992#0 · Rulings: R325 · Replaces: R225 (its first grade (a source that died with its trigger on the stack places nothing) was reversed by R325) · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.resolution.source-gone</sub>

<a id="r704.7a"></a>**704.7a** Where such an effect reads its source (its attributes, power, defense, or the formation it stood in), it uses the source's last-known state: what the source was at the moment it left play. See rule 714.

> *Example (non-normative): Bellowing Boulder dies with its ping on the stack; the ping is still Deadly, from its last state.* <sub>test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ dead unit: Bellowing Boulder dead with its ping on the stack still pings with Deadly, its last state</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1353895783266516992#6 · Rulings: R325 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts, 401-raq-fix-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.resolution.source-gone.last-known</sub>

<a id="r704.7b"></a>**704.7b** An effect that acts on its source itself, or that says "if I am still in formation", does nothing if the source is gone. See rule 714.

> *Example (non-normative): Hooba-Nan gone with its trigger on the stack makes nothing.* <sub>test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ dead unit: Hooba-Nan gone with its trigger on the stack makes nothing</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1353895783266516992#1 · Rulings: R325 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.resolution.source-gone.needs-body</sub>

<a id="r705"></a>
### 705. Activated Abilities

<a id="r705.1"></a>**705.1.** An activated ability is written with a colon (":"). Everything before the colon is the cost of activating the ability; everything after it is the effect the ability has. See rule 109.2.

> *Example (non-normative): Glook's "[once] Discard X cards: Glimpse 1, X times" — discarding X cards is the cost, and glimpsing X times is the effect.* <sub>test: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts::R196 Glook</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.41; Manual p.41; Manual p.41 · Tests: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts · Key: effects.activated.what</sub>

<a id="r705.2"></a>**705.2.** An activated ability may print a timing icon of its own. An ability marked {Battle} can be activated only during battle, and one marked {Deployment} only during deployment. The icon is checked when the ability is activated. See rules 109.2a, 109.2b.

> *Example (non-normative): Grox's ability is marked {Battle}, so it cannot be activated during deployment.* <sub>test: 43-dark-c.test.ts::Grox: R49 — the printed [Battle] marker is enforced at ACTIVATION</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Cadaverous Cultivator's {Battle} ability is refused when activated outside battle, rather than doing nothing when it resolves.* <sub>test: 45-hybrids-ld-b.test.ts::Cadaverous Cultivator: R49 — [Battle] is enforced at ACTIVATION, not at resolution</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R49 (its activation-timing marker), R49 (its activation-timing marker) · Tests: 43-dark-c.test.ts, 45-hybrids-ld-b.test.ts · Key: effects.activated.timing-icon</sub>

<a id="r705.3"></a>**705.3.** To activate an ability, the player takes the steps below, in order. Everything is chosen and paid before the ability is put on the stack, so no player can respond between the payment of its cost and the ability going on the stack. See rules 111.7, 703.

> *Example (non-normative): while the steps are being taken, the opponent has no legal action.* <sub>test: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts::R196 nothing may act INSIDE the cast window</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R57 (targets before fixed costs; costs paid before the stack), R49 (its costs-at-cast rule) · Tests: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts · Key: effects.activated.procedure</sub>

<a id="r705.3a"></a>**705.3a** Step 1: the game checks that the ability can be activated: its timing allows it, any printed condition on it ("Activate this ability only if …") is met, every part of its cost can be paid, and every target it requires has a legal choice. If any check fails, the ability cannot be activated and nothing is paid. See rules 111.6a, 111.7b.

> *Example (non-normative): Instrument of Reassignment costs [x] and "sacrifice another nontoken unit". With only a token beside it, it is not offered and cannot be activated, and the 3 open mana are not spent either.* <sub>test: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts::R196 the COMPOUND half-pay hazard</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Rulings: R77, R77, R77, R77, R196 · Tests: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts, 426-cr-abilities-and-replacement.test.ts · Key: effects.activated.procedure.gates</sub>

<a id="r705.3b"></a>**705.3b** Step 2: if the cost has a variable part (a printed [x], "Discard X cards", "Sacrifice X units"), the player pays it, one at a time, until they stop. The amount paid is X. See rules 111.7, 702.6b.

> *Example (non-normative): Celestial Shifter's "[x]" is paid while activating, so the opponent sees X before deciding whether to respond.* <sub>test: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts::R196 Celestial Shifter</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Rulings: R196, R64 (its cost half) · Tests: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts · Key: effects.activated.procedure.variable-cost</sub>

<a id="r705.3c"></a>**705.3c** Step 3: the player declares the ability's targets. See rule 110.

> *Example (non-normative): Slag Spewer's target is declared before its mod is erased to pay the cost.* <sub>test: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts::R196 Slag Spewer</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R57 (targets before fixed costs), R57 (targets before fixed costs) · Tests: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts · Key: effects.activated.procedure.targets</sub>

<a id="r705.3d"></a>**705.3d** Step 4: the player pays the rest of the cost: its mana, including any tax on activating abilities (rule 111.10f), and any life, debt, sacrifice or other fixed part. See rules 111.7, 111.10f.

> *Example (non-normative): Auric Ascendant's "Recall another ally" is paid before the ability is on the stack, so the opponent already knows which ally left.* <sub>test: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts::the RECALL is a cost, named before the opponent answers</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R64 (its cost half), R57 (targets before fixed costs) · Tests: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts · Key: effects.activated.procedure.fixed-costs</sub>

<a id="r705.3e"></a>**705.3e** Step 5: the ability is put on the stack as an effect, and players receive priority as rule 703 describes. See rule 703.

> *Example (non-normative): Infernal Cultivator's sacrificed units are gone while the ability waits on the stack, so negating it refunds nothing.* <sub>test: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts::R196 Infernal Cultivator</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R57 (targets before fixed costs; costs paid before the stack) · Tests: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts · Key: effects.activated.procedure.stack</sub>

<a id="r705.4"></a>**705.4.** If a part of an ability's cost names something that is not there to pay with (no other ally to recall, no mod to erase), the ability cannot be activated. Nothing is paid, and a [once] on the ability is not used. See rules 111.6, 109.9b.

> *Example (non-normative): Auric Ascendant with no other ally is not offered, so its [one] is not paid and its [once] is kept.* <sub>test: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts::R196 Auric Ascendant with no other ally is NOT OFFERED</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R196, R196 · Tests: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts · Key: effects.activated.cost-cannot-whiff</sub>

<a id="r705.5"></a>**705.5.** An activated ability that a mod gives its host is an ability of the host. The host's controller activates it, and "I" and "me" in it mean the host. See rule 720.

> *Example (non-normative): Living Forge augmented onto another unit lets that unit's controller activate "[three]: create a Robot 2" through the mod.* <sub>test: 27-metal-b.test.ts::Living Forge: donated on a host, the [three] ability activates via the mod</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Aurozoa's "[Augment] Pay 1 life: Recall me" recalls the host when Aurozoa is a mod.* <sub>test: 46-hybrids-ld-c.test.ts::Aurozoa: "[Augment] Pay 1 life: Recall me" — on itself and donated to a host</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R77, R157 (its §6) · Tests: 27-metal-b.test.ts, 46-hybrids-ld-c.test.ts · Key: effects.activated.from-mod</sub>

<a id="r705.6"></a>**705.6.** Some actions are not activated abilities, and rules and effects that apply to activating abilities do not apply to them: applying a mod (an augment or a graft), playing a card as an Ambush, casting a spell token, using a resource, and taking an option a card offers as a spell is played (rule 109.6). See rules 109.6, 701.2, 111.10f.

> *Example (non-normative): during battle Crevice Lurker taxes activated abilities, but applying an augment costs nothing extra.* <sub>test: 16-earth-a.test.ts::Crevice Lurker: R121 — applying an augment during battle is NOT taxed (R37: a mod is not an activation)</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R121 (its activation tax and designer rulings), R121 (its activation tax and designer rulings), R178 (its §3) · Tests: 16-earth-a.test.ts, 151-copy-and-moved-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.activated.not-activations</sub>

<a id="r706"></a>
### 706. Triggered Abilities

<a id="r706.1"></a>**706.1.** A triggered ability is an ability that happens when something else takes place. "When" and "Whenever" mark a triggered ability. A triggered ability can also happen at a stated time, such as "After combat" or "At the end of turn". See rule 109.3.

> *Example (non-normative): Embermaw Fledgling's "after combat" ability creates an X/X unit after combat.* <sub>test: 11-fire-wood.test.ts::Embermaw Fledgling: after combat → X/X, X = attacking units in my formation</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.41; Manual p.41; Manual p.41; Manual p.41 · Tests: 11-fire-wood.test.ts · Key: effects.triggered.what</sub>

<a id="r706.2"></a>**706.2.** A triggered ability triggers at the moment its event happens, and whether it triggers is decided then (rule 109.3a). It is put on the stack afterwards, at one of the times this section gives, and its targets are chosen and its costs paid only as it is put on the stack. See rules 109.3a, 111.8.

> *Example (non-normative): a "whenever I am dealt damage" ability triggers inside the combat damage step, but is put on the stack, and has its target chosen, after the step.* <sub>test: 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts::R261: a combat-damage trigger is announced INSIDE the damage step and pushed to the stack AFTER it</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): the {Alluring} trigger chooses its target as it goes on the stack, and can then be negated.* <sub>test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::R84: the trigger goes on the stack, targets at cast (R67), and can be NEGATED</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R261 (its firing-versus-stacking distinction), R261 (its firing-versus-stacking distinction), R144 (its half (b)) · Tests: 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts, 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Key: effects.triggered.two-moments</sub>

<a id="r706.3"></a>**706.3.** Triggered abilities that have triggered are put on the stack at the times below, depending on when they triggered.

> *Example (non-normative): Eminence of the Barrens damaged by a spell in battle has its trigger on the stack as soon as the spell has resolved, while Lithoghul damaged in combat triggers inside the damage step and is put on the stack only in the after combat step.* <sub>test: 426-cr-abilities-and-replacement.test.ts::cr:effects.triggered.when-stacked — a triggered ability is put on the stack, and when depends on when it triggered: at once outside the damage step, after combat inside it</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Rulings: R250 (its §3 outside the combat damage step) · Tests: 229-cosmic-and-control.test.ts, 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts, 426-cr-abilities-and-replacement.test.ts · Key: effects.triggered.when-stacked</sub>

<a id="r706.3a"></a>**706.3a** During battle, outside the combat damage step: as soon as the action or resolution that made them trigger is complete, on top of anything already on the stack. Players then receive priority and may respond to them. See rule 703.

> *Example (non-normative): Eminence of the Barrens dealt damage by a spell in battle puts its trigger on the stack, and the opponent may respond to it.* <sub>test: 229-cosmic-and-control.test.ts::R250: a trigger fired OUTSIDE the damage step reaches the stack and IS respondable</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R250 (its §3 outside the combat damage step), R250 (its §3 outside the combat damage step), R53 · Tests: 229-cosmic-and-control.test.ts · Key: effects.triggered.when-stacked.battle</sub>

<a id="r706.3b"></a>**706.3b** During the combat damage step: they wait. They are put on the stack in the after combat step, or at a window between damage sub-steps, as rules 608.9b and 608.9c describe. See rules 608.9b, 608.9c.

> *Example (non-normative): a "when I die" ability of a unit killed by combat damage waits with the others and goes on the stack after combat.* <sub>test: 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts::R261: a combat DEATH trigger waits with the rest</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1540678747953569832#2 · Rulings: R300 · Tests: 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts · Key: effects.triggered.when-stacked.combat-damage</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U04-8 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r706.3c"></a>**706.3c** During deployment: on the deployment stack of the player who controls them (rule 703.7). All the abilities that trigger at the same moment are put on that stack before any of them resolves. See rule 703.7.

> *Example (non-normative): three start-of-deployment abilities are all on the stack before the first of them resolves.* <sub>test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::R144(a): every start-of-deployment trigger is on the stack before any of them resolves</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R144 (deployment triggers use the stack), R102 · Replaces: R144 (its single shared deployment stack and its "no priority in deployment" were amended by R286: one stack per player, and that player holds priority over it) · Tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts · Key: effects.triggered.when-stacked.deployment</sub>

<a id="r706.3d"></a>**706.3d** In the end-of-turn step: they resolve as special actions. No player can play cards in response to them (rule 508.1a). See rule 508.1a.

> *Example (non-normative): while an end-of-turn trigger is asking its controller a question, neither player may play a card.* <sub>test: 420-cr-battle-regroup-deploy.test.ts::cr:turn.initiative.end-of-turn.no-responses</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.26; Manual p.26; Manual p.26 · Tests: 420-cr-battle-regroup-deploy.test.ts · Key: effects.triggered.when-stacked.end-of-turn</sub>

<a id="r706.4"></a>**706.4.** An ability that triggers on a card being played, or on something being targeted, is put on the stack above the effect that made it trigger, so it resolves first. It still resolves if that effect is negated afterwards.

> *Example (non-normative): Mycelial Mentor is played while Bloomcaster is in play. Bloomcaster's 1/1 is created before the Mentor arrives, so the Mentor does not see that token being created.* <sub>test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Bloomcaster: its 1/1 resolves before the Mycelial Mentor it was played with arrives</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): a spell unit that is negated after Bloomcaster triggered still leaves Bloomcaster's 1/1 behind.* <sub>test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Bloomcaster: a negated spell unit still leaves the Bloomcaster 1/1 behind</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1353862592661164152#0; RAQ 1353862592661164152#1 · Rulings: R53 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Key: effects.triggered.above-cause</sub>

<a id="r706.5"></a>**706.5.** Triggered abilities that are put on the stack at the same time are put there in the order of rule 703.4: each player orders their own, the initiative player puts all of theirs on first, and the non-initiative player's resolve first. A player may order their own abilities in any way, whatever made each of them trigger. See rule 703.4.

> *Example (non-normative): a player with a "when I die" ability triggered by combat damage and an "after combat" ability orders the two in one choice.* <sub>test: 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts::R261 THE RAQ BATCH</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.43; Manual p.43 · Designer: RAQ 1540678747953569832#0 · Rulings: R2 · Tests: 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts · Key: effects.triggered.order</sub>

<a id="r706.6"></a>**706.6.** A triggered ability triggers once each time its event happens. If one action makes the event happen several times, the ability triggers that many times. See rule 109.3d.

> *Example (non-normative): an enemy spell that targets two allies triggers Earnest Defender twice, and two 1/1s are created.* <sub>test: 136-triggers-and-modes.test.ts::R157 §16: two targeted allies are TWO TRIGGERS on the stack, not one that makes two</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R157 (its §16) · Tests: 136-triggers-and-modes.test.ts · Key: effects.triggered.once-per-event</sub>

<a id="r706.6a"></a>**706.6a** Several cards that enter a hand together in one move are one event. An ability that triggers when a card, or one or more cards, enters a hand triggers once for that move.

> *Example (non-normative): recalling two units out of a bin in one move is one entry into the hand, as a two-card draw is.* <sub>test: 152-hand-entry.test.ts::a multi-card move fires exactly ONE handEntered, like a multi-card draw</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R179, R179 · Tests: 152-hand-entry.test.ts · Key: effects.triggered.once-per-event.one-move</sub>

<a id="r706.6b"></a>**706.6b** Each mod that Reconfigure moves onto a new host is applied to that host separately. An ability that triggers whenever a mod is applied triggers once for each of them. See rule 721.

> *Example (non-normative): Reconfiguring a unit carrying three mods onto Perpetual Construct triggers it three times.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Reconfigure onto Perpetual Construct</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1353856176558706769#0 · Rulings: R332 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.triggered.once-per-event.moved-mods</sub>

<a id="r706.7"></a>**706.7.** A triggered ability triggers only on events in the region its card is in. An event in another region does not trigger it, even when the event involves its controller. See rule 601.

> *Example (non-normative): Refuse Reclaimer does not grow when a unit dies in a region it is not in.* <sub>test: 28-metal-c.test.ts::Refuse Reclaimer: a death in a region it is not in leaves it cold (R12)</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.42; Manual p.21 · Tests: 28-metal-c.test.ts · Key: effects.triggered.region</sub>

<a id="r706.7a"></a>**706.7a** An "after combat" ability triggers only in a region where a battle took place. See rule 609.

> *Example (non-normative): a unit with an "after combat" ability in a region where no battle happened makes nothing.* <sub>test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ after combat: the control, an after-combat unit in ANOTHER region makes nothing</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): a unit with an "after combat" ability that stands in the battle region but in no formation still triggers.* <sub>test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ after combat: an after-combat trigger fires for a unit in the battle region that is not in formation</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: Manual p.43; Manual p.43 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.triggered.region.after-combat</sub>

<a id="r706.8"></a>**706.8.** An ability of a unit that triggers on its own death ("When I die") triggers when the unit dies, although the unit has then left play. The ability is put on the stack in the region where the unit died. See rule 714.

> *Example (non-normative): a "when I die" ability of a unit that died in the battle region offers targets in the battle region, not in its controller's home region.* <sub>test: 62-death-facts.test.ts::R70: a "when I die" trigger resolves in the region the unit DIED in</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R278, R70 · Tests: 62-death-facts.test.ts · Key: effects.triggered.own-death</sub>

<a id="r706.8a"></a>**706.8a** An ability that triggers when its unit despawns ("When I despawn"), including one a mod gives its host, triggers whichever way the unit leaves play: when it dies, when it is recalled, and when it is cached.

> *Example (non-normative): a host carrying Growing Plague that is recalled to its hand triggers Growing Plague's despawn ability.* <sub>test: 141-despawn-mods.test.ts::R167 (i)</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): the same host cached triggers it too.* <sub>test: 141-despawn-mods.test.ts::R167 (ii)</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R167 · Tests: 141-despawn-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.triggered.own-death.despawn</sub>

<a id="r706.8b"></a>**706.8b** Moving a unit and its mods onto another unit (Reconfigure) is not a despawn: the unit does not change zones, so its "When I despawn" abilities do not trigger. See rule 721.

> *Example (non-normative): Bubb wearing Growing Plague is Reconfigured onto a Robot; Growing Plague does not trigger.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Reconfigure vs Despawn</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1353847640214999170#0 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.triggered.own-death.reconfigure</sub>

<a id="r706.8c"></a>**706.8c** Units that die together hear each other. A unit destroyed in the same batch of deaths as other units still triggers on their deaths, and on their cards being trashed, as it would have had it survived. See rule 713.

> *Example (non-normative): Muck Rummager killed by combat damage alongside two allies still draws for its controller trashing those allies.* <sub>test: 258-simultaneous-disposal-listeners.test.ts::R278: Muck Rummager hears an ally trashed in the same combat-damage batch it dies in</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R278, R278 · Tests: 258-simultaneous-disposal-listeners.test.ts · Key: effects.triggered.own-death.same-batch</sub>

<a id="r706.9"></a>**706.9.** An ability that triggers when a spell is played targeting something reads the targets the spell declared as it was played. A target changed onto that thing later does not make the ability trigger, and a target changed away from it later does not undo the trigger. See rule 109.3a.

> *Example (non-normative): a spell played at another unit and then retargeted onto Earthbound Replicator makes no copy.* <sub>test: 151-copy-and-moved-mods.test.ts::R178 Earthbound Replicator: a spell played at something ELSE and retargeted onto me makes NO copy</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): a spell played at Earthbound Replicator and then retargeted away still makes its copy.* <sub>test: 151-copy-and-moved-mods.test.ts::R178 Earthbound Replicator: a spell played AT ME and retargeted away still makes its copy</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1355613076506017894#3 · Rulings: R178 (its §1) · Tests: 151-copy-and-moved-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.triggered.targets-as-played</sub>

<a id="r706.10"></a>**706.10.** An "If you do" clause in a triggered ability is part of that ability, not a separate triggered ability. It resolves as part of the ability, and it is not put on the stack or taxed separately.

> *Example (non-normative): Example (illustrative): Eminence of the Barrens' "you may pay [one]. If you do, I fight another target unit" is one triggered ability.*

> *Example (non-normative): Eminence of the Barrens attacks under an enemy Crevice Lurker and is damaged by a spell. Its controller is asked the Crevice Lurker tax once for the trigger, and the [one] to fight is asked while that same trigger resolves, and is never taxed itself: each trigger costs 2 in all, the tax plus the fight.* <sub>test: 426-cr-abilities-and-replacement.test.ts::cr:effects.triggered.if-you-do — Eminence of the Barrens under an enemy Crevice Lurker is taxed once per trigger, and its pay-to-fight is asked inside that one trigger</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Rulings: R121 (its activation tax and designer rulings), R121 (its activation tax and designer rulings) · Tests: 426-cr-abilities-and-replacement.test.ts · Key: effects.triggered.if-you-do</sub>

<a id="r706.11"></a>**706.11.** {Alluring} and {Resonant} work as triggered abilities of the unit or source that has them. What they do is put on the stack, so it can be responded to and negated, and an effect that taxes triggered abilities applies to it. See rules 802, 111.10f.

> *Example (non-normative): Crevice Lurker taxes the {Alluring} trigger, and declining the tax stops the lure.* <sub>test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ trigger-like attributes: Crevice Lurker taxes the Alluring trigger</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Containment Protocol negates an {Alluring} trigger waiting on the stack.* <sub>test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ trigger-like attributes: Containment Protocol negates a waiting Alluring trigger</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): a {Resonant} source's extra damage waits on the stack after combat as that source's ability, and can be negated.* <sub>test: 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts::R315: the Resonant rider waits on the stack after combat, as its source, and can be negated</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 3 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1366446116274442291#0 · Rulings: R315 (its ruling), R315 (its ruling) · Replaces: R94 (its "OPEN" note that the engine riders the undoubled {Resonant} amount is overtaken by R315 (the rider is damage from the source); not marked in the register (D-U15-7)) · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts, 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts · Key: effects.triggered.attributes</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U15-1, D-U15-7 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r706.12"></a>**706.12.** Some triggered abilities choose a unit without targeting it, such as a Wraith's start-of-deployment ability choosing "an ally". The unit is chosen as the ability is put on the stack. Several such abilities may choose the same unit, even if together they would do more than destroying it takes; if the chosen unit has left play when one resolves, that one fizzles. See rule 704.5c.

> *Example (non-normative): three Wraith abilities all choose one 1/1 ally. The first kills it, and the other two fizzle.* <sub>test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::R144(b): three Wraith triggers may all aim at one 1/1, and the surplus fizzles</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): a Wraith with no other ally is its own only ally. Its ability chooses it without asking, resolves on it (it shrinks to 2/2), and nothing fizzles.* <sub>test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::R144(b): "no ally at all" still does nothing</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 2 tests run · Rulings: R144 (its half (b)), R144 (its half (b)) · Tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts · Key: effects.triggered.chosen-unit</sub>

<a id="r706.12a"></a>**706.12a** Choosing a unit this way is not targeting it. It does not trigger "when I become targeted" abilities, and it cannot be redirected.

> *Example (non-normative): a Wraith ability choosing Mohruung does not give its controller a Crystal.* <sub>test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::R144(b): a subject is not a target</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R144 (its half (b)), R144 (its half (b)) · Tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts · Key: effects.triggered.chosen-unit.not-target</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U15-8 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r707"></a>
### 707. Static Abilities

<a id="r707.1"></a>**707.1.** A static ability states a change that its card continuously makes to the game for as long as the card is in play. See rule 109.4.

> *Example (non-normative): Prickly Protector's "+1/+1 for each other ally" is counted again whenever its stats are read.* <sub>test: 24-wood-b.test.ts::Prickly Protector: +1/+1 per other ally</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.41 · Tests: 24-wood-b.test.ts · Key: effects.static.what</sub>

<a id="r707.2"></a>**707.2.** A static ability does not use the stack. It cannot be responded to or negated, and an effect that changes what abilities cost to activate or trigger does not apply to it.

> *Example (non-normative): Crevice Lurker does not tax Tranquility's "spells cost [one] more"; Tranquility still adds exactly one.* <sub>test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ Crevice Lurker: a static ability is not taxed</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Aetherflux Golem's "I gain +2/+2" never goes on the stack, so Containment Protocol cannot negate it.* <sub>test: 142-static-conformance.test.ts::R168: Aetherflux Golem is a STATIC</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1355103348378042515#3 · Rulings: R168 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts, 142-static-conformance.test.ts · Key: effects.static.no-stack</sub>

<a id="r707.3"></a>**707.3.** Only triggered abilities and activated abilities put anything on the stack. A triggered ability says "When" or "Whenever" or names a time such as "After combat"; {Alluring} and {Resonant} also work as triggered abilities; an activated ability is written with a colon. A sentence that states a standing fact ("I gain +2/+2", "Spells cost [one] more to play during battle") is a static ability, and a sentence that says "instead", "as" or "if" and names no target is a replacement effect. Neither goes on the stack, except that a replacement whose substitute names a target puts that substitute on the stack. See rules 708.1, 109.5a, 706.1, 706.11, 705.1, 708.2a.

> *Example (non-normative): a card whose whole printed text states standing facts has nothing that can reach the stack.* <sub>test: 142-static-conformance.test.ts::a card whose whole printed text is continuous declares NOTHING that reaches the stack</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): a card whose whole printed text is a replacement that names no target has no ability that goes on the stack.* <sub>test: 88-replacement-conformance.test.ts::a card whose whole text is an untargeted replacement declares NO ability at all</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 2 tests run · Printed: Manual p.41; Manual p.41 · Rulings: R104 (its stack rule), R104 (its stack rule), R168, R315 (its ruling), R102 · Tests: 142-static-conformance.test.ts, 88-replacement-conformance.test.ts · Key: effects.static.printed-form</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U15-12 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r707.4"></a>**707.4.** A static ability applies continuously to everything it describes, including units that enter play after it began to apply. When its source leaves play, the change ends. See rule 709.

> *Example (non-normative): a unit that enters play while Transmogrifant is in play has no attributes, and gets them back when Transmogrifant leaves.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Transmogrifant: a unit that enters play under it has no attributes</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1355845893219287132#0; RAQ 1355845893219287132#0 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.static.continuous</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U15-2 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r707.4a"></a>**707.4a** A unit that enters play while a static ability applies to it enters with the change already made. An ability that triggers on the unit entering play sees the unit as changed.

> *Example (non-normative): under Sandstone Defender a 1/1 enters as a 1/3, so Nectar Ridge Oracle ("an ally spawns with greater defense than power") draws.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Nectar Ridge: under Sandstone Defender</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): under Infernal Wispweaver a 0/1 Wisp enters as a 2/2, so Nectar Ridge Oracle does not draw.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Nectar Ridge: under Infernal Wispweaver</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Animated Spark's +X/+0 applies to a unit that spawns mid-battle from the moment it spawns.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Nectar Ridge: Animated Spark statics a unit that spawns mid-battle</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 3 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1355633589890584636#0; RAQ 1355633589890584636#1; RAQ 1355633589890584636#2 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.static.continuous.on-arrival</sub>

<a id="r707.4b"></a>**707.4b** A static ability that changes stats ("I gain +2/+2") puts no counters on the unit. Effects that count, move, double or remove counters do not see the change, and it ends as soon as its source stops applying it.

> *Example (non-normative): Aetherflux Golem's "+2/+2" is a static change in both of its forms, like the other cards that print "I gain ±N/±N".* <sub>test: 142-static-conformance.test.ts::R168: Aetherflux Golem is a STATIC, like the two cards printing its sentence</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R168, R168 · Tests: 142-static-conformance.test.ts · Key: effects.static.continuous.not-counters</sub>

<a id="r707.5"></a>**707.5.** A card's statement that it enters play with counters ("I spawn with two +1/+1 counters") is not a triggered ability. The unit enters play already holding those counters; nothing goes on the stack, and an ability that triggers on the unit entering play sees it with them.

> *Example (non-normative): Aethercap Siphoner (printed 4/4, "I spawn with three -1/-1 counters on me") is seen as a 1/1 by an ability that triggers when it spawns.* <sub>test: 139-spawn-and-play.test.ts::Aethercap Siphoner: a spawn watcher sees the 1/1 the card prints, not the printed 4/4</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): neither Powerforge Synergist's nor Aethercap Siphoner's counters can be responded to.* <sub>test: 139-spawn-and-play.test.ts::Powerforge Synergist / Aethercap Siphoner: "I spawn with N counters" never reaches the stack</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R165, R165 · Tests: 139-spawn-and-play.test.ts · Key: effects.static.spawn-counters</sub>

<a id="r707.5a"></a>**707.5a** Replacement effects that change how many counters are put on a unit apply to those counters. But no player puts them on the unit, so abilities that trigger when a player puts counters on a unit do not trigger.

> *Example (non-normative): under an allied Flux Resonator a Robot 2 enters as a 3/3.* <sub>test: 27-metal-b.test.ts::Flux Resonator: an allied Robot spawns with one more counter (report #88)</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Aethercap Siphoner's own -1/-1 counters do not count as its controller putting counters on an ally.* <sub>test: 139-spawn-and-play.test.ts::Aethercap Siphoner: spawning with counters is not</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R165, R130 (its counter-attribution ruling) · Tests: 27-metal-b.test.ts, 139-spawn-and-play.test.ts · Key: effects.static.spawn-counters.modifiers</sub>

<a id="r707.6"></a>**707.6.** A static ability applies only in the region its source is in. See rule 601.

> *Example (non-normative): Rotspore Herald ("Everything is {deadly}") in its home region does not make a spell resolving in the battle region deadly.* <sub>test: 107-semantics-statics.test.ts::Rotspore Herald: R125 — the scope is the REGION</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.42; Manual p.42 · Rulings: R237, R237 · Tests: 107-semantics-statics.test.ts · Key: effects.static.region</sub>

<a id="r707.7"></a>**707.7.** A static ability applies to everything its text names, with no limit its text does not state. "Everything" means every unit, spell and spell token in its region, on both sides.

> *Example (non-normative): with Rotspore Herald in the region, a spell that deals 1 damage destroys a 7/5.* <sub>test: 107-semantics-statics.test.ts::Rotspore Herald: R125 — a SPELL resolving in the region is deadly</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): a Fireball 1 spell token in Rotspore Herald's region is {Deadly} too.* <sub>test: 107-semantics-statics.test.ts::Rotspore Herald: R125 — a SPELL TOKEN standing in the region is deadly too</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R125, R125, R237 · Tests: 107-semantics-statics.test.ts · Key: effects.static.literal</sub>

<a id="r707.7a"></a>**707.7a** A static ability that names "spells" applies to spell tokens too, because spell tokens are spells. See rule 108.2.

> *Example (non-normative): Emberflame Enlightener ("Your units and spells gain {Powerful}") doubles the damage of its controller's Burst Fireball.* <sub>test: 111-literal-fire.test.ts::Emberflame and Envoy of Lightning ask the SAME question about a spell token</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R157 (its §13), R94 · Tests: 111-literal-fire.test.ts · Key: effects.static.literal.spell-tokens</sub>

<a id="r707.8"></a>**707.8.** A static ability that applies to effects with a number of targets ("spell effects with a single target") counts the targets the effect declared as it was played, including targets that have since become illegal.

> *Example (non-normative): Twin Flame played at two units is not "a single target" for Envoy of Lightning, even after one of them is removed.* <sub>test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::Envoy of Lightning: two DECLARED targets is not</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R94, R94 · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts · Key: effects.static.declared-targets</sub>

<a id="r707.9"></a>**707.9.** A static ability or replacement effect that a mod gives its host works from the host. "I" and "me" mean the host, "you" and "your" mean the host's controller, and it applies in the host's region. See rule 720.

> *Example (non-normative): Transmogrifant as a mod gives "your other units +2/+2" from its host.* <sub>test: 28-metal-c.test.ts::Transmogrifant: the augment-donated static anchors on the host</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Crevice Lurker as a mod taxes abilities in its host's region.* <sub>test: 16-earth-a.test.ts::Crevice Lurker: R121 — donated as an augment, the HOST's region carries the tax</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): a replacement effect on a mod reads from its host.* <sub>test: 87-replacement-layer.test.ts::a donated [Augment] replacement reads from its HOST</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 3 tests run · Rulings: R157 (its §6), R94, R94 · Tests: 28-metal-c.test.ts, 16-earth-a.test.ts, 87-replacement-layer.test.ts · Key: effects.static.from-mod</sub>

<a id="r707.10"></a>**707.10.** A permission a card grants ("You may play one unit with no abilities from your bin each deployment") is a standing fact, not an ability that goes on the stack. Using it cannot be responded to, and an effect that negates activated or triggered abilities cannot stop it. (engine differs, see F-U15-1) *(Engine differs, see F-U15-1.)*

> *Example (non-normative): Example (illustrative): Containment Protocol cannot negate The Bonesculptor's permission, because there is nothing on the stack to negate.*

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Rulings: R165, R168 · Key: effects.static.permission</sub>

<a id="r708"></a>
### 708. Replacement and Prevention Effects

<a id="r708.1"></a>**708.1.** A replacement effect is an ability that changes an event as it happens, written "If … instead". It replaces the event, rather than triggering in response to it. See rule 109.5.

> *Example (non-normative): Flux Resonator ("if one or more counters would be put on a unit by an allied source, put that many counters plus one instead") makes a counter put on an ally one more.* <sub>test: 27-metal-b.test.ts::Flux Resonator: a counter you put on an allied unit becomes one more</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.41; Manual p.41 · Tests: 27-metal-b.test.ts · Key: effects.replacement.what</sub>

<a id="r708.2"></a>**708.2.** A replacement effect does not use the stack. It cannot be responded to, and an effect that negates triggered and activated effects (Containment Protocol) cannot stop it or undo what it did.

> *Example (non-normative): Containment Protocol on the stack cannot negate Nullbringer's life-gain replacement.* <sub>test: 87-replacement-layer.test.ts::Containment Protocol on the stack cannot negate a life-gain replacement</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Conduit of Pain's extra damage never reaches the stack, so nothing can negate it.* <sub>test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::Conduit of Pain: the extra damage never reaches the stack</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: Manual p.41 · Rulings: R104 (its stack rule) · Tests: 87-replacement-layer.test.ts, 12-fire-a.test.ts · Key: effects.replacement.no-stack</sub>

<a id="r708.2a"></a>**708.2a** A replacement effect whose substitute names a target is the one exception (rule 109.5a): the event is replaced at once, and the substitute goes on the stack as a triggered ability. If the substitute later has no legal target or fizzles, the replaced event still does not happen. See rule 109.5a.

> *Example (non-normative): Beyond, Codex Incarnate replaces its controller's rot damage with -1/-1 counters on a target unit; the damage never lands, whatever becomes of the counters.* <sub>test: 43-dark-c.test.ts::Beyond, Codex Incarnate: R102 — the rot replacement asks its controller for a target, and the damage never lands</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R102, R102 · Tests: 43-dark-c.test.ts · Key: effects.replacement.no-stack.targeted</sub>

<a id="r708.3"></a>**708.3.** The event a replacement effect replaces does not happen, and the substitute happens instead. Abilities that trigger on the replaced event do not trigger. When the substitute is still damage (damage dealt "as" rot), the damage was still dealt (rule 112.12). See rule 112.12.

> *Example (non-normative): under Nullbringer a player who would gain life loses that much instead; nothing that triggers on gaining life triggers.* <sub>test: 87-replacement-layer.test.ts::a replaced life gain fires no lifeGained</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): a Robot that Cosmic Conspirator replaces with a Fireball is never created, so nothing that triggers on a unit spawning triggers for it.* <sub>test: 87-replacement-layer.test.ts::a replaced token creation fires no spawned</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): with Blightsea Polyp in play, Zephyrzoa's column still deals combat damage to the opponent, although the opponent gains rot instead of losing life.* <sub>test: 210-zephyrzoa-hears-a-replaced-hit.test.ts::R238: Zephyrzoa fires on a hit that was REPLACED and cost no life</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 3 tests run · Rulings: R104 (its two families and hooks), R238 · Tests: 87-replacement-layer.test.ts, 210-zephyrzoa-hears-a-replaced-hit.test.ts · Key: effects.replacement.substitute</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U12-21 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r708.4"></a>**708.4.** A replacement effect applies to an event only once. What it produces is not replaced again by the same effect, unless a new event occurs. See rules 608.8c, 708.4a.

> *Example (non-normative): 10 {Piercing} combat damage redirected into a 2/4 Oorblak: 4 destroy it, and the other 6 reach the player and are not redirected again.* <sub>test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Oorblak: 10 Piercing combat damage redirected into a 2/4 Oorblak</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): two Nullbringers turn one life gain into one loss, not into a gain again.* <sub>test: 40-light-c.test.ts::Nullbringer: two copies do not stack</sub>
