<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Rulings: R70, R70 · Tests: 62-death-facts.test.ts · Key: effects.last-known.departure-facts.region</sub>

<a id="r720"></a>
### 720. Modifications, General

<a id="r720.1"></a>**720.1.** A modification (mod) changes a card's abilities by combining cards together. A card that can be a mod carries one of two mod symbols: the augment symbol (721) or the graft symbol (722). See rules 721, 722, 305.

> *Example (non-normative): Aetherflux Golem (augment) and Flame Juggle (graft) are offered as mods; The Foretold, with neither symbol, is not.* <sub>test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.mods.what — only a card with the augment or graft symbol is offered as a mod, and applying one changes the host</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.32; Manual p.32 · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.what</sub>

<a id="r720.1a"></a>**720.1a** Virus and Modular are not further kinds of mod. A Virus is a card that can also be applied as an augment during battle (723). Modular lets mods be applied to a card as it is played (724). See rules 723, 724.

> *Example (non-normative): A Virus applied in battle is an ordinary augment action, and attaches as an augment.* <sub>test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.mods.what.virus-modular — a Virus applied in battle is an augment action and attaches as an augment; no virus or modular kind of mod exists</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.34; card: Spellbind · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.what.virus-modular</sub>

<a id="r720.2"></a>**720.2.** Applying a mod is a special action, which a player may perform during the deployment phase. See rule 507.2.

> *Example (non-normative): A graft is offered in deployment and is not offered in the haste step or in battle.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 1:</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.32; Manual p.32 · Designer: RAQ 1357483405276614856#1 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.special-action</sub>

<a id="r720.2a"></a>**720.2a** A timing icon other than Virus does not change when a card can be applied as a mod. A Battle card cannot be applied as a mod during battle, except under a card that lets cards be augmented as if they were Viruses (723.5) or to a Modular card as it is played (724). See rules 207.6, 723.5, 724, 720.2b.

> *Example (non-normative): Burning Vengeance, a Battle card, is not offered as a mod during battle, but it is offered to Spellbind, a Modular card, played in battle.* <sub>test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.mods.special-action.timing-icons — a {Battle} graft card is not offered as a mod in battle, but is on the menu of a Spellbind cast in battle</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Hooba-Lin, a Haste augment card, cannot be applied as a mod in the haste step when no card such as Slurpr allows it.* <sub>test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.mods.special-action.timing-icons — a {Haste} augment card (Hooba-Lin) is neither offered nor accepted as a mod in the haste step without Slurpr</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 2 tests run · Printed: Manual p.32; Manual p.32; card: Rook; card: Spellbind · Rulings: R105 · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.special-action.timing-icons</sub>

<a id="r720.2b"></a>**720.2b** A mod can be applied outside deployment only where a rule or a card says so: a Virus during battle (723.2); a card augmented in battle under a card that lets it be augmented as if it were a Virus, such as Rook (723.5); a mod applied in the haste step under a card that allows it, such as Slurpr (504.8a); and a mod applied to a Modular card as it is played (724). No other card widens the window. See rules 723, 504.8a, 724.

> *Example (non-normative): Without a Slurpr, a mod is refused in the haste step.* <sub>test: 40-light-c.test.ts::without a Slurpr the [Haste] refusal is unchanged</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Rook; card: Slurpr; Manual p.34 · Rulings: R95 (its opt-in permission half) · Tests: 40-light-c.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.special-action.exceptions</sub>

<a id="r720.2c"></a>**720.2c** An effect that lets a player play cards does not let them apply mods. Tides of the Cosmos cannot graft a card or apply a non-Virus augment; it may only put a Virus card onto a unit as a Virus. See rule 701.2c.

> *Example (non-normative): Tides plays a card and is never offered a graft or a plain augment.* <sub>test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Tides 4:</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A Virus card picked by Tides augments a unit as a Virus and never enters play.* <sub>test: 404-raq-fix-tides.test.ts::R337: a Virus card played by Tides as a Virus augments a unit and never enters play</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1396955380000755795#3; RAQ 1357483405276614856#1; RAQ 1537748882501668934#2 · Rulings: R337 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts, 404-raq-fix-tides.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.special-action.tides</sub>

<a id="r720.3"></a>**720.3.** Applying a mod is not playing a card, from whatever zone the mod comes. An ability that triggers when a player plays a unit, a spell or a card does not trigger when a mod is applied. See rules 701.2, 701.2a.

> *Example (non-normative): Stalwart Sentinel counts a spell played from the bin, but not a mod applied from the bin.* <sub>test: 105-semantics-playwatch.test.ts::Stalwart Sentinel: R96/R123</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A Virus applied during battle is not a spell: Origon does not negate it, and its first-spell count is untouched.* <sub>test: 105-semantics-playwatch.test.ts::Origon: a virus applied during battle is not a spell</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1537748882501668934#0 · Rulings: R37 · Tests: 105-semantics-playwatch.test.ts, 119-play-and-token-events.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.not-played</sub>

<a id="r720.4"></a>**720.4.** To apply a mod, a player must meet the mod card's affinity requirement and pay its mana cost, wherever the mod comes from. See rules 105.8, 720.4b.

> *Example (non-normative): An augment from hand needs its affinity and pays its cost.* <sub>test: 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts::RAQ Mods are NOT Played: an augment from hand needs its affinity and pays its cost</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A Virus applied in battle needs its affinity and pays its cost.* <sub>test: 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts::RAQ Mods are NOT Played: a Virus in battle needs its affinity and pays its cost</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: Manual p.32; Manual p.32 · Designer: RAQ 1537748882501668934#1 · Tests: 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.cost</sub>

<a id="r720.4a"></a>**720.4a** A modifier to the cost of playing cards or spells does not change the cost of applying a mod, and a modifier to the cost of activating or triggering abilities does not apply to applying a mod either. See rules 701.2b, 111.10.

> *Example (non-normative): Under Crevice Lurker, applying an augment during battle costs only its own mana.* <sub>test: 16-earth-a.test.ts::Crevice Lurker: R121 — applying an augment during battle is NOT taxed</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 3 tests run · Rulings: R303, R121 (its mod-not-taxed half) · Tests: 16-earth-a.test.ts, 40-light-c.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.cost.not-taxed</sub>

<a id="r720.4b"></a>**720.4b** A mod applied from the cache is priced by the permission that lets it be used. Under a fulfilled prophecy it costs nothing and ignores affinity. Under a glimpse this turn it costs its mana but ignores affinity. See rules 403.3c, 720.5a.

> *Example (non-normative): A live glimpse grafts for the card's mana, ignoring affinity.* <sub>test: 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts::R303: a LIVE glimpse grafts for the card's mana, ignoring affinity</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A fulfilled prophecy grafts for free, affinity and all.* <sub>test: 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts::R303: a FULFILLED prophecy still grafts for free, affinity and all</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A glimpse waives the pips but not the mana: with too little mana the mod is refused.* <sub>test: 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts::R303: the glimpse waives the pips, NOT the mana</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 3 tests run · Rulings: R303, R303, R303 · Tests: 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts, 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.cost.cache</sub>

<a id="r720.5"></a>**720.5.** A mod may be applied from the player's hand or from their bin. See rule 405.8.

> *Example (non-normative): A graft is applied from the bin.* <sub>test: 04-mods.test.ts::grafts can be applied from the bin</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A graft comes from the bin as well as the hand, when its cost and affinity are met.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 3</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: Manual p.32; Manual p.32; Rulebook 2023 p.15 · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#2 · Tests: 04-mods.test.ts, 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.zones</sub>

<a id="r720.5a"></a>**720.5a** A mod may also be applied from the cache, but only while a permission to use that card is live: a fulfilled prophecy, or a glimpse this turn. A cached card with no live permission cannot be applied as a mod. See rules 403.3b, 720.4b.

> *Example (non-normative): An expired glimpse cannot be grafted or augmented.* <sub>test: 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts::R303: an expired glimpse is not a graft, not an augment, not anything</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): An unfulfilled prophecy cannot be grafted.* <sub>test: 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts::R303: an UNFULFILLED prophecy cannot be grafted</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1537748882501668934#4 · Rulings: R303, R303 · Tests: 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts, 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.zones.cache</sub>

<a id="r720.6"></a>**720.6.** A mod becomes part of the card it is applied to, its host. A modified card is treated as a single card with all of the additional text from its mods; the mods are not separate from it. See rule 305.1.

> *Example (non-normative): Aetherflux Golem augmented onto a unit gives that unit +2/+2 and is not a unit of its own.* <sub>test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.mods.one-card — an augment becomes part of its host: the host has its text, and the mod is not a separate unit</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.32; Rulebook 2023 p.15 · Rulings: R244 (its part-of-the-unit half) · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.one-card</sub>

<a id="r720.6a"></a>**720.6a** A mod is controlled by its host's controller. A player who augments a card onto an opponent's unit gives that opponent control of the mod and all of its text. See rule 102.6a.

> *Example (non-normative): Corrupting Blight applied as a Virus to an enemy unit steals that unit for the Virus's new controller's choice of player after combat.* <sub>test: 23-wood-a.test.ts::Corrupting Blight: defects after combat when played normally; steals the host as a Virus</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.34; Manual p.34; Rulebook 2023 p.15 · Rulings: R244 (its trasher half) · Tests: 23-wood-a.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.one-card.control</sub>

<a id="r720.6b"></a>**720.6b** On a mod's text, "you" means the host's controller. See rule 102.6a.

> *Example (non-normative): Oorblak applied as a Virus to an enemy unit redirects the combat damage that would be dealt to that enemy, onto that enemy's own unit.* <sub>test: 17-earth-b.test.ts::Oorblak: as a Virus, "me" is the HOST</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R216, R157 (its §6) · Tests: 17-earth-b.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.one-card.you</sub>

<a id="r720.6c"></a>**720.6c** On a mod's text, "I", "me" and "my" mean the host.

> *Example (non-normative): Life Leech applied as a Virus gives its host, not the Leech, +3/+3 when its controller pays 5 life.* <sub>test: 40-light-c.test.ts::Life Leech: donated as a Virus, "I" is the HOST</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R131 · Tests: 40-light-c.test.ts, 17-earth-b.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.one-card.me</sub>

<a id="r720.6d"></a>**720.6d** On a mod's text, "other" and "another" exclude only that mod itself, not other mods made from copies of the same card.

> *Example (non-normative): A host wearing two Rotbeast augments: each Rotbeast moves the other.* <sub>test: 121-another-identity.test.ts::R131 Rotbeast: a SECOND Rotbeast augment is "another"</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R131 · Tests: 121-another-identity.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.one-card.other</sub>

<a id="r720.6e"></a>**720.6e** When a unit changes controller, its mods change controller with it. See rule 711.

> *Example (non-normative): Download steals a modded unit token, and its augment changes controller with it.* <sub>test: 26-metal-a.test.ts::Download steals a MODDED unit token</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R112, R148 · Tests: 26-metal-a.test.ts, 24-wood-b.test.ts, 04-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.one-card.control-change</sub>

<a id="r720.6f"></a>**720.6f** There is no limit to the number of mods a card can have.

> *Example (non-normative): Six Aetherflux Golems augmented onto one unit give it +12/+12.* <sub>test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.mods.one-card.no-limit — six augments are applied to one unit and every one of them counts</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.32; Manual p.33; Rulebook 2023 p.15 · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.one-card.no-limit</sub>

<a id="r720.7"></a>**720.7.** As long as a card is modded, it has {Unstable}: when it dies or is erased, it and all of its mods are erased. See rules 410.4b, 803.

> *Example (non-normative): A host carrying Ephemeral Skywalker is destroyed; neither card reaches the bin.* <sub>test: 04-mods.test.ts::augments: type-line attribute grant, unstable erasure</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.35; Rulebook 2023 p.15 · Tests: 04-mods.test.ts, 224-mod-trash.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.unstable</sub>

<a id="r720.7a"></a>**720.7a** If a modded card leaves play without dying or being erased, for example when it is returned to a hand, its mods are put into the bin and the card goes on alone. See rules 410.4, 410.4a.

> *Example (non-normative): A nontoken mod on a host that is recalled, cached or killed is binned and trashed exactly once on each route.* <sub>test: 141-despawn-mods.test.ts::R167 (iv): a nontoken mod is binned and trashed exactly once on all three routes</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.35; Manual p.35; Manual p.35 · Tests: 141-despawn-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.unstable.leave-play</sub>

<a id="r720.7b"></a>**720.7b** When a modded unit is cached, its mods do not follow it into the cache; they go to the bin. See rule 403.7.

> *Example (non-normative): Caching a unit sheds its mods to the bin.* <sub>test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::R46: caching a unit sheds its mods to the bin</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R46 · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.unstable.cache</sub>

<a id="r720.7c"></a>**720.7c** A token mod has no card of its own. It never enters a bin: however its host leaves play, the token mod is erased. See rules 410.4c, 407.3a.

> *Example (non-normative): A token mod reaches the erased pile exactly once, and no bin, whether its host is recalled, cached or killed.* <sub>test: 141-despawn-mods.test.ts::R167 (v): a token mod reaches the erased pile exactly once</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R156 (its announce-on-every-route half) · Tests: 141-despawn-mods.test.ts, 129-disposal-tail.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.unstable.token-mod</sub>

<a id="r720.7d"></a>**720.7d** The {Unstable} that a mod gives goes with the mod. A unit stops having {Unstable} for this reason when its last mod leaves it, and a unit a mod is moved onto has it from then on. See rule 720.10.

> *Example (non-normative): Rotbeast moves its host's other augments onto an enemy; the enemy becomes Unstable and the augment's static goes with it.* <sub>test: 151-copy-and-moved-mods.test.ts::R178 Rotbeast: a moved augment takes {Unstable} and its static with it</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R178 (its §4 Unstable half) · Replaces: R178 (§4's claim that every bounded budget rides with the moved mod corrected by R331; the Unstable half stands) · Tests: 151-copy-and-moved-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.unstable.moves</sub>

<a id="r720.7e"></a>**720.7e** A copy of a modded unit (Borrower of Forms) is not itself modded and does not have {Unstable} for that reason. A mod applied to the copy afterwards makes it {Unstable} in the ordinary way. See rule 710.

> *Example (non-normative): A Borrower of Forms that has resolved becomes Unstable when a mod is attached to it.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Borrower of Forms: a mod attached to it after it resolved makes it Unstable</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A Borrower that copied a modded unit dies to the bin.* <sub>test: 403-raq-fix-mods.test.ts::R336: a Borrower that copied a modded unit dies to the bin</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1372468222158180424#3 · Rulings: R336 · Replaces: R118 (ruling 2's 'the copy IS Unstable' half reversed by R336) · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 403-raq-fix-mods.test.ts, 26-metal-a.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.unstable.copy</sub>

<a id="r720.8"></a>**720.8.** When a host is recalled or cached and its nontoken mods are left in a bin, each of those mods is trashed, and the host's controller is the player who trashes it. See rule 405.4.

> *Example (non-normative): A mod left behind by a recall is trashed by the host's controller, not by the mod's owner.* <sub>test: 224-mod-trash.test.ts::R244: a mod trashed on a recall is trashed by the host controller, not by its owner</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A cached host's left-behind mods are attributed the same way.* <sub>test: 224-mod-trash.test.ts::R244: a cached host attributes its left-behind mods the same way a recalled one does</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R244 (its trasher half), R244 (its trasher half) · Replaces: R244 (§1's 'THE DESTINATION DOES NOT MOVE' paragraph (owner's bin) reversed by R250: the mod goes to the controller's bin); R152 (§2 (each mod to its owner's bin; trashed before the sweep) superseded by R244 and R250) · Tests: 224-mod-trash.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.trash</sub>

<a id="r720.8a"></a>**720.8a** A nontoken mod erased together with its {Unstable} host is not trashed. The host's single trash counts for the whole unit. See rule 405.4.

> *Example (non-normative): A Virus on a host that dies is erased with it and is not trashed.* <sub>test: 224-mod-trash.test.ts::R244: a nontoken mod erased with its Unstable host is not trashed at all</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R244 (its erased-with-host half) · Replaces: R152 (§2's trash of a nontoken mod on an {Unstable} host superseded by R244) · Tests: 224-mod-trash.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.trash.erased-with-host</sub>

<a id="r720.9"></a>**720.9.** An effect or a cost can erase a mod off a host that stays in play. The mod card goes to the erased pile of the mod's controller. The host stays in play, and can die if losing the mod leaves it unable to survive. See rules 407.2, 407.2a. *(Engine differs, see F-U17-1.)*

> *Example (non-normative): Return to Nature negates everything on the stack and erases all mods in the region.* <sub>test: 17-earth-b.test.ts::Return to Nature: negates everything on the stack and erases all mods in the region</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A mod on a stolen host, erased off it, is filed on the thief's erased pile, not its owner's.* <sub>test: 246-zones-follow-control.test.ts::R262 §5: the erased pile files a stolen mod under the THIEF</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 3 tests run · Rulings: R219, R208 (its primitive half), R262 · Replaces: R208 (its held behaviour that a mod erased off a living host files nothing reversed by R219) · Tests: 17-earth-b.test.ts, 178-played-item-and-erased-mods.test.ts, 246-zones-follow-control.test.ts, 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.erase-off-host</sub>

<a id="r720.9a"></a>**720.9a** A token mod erased off a host that stays in play is not recorded on the erased pile, because a token is not a card. See rule 720.7c. *(Engine differs, see F-U17-4.)*

> *Example (non-normative): A Wraith token mod erased off a host that stays in play, as the payment of a cost, is not filed on the erased pile.* <sub>test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.mods.erase-off-host.token — a Wraith token mod erased off a living host as a cost (eraseMod) is not filed on the erased pile</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 0 tests run · Rulings: R219 · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.erase-off-host.token</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U07-5 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r720.10"></a>**720.10.** An effect can move a mod from one host to another (Reconfigure, Rotbeast). Moving a mod is not a zone change: the mod never leaves play, and nothing despawns. See rules 410.1b, 721.5.

> *Example (non-normative): Reconfigure moves Bubb and its Growing Plague onto a Robot; Growing Plague's "when I despawn" does not trigger.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Reconfigure vs Despawn</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1353847640214999170#0 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 151-copy-and-moved-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.moving</sub>

<a id="r720.10a"></a>**720.10a** A moved mod is controlled by its new host's controller. See rule 720.6a.

> *Example (non-normative): Rotbeast's augments moved onto an enemy now work for that enemy. (illustrative)*

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R178 (its §4 controller half) · Key: effects.mods.moving.control</sub>

<a id="r720.10b"></a>**720.10b** Moving a mod does not refresh it. A once-per-turn ability on the mod that was already used this turn stays used on the new host. See rule 109.9e.

> *Example (non-normative): A Graxxlid used this turn and moved by Reconfigure cannot be used again this turn.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Reconfigure vs Once per Turn</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): The spent mark is copied to the new host, so nothing is refreshed anywhere.* <sub>test: 403-raq-fix-mods.test.ts::R331: a moved mod carries its spent augment budget</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1353848722974445658#0 · Rulings: R331 · Replaces: R178 (§4's claim that every bounded budget rides with the moved mod entity corrected by R331) · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 403-raq-fix-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.moving.once</sub>

<a id="r720.10c"></a>**720.10c** Moving a mod is not applying it. An ability that triggers when a mod is applied does not trigger when a mod is moved, unless the moving effect says the mods are augmented (721.5a). See rule 721.5a.

> *Example (non-normative): Rotbeast moves its Curio Drifter augment onto an enemy Perpetual Construct, which makes no unit.* <sub>test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.mods.moving.not-applying — Rotbeast moving an augment onto Perpetual Construct fires no mod-applied event and makes no unit</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Rulings: R178 (its §4 no-event half), R332 · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.moving.not-applying</sub>

<a id="r720.11"></a>**720.11.** A mod's effects take their timestamp from when the mod was applied. A mod applied after an effect that removes attributes and abilities on the same layer (Monke) still gives its attribute and ability. See rules 709, 113.2.

> *Example (non-normative): A Virus applied after Monke's effect began still gives its attribute.* <sub>test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ timestamps: a virus applied AFTER Monke still gives its attribute</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1357965714807586897#0 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.timestamps</sub>

<a id="r720.12"></a>**720.12.** An ability that triggers when a mod is applied to its unit triggers once for each mod applied. See rule 721.5a.

> *Example (non-normative): Perpetual Construct makes an X/X for an applied mod, X the mod's cost.* <sub>test: 17-earth-b.test.ts::Perpetual Construct: an applied mod creates an X/X, X = the mod's cost</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Reconfigure moves three mods onto Perpetual Construct: three triggers, a 1/1, a 3/3 and a 4/4.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Reconfigure onto Perpetual Construct</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: card: Perpetual Construct · Designer: RAQ 1353856176558706769#0 · Tests: 17-earth-b.test.ts, 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.mods.applied-triggers</sub>

<a id="r721"></a>
### 721. Augment

<a id="r721.1"></a>**721.1.** Augment is a modification. An augment adds the text that follows its augment symbol to the card it is applied to. See rule 208.

> *Example (non-normative): Aetherflux Golem, a 1/1 whose augment text is "I gain +2/+2", gives its host +2/+2.* <sub>test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.augment.what — an augment adds the text after its augment symbol to the host, not the rest of the card</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.32; Manual p.32; Rulebook 2023 p.15 · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Key: effects.augment.what</sub>

<a id="r721.1a"></a>**721.1a** An augment symbol at the start of a paragraph in the text box gives the host that whole paragraph. See rule 208.2.

> *Example (non-normative): Growing Plague applied as an augment gives its host "When I despawn, each other player draws two cards."* <sub>test: 23-wood-a.test.ts::Growing Plague: draws on spawn; despawn (as augment) makes each other player draw two</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.32; Manual p.32 · Tests: 23-wood-a.test.ts · Key: effects.augment.what.text-box</sub>

<a id="r721.1b"></a>**721.1b** An augment symbol on the type line gives the host the attributes on that type line. It gives no stats. See rule 208.3.

> *Example (non-normative): Bubb ([Augment] {Unaware}) gives its host Unaware, and not its 5/6.* <sub>test: 16-earth-a.test.ts::Bubb: 5/6 Unaware; type-line [Augment] donates Unaware (attrs only, no stats)</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.32; card: Chitin Shredder · Tests: 16-earth-a.test.ts, 04-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.augment.what.type-line</sub>

<a id="r721.1c"></a>**721.1c** On a host, only the augment's own augment text works. The rest of the augment card's text, including body text printed outside the augment paragraph and attributes printed before a text-box augment symbol, does nothing for the host. See rule 208.1.

> *Example (non-normative): Infernal Wispweaver's body text radiates when it is played as a unit, and never from a mod.* <sub>test: 248-augment-box-scope.test.ts::§3 GUARD: a card that prints both halves radiates its body clause from play, never from a mod</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Smouldering Inferno, whose {Piercing} is on its type line before no augment symbol, gives its host only its text-box line.* <sub>test: 04-mods.test.ts::virus augment during battle: on the stack, donated to an enemy, text-only transfer</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R268, R268 · Tests: 248-augment-box-scope.test.ts, 04-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.augment.what.box-only</sub>

<a id="r721.1d"></a>**721.1d** A card that is played normally reads its whole text, its augment text included. See rules 305.4, 109.7.

> *Example (non-normative): A card played normally still reads its own augment paragraph.* <sub>test: 248-augment-box-scope.test.ts::§5 PIN: a card played normally still reads its own [Augment] box</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.43; Manual p.35 · Rulings: R268 · Tests: 248-augment-box-scope.test.ts, 16-earth-a.test.ts · Key: effects.augment.what.played</sub>

<a id="r721.1e"></a>**721.1e** Augment text keeps its kind on the host. A static ability given by an augment ("I gain +2/+2") is a continuous effect on the host for as long as the mod is attached; it is not a triggered ability and does not use the stack. See rule 707.

> *Example (non-normative): Aetherflux Golem's "[Augment] I gain +2/+2" is a static, like the two other cards printing that sentence.* <sub>test: 142-static-conformance.test.ts::R168: Aetherflux Golem is a STATIC</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R168, R168 · Tests: 142-static-conformance.test.ts, 16-earth-a.test.ts · Key: effects.augment.what.kind-kept</sub>

<a id="r721.1f"></a>**721.1f** Augment text that triggers on the host's own departure ("When I despawn") triggers whichever way the host leaves play: when it dies, is recalled or is cached. See rule 410.

> *Example (non-normative): A donated "When I despawn" fires on a recall.* <sub>test: 141-despawn-mods.test.ts::R167 (i): a donated "[Augment] When I despawn" fires on a RECALL</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): It fires on a cache too.* <sub>test: 141-despawn-mods.test.ts::R167 (ii): a donated "[Augment] When I despawn" fires on a CACHE</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R167 · Tests: 141-despawn-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.augment.what.despawn</sub>

<a id="r721.2"></a>**721.2.** A card can be applied as an augment if it prints the augment symbol, in its text box or on its type line, whether or not its augment text does anything. See rule 208.4.

> *Example (non-normative): Chitin Shredder prints the augment symbol only on its type line and has no text box, and it can be applied as an augment.* <sub>test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.augment.which-cards — a card with the augment symbol on its type line and an empty text box (Chitin Shredder) is applied as an augment</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.32 · Rulings: R55 · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Key: effects.augment.which-cards</sub>

<a id="r721.3"></a>**721.3.** To apply an augment, the player takes these steps in order: (1) meets the augment's affinity requirement; (2) pays its mana cost; (3) selects a target to apply it onto; (4) places the augment card beneath the target, with its text box visible beneath the target's. See rules 720.4, 110.10.

> *Example (non-normative): An augment from hand needs its affinity and pays its cost.* <sub>test: 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts::RAQ Mods are NOT Played: an augment from hand needs its affinity and pays its cost</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.32; Manual p.32; Manual p.32; Manual p.32 · Tests: 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts · Key: effects.augment.procedure</sub>

<a id="r721.4"></a>**721.4.** During deployment a player can augment only their own units. An opponent's unit can be augmented only with a Virus during battle (723.2), or under a card that lets cards be augmented as if they were Viruses (723.5). See rules 723.2, 723.5.

> *Example (non-normative): In deployment Curio Drifter can augment your own unit but not an opponent unit; in battle Aetherflux Golem (a Virus) can augment the attacking enemy.* <sub>test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.augment.hosts — in deployment an augment goes only onto your own unit; in battle a Virus may go onto an opposing unit</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.32; Manual p.32; Rulebook 2023 p.15 · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Key: effects.augment.hosts</sub>

<a id="r721.4a"></a>**721.4a** During deployment a player may also augment a spell token they have in play, with any augment, not only a Virus. The token gains only the augment's attributes. See rules 305.6, 507.2b.

> *Example (non-normative): A spell token is offered as an augment host during deployment.* <sub>test: 78-round17-core.test.ts::R89: a spell token is a legal augment host during deployment</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): An augmented token deals {Powerful} damage when cast.* <sub>test: 78-round17-core.test.ts::R89: only ATTRIBUTES transfer</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R89, R89, R89 · Replaces: R79 (its 'not in scope' bullet excluding deployment augmenting of a spell token superseded by R89) · Tests: 78-round17-core.test.ts · Key: effects.augment.hosts.spell-token</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U06-9 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r721.4b"></a>**721.4b** An augment applied to a spell, on the stack (723.4) or as it is played through Modular (724), gives the spell only its type-line attributes. Augment text and static abilities give a spell nothing, but applying such an augment is still legal. See rules 723.4, 724.4.

> *Example (non-normative): A text-only augment on a spell token grants nothing.* <sub>test: 78-round17-core.test.ts::R89: a text-only augment on a token grants nothing, and says so</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): An augment-text mod applied to Spellbind is accepted and does nothing.* <sub>test: 91-modular.test.ts::R105: an [Augment]-TEXT mod is accepted and does nothing</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R79 (its stack-host half), R79 (its stack-host half) · Tests: 78-round17-core.test.ts, 91-modular.test.ts, 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts · Key: effects.augment.hosts.spell</sub>

<a id="r721.5"></a>**721.5.** Reconfigure augments a unit and all of its mods onto another unit. Its first target must have the augment symbol. See rule 720.10.

> *Example (non-normative): Reconfigure moves an augment unit and its mods onto another unit.* <sub>test: 29-hybrids-wm-a.test.ts::Reconfigure: moves target augment unit AND its mods onto another target unit</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Reconfigure; card: Reconfigure · Tests: 29-hybrids-wm-a.test.ts, 151-copy-and-moved-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.augment.reconfigure</sub>

<a id="r721.5a"></a>**721.5a** Each mod Reconfigure moves is applied to the new host. An ability that triggers when a mod is applied to that unit triggers once for each moved mod. See rule 720.12.

> *Example (non-normative): Bubb with two mods reconfigured onto Perpetual Construct makes three tokens, one per mod applied.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Reconfigure onto Perpetual Construct</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1353856176558706769#0 · Rulings: R332 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.augment.reconfigure.each-applied</sub>

<a id="r721.5b"></a>**721.5b** A unit that has become a copy of a card with the augment symbol does not have that symbol, so it cannot be Reconfigure's first target. See rules 208.5, 710.

> *Example (non-normative): A Borrower of Forms that copied an augment unit is not offered as Reconfigure's first target. (illustrative)*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1372468222158180424#6 · Rulings: R336 · Key: effects.augment.reconfigure.copy</sub>

<a id="r721.6"></a>**721.6.** An effect can augment a card onto a unit when it resolves. When the effect augments a token ("Augment a Wraith onto an ally"), the token is created directly as a mod of that unit. See rule 304.

> *Example (non-normative): "Augment a Wraith onto a unit" makes the Wraith token directly as a mod.* <sub>test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::R71: "augment a Wraith onto a unit" makes the same token, directly as a mod</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): An augmented Wraith gives its host its first line: at the start of deployment the host puts a -1/-1 counter on an ally (itself, its only ally), so a 4/4 host becomes 3/3. The test does not exercise the second line.* <sub>test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::R71: an augmented Wraith donates BOTH lines to its host</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 2 tests run · Printed: card: Wraith; card: Blight's End; card: Xzydris · Tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts · Key: effects.augment.by-effect</sub>

<a id="r722"></a>
### 722. Graft

<a id="r722.1"></a>**722.1.** Graft is a modification that combines several effects under a single cause. It is marked by the graft symbol, written [Switch] (unbounded) or [Switch1] (bounded) in the card text this document quotes. See rule 205.4.

> *Example (non-normative): Flame Juggle grafted onto Oracle of the Flame: one sacrifice makes the Oracle Fireball 1 and Flame Juggle three Fireball 1s.* <sub>test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.graft.what — a graft puts a second effect under the host cause: one sacrifice of Oracle of the Flame makes both effects</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.33; Manual p.33; card: Oracle of the Flame · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.what</sub>

<a id="r722.1a"></a>**722.1a** A graft card's ability has a cause, before the graft symbol, and an effect, after it. Oracle of the Flame's cause is "Sacrifice me" and its effect is "Create a Fireball 1". See rule 205.4.

> *Example (non-normative): Activating Oracle of the Flame sacrifices it and creates one Fireball 1.* <sub>test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.graft.what.cause-effect — Oracle of the Flame cause is Sacrifice me and its effect is Create a Fireball 1</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.33; Manual p.33; Rulebook 2023 p.16 · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.what.cause-effect</sub>

<a id="r722.1b"></a>**722.1b** When a card is grafted, only what follows its graft symbol is added to the host. Everything printed before the symbol, its cost and cause included, is ignored. See rule 205.4.

> *Example (non-normative): A grafted Omniwield Evoker adds its counter to the host's trigger and charges nothing of its [three].* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 6</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#5 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.what.after-symbol</sub>

<a id="r722.1c"></a>**722.1c** A graft card still works as written when it is played normally. A spell or spell unit with a graft symbol resolves normally when it is played, and can later be grafted from the bin. See rules 305.5, 305.4.

> *Example (non-normative): A dead Leaping Lillik is a graft from the bin.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 4</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.35 · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#3 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.what.played</sub>

<a id="r722.2"></a>**722.2.** Both cards must have the graft symbol. The host must be a unit in play with a graft cause of its own.

> *Example (non-normative): A graft is refused onto a card without the graft symbol and a cause.* <sub>test: 04-mods.test.ts::grafting requires the graft symbol on both cards and a cause on the host</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Only a unit with a graft cause of its own can be grafted onto.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 2</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: Manual p.33; Rulebook 2023 p.16 · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#1 · Tests: 04-mods.test.ts, 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.requirements</sub>

<a id="r722.3"></a>**722.3.** Applying a graft follows the same cost and timing as an augment: from the hand or the bin, during deployment, paying the card's cost and meeting its affinity. See rules 720.4, 720.5.

> *Example (non-normative): A graft comes from the bin as well as the hand, only when its cost and affinity are met.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 3</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.33; Manual p.33; Manual p.33 · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#2 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.applying</sub>

<a id="r722.3a"></a>**722.3a** A graft is applied only in deployment, never in the haste step or in battle, even when the graft card has Haste. The exceptions are a card that allows mods in the haste step, such as Slurpr (504.8a), and a Modular card, to which a graft card may be applied as the Modular card is played, in battle too (724). See rules 504.8a, 507.2a, 724, 720.2b.

> *Example (non-normative): A graft is never offered in the haste step or in battle, even for a Haste card.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 1:</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Under Slurpr a graft lands during the haste step.* <sub>test: 40-light-c.test.ts::Slurpr: a GRAFT lands during [Haste] too</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 2 tests run · Printed: card: Slurpr; card: Spellbind · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#0; RAQ 1355115946032889914#0 · Rulings: R105 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 40-light-c.test.ts, 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.applying.deployment-only</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U17-12 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r722.3b"></a>**722.3b** A card that lets cards be augmented in battle as if they were Viruses (Rook) does not let a card be grafted in battle. See rule 723.5.

> *Example (non-normative): With Rook in play, Curio Drifter is offered as an augment in battle, but Flame Juggle is not offered as a graft.* <sub>test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.graft.applying.not-by-rook — with Rook in play an augment card is offered in battle but a graft card is not</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: card: Rook · Rulings: R95 (its Rook-grant half) · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.applying.not-by-rook</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U17-5 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r722.3c"></a>**722.3c** Applying a graft targets the host. An ability that triggers when its unit becomes targeted (Mohruung) triggers first, before the graft is attached. See rules 110.10, 110.11.

> *Example (non-normative): Grafting onto Mohruung targets it, so it makes its Crystal.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 5</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#4 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.applying.targets</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U03-13 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r722.3d"></a>**722.3d** A player applying a new graft may insert it at any position below the host's own card, but may not re-order the grafts already applied.

> *Example (non-normative): A new graft slides between two already applied, whose order stays fixed.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 10</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): The insert position decides the order the composite resolves in.* <sub>test: 04-mods.test.ts::graft insert position: below the base, order controls resolution</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: Manual p.33; Manual p.33; Manual p.43 · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#9 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 04-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.applying.position</sub>

<a id="r722.4"></a>**722.4.** Each grafted effect is added to the cause of the host's own card. The host's ability then reads "cause: effect 1 AND effect 2 AND effect 3 …", in the order the grafts sit.

> *Example (non-normative): Accelerated Germination grafted onto Oracle of the Flame reads "Sacrifice me: Create a Fireball 1 AND (once per turn) create two 1/1 units." (illustrative)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.33; Manual p.33; Rulebook 2023 p.16 · Key: effects.graft.composite</sub>

<a id="r722.4a"></a>**722.4a** The host's own graft cause decides when the whole composite triggers or can be activated.

> *Example (non-normative): The host's attack trigger fires the host's effect and every graft under it.* <sub>test: 04-mods.test.ts::graft composition: composite fires as ONE stack item, top-to-bottom</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#6 · Tests: 04-mods.test.ts, 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.composite.top-cause</sub>

<a id="r722.4b"></a>**722.4b** The composite is a single ability. It goes on the stack as one item, resolves all at once, and a single negation stops all of it. See rule 703.

> *Example (non-normative): The host trigger and every graft under it are one stack item, and one negate stops all of it.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 8</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): In battle a single negation kills the whole composite.* <sub>test: 04-mods.test.ts::composite is ONE stack item in battle</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: Manual p.33; Manual p.33; Rulebook 2023 p.16 · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#7 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 04-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.composite.one-ability</sub>

<a id="r722.4c"></a>**722.4c** The composite resolves from top to bottom: the host's own effect first, then each graft in the order it sits. See rule 704.

> *Example (non-normative): Under Mohruung, Overbloom above Spewing Mushroom makes a Poison 8; below it, a Poison 1.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 9</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.33; Manual p.33 · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#8 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.composite.order</sub>

<a id="r722.4d"></a>**722.4d** Every target of the composite is declared when it is put on the stack. A part that requires a target must take one if any is legal, even one of the player's own units. See rules 110, 702.8b.

> *Example (non-normative): With no enemy on the board, the grafted delete must take one of the player's own units.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 Plodding Pebble example</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#15; RAQ 1355115946032889914#15 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.composite.targets</sub>

<a id="r722.4e"></a>**722.4e** A triggered composite with a part that requires a target, when that part has no legal target, is not put on the stack at all. Its untargeted parts do not happen either. See rule 702.8b. *(Engine differs, see F-U14-1.)*

> *Example (non-normative): Megadeath with Resurrect grafted attacks with no cheap unit in the bin: no Poison 5 either.* <sub>test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ target requirements: a graft trigger with a required target and none available makes nothing at all</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1410252965276684418#2 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.composite.no-target</sub>

<a id="r722.4f"></a>**722.4f** A composite fizzles only when it has lost all of its targets, and then none of it happens, its untargeted parts included. While at least one target remains, every part resolves as far as it can. A composite that declared no target anywhere never fizzles. See rule 704.

> *Example (non-normative): A composite that loses its only target fizzles whole: no Poison from the untargeted grafts.* <sub>test: 78-round17-core.test.ts::R86: a graft composite that loses its ONLY target fizzles whole</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): One surviving target carries the untargeted grafts through.* <sub>test: 78-round17-core.test.ts::R86: one surviving target carries the untargeted grafts through</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): An item that declares no target anywhere never fizzles.* <sub>test: 78-round17-core.test.ts::R86: an item that declares NO target anywhere never fizzles</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 3 tests run · Rulings: R86, R86, R86 · Tests: 78-round17-core.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.composite.fizzle</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U17-6 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r722.4g"></a>**722.4g** A graft composite is a triggered or activated ability like any other. A modifier to the cost of activating or triggering abilities (Crevice Lurker) applies to it. See rule 111.10f.

> *Example (non-normative): Crevice Lurker taxes a graft trigger like any other.* <sub>test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ Crevice Lurker: a graft trigger is taxed like any other</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1355103348378042515#1 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.composite.tax</sub>

<a id="r722.5"></a>**722.5.** A graft is either unbounded ([Switch]) or bounded ([Switch1]). An unbounded graft can trigger any number of times; a bounded graft can trigger only once per turn. See rule 109.9.

> *Example (non-normative): Plodding Pebble's bounded graft gives one counter per turn.* <sub>test: 17-earth-b.test.ts::Plodding Pebble: dealt damage → a +1/+1 counter, once per turn ([Switch1])</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.33; Manual p.33; Rulebook 2023 p.16 · Tests: 17-earth-b.test.ts, 04-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.bounded</sub>

<a id="r722.5a"></a>**722.5a** Under an unbounded cause, the composite can fire any number of times, but each bounded graft in it is included only the first time in a turn. See rule 109.9i.

> *Example (non-normative): An unbounded host activated twice carries its bounded graft only the first time.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 12: an unbounded host activated twice</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.33 · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#13 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 04-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.bounded.unbounded-cause</sub>

<a id="r722.5b"></a>**722.5b** Under a bounded cause, the whole composite fires only once per turn, its unbounded grafts included. See rule 109.9h.

> *Example (non-normative): A bounded host triggers once per turn, so an unbounded graft under it happens once.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 12: a bounded host triggers once per turn</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.33 · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#14 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 04-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.bounded.bounded-cause</sub>

<a id="r722.5c"></a>**722.5c** Each grafted card has its own use. Two copies of the same bounded graft on one host each have one use. See rule 109.9k.

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Rulings: R113 · Tests: 94-bounded-uses.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.bounded.per-mod</sub>

<a id="r722.5d"></a>**722.5d** A unit that leaves play and comes back is a new object, so its bounded graft can be used again the same turn. See rule 410.

> *Example (non-normative): A recalled and replayed Engorged Caudex draws from its bounded graft again the same turn.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 calebgannon</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#16 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.bounded.new-object</sub>

<a id="r722.6"></a>**722.6.** A graft printed "{graft} [cost]: effect" adds a cost to the composite. That cost must be paid; it cannot be declined. See rule 111.15.

> *Example (non-normative): A payable [cost] graft must be paid; there is no opting out.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 11: a payable [cost] graft must be paid</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A grafted Immolate's sacrifice is paid at composite cast time, with no decline offered.* <sub>test: 32-cast-costs.test.ts::grafted Immolate: the carrier must pay the cost at composite cast time</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#11 · Rulings: R334 · Replaces: R35 (its grafted riders 'may be declined' and 'an unpayable rider is skipped' reversed by R334) · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 32-cast-costs.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.costs</sub>

<a id="r722.6a"></a>**722.6a** If a grafted cost cannot be paid, the whole composite stays off the stack: the host's own effect and every other graft with it. See rule 111.15.

> *Example (non-normative): An unpayable [cost] graft keeps the host and the other grafts off the stack too.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 11: an unpayable [cost] graft keeps the whole composite off the stack</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): An activated graft cause whose grafted cost cannot be paid is not offered.* <sub>test: 403-raq-fix-mods.test.ts::R334: an activated graft cause whose grafted [cost] cannot be paid is not offered at all</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#10 · Rulings: R334 · Replaces: R110 (narrowed by R334: an unpayable multiplied graft cost withholds the whole composite, not just that graft) · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 403-raq-fix-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.costs.unpayable</sub>

<a id="r722.6b"></a>**722.6b** The cost is paid as the composite goes on the stack. No player can respond to the payment, and units the composite itself would create cannot pay it. See rule 111.

> *Example (non-normative): A "[cost]: effect" graft under Lost Guardian pays its cost twice and resolves twice.* <sub>test: 17-earth-b.test.ts::graft under Lost Guardian pays its cost TWICE and resolves twice</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#12 · Tests: 17-earth-b.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.costs.instant</sub>

<a id="r722.7"></a>**722.7.** Some graft causes trigger several copies of the graft ability as one single trigger: Lost Guardian two, Amphivore and Witness of the Crossing three. The copies are one effect on the stack. See rule 111.14.

> *Example (non-normative): Amphivore's combat damage to an opponent triggers its grafts three times, in one trigger.* <sub>test: 14-water-a.test.ts::Amphivore: combat damage to an opponent triggers grafts thrice (one trigger)</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Lost Guardian's after-combat trigger runs each graft twice as one trigger.* <sub>test: 17-earth-b.test.ts::Lost Guardian: after combat, each attached graft triggers twice as one trigger</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 3 tests run · Printed: card: Lost Guardian; card: Amphivore; card: Witness of the Crossing · Designer: RAQ 1353859961855148103#0 · Tests: 14-water-a.test.ts, 17-earth-b.test.ts, 40-light-c.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.multiplier</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U17-8 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r722.7a"></a>**722.7a** The copies run top to bottom, then top to bottom again, once for each copy. See rule 722.4c.

> *Example (non-normative): Amphivore with Plodding Pebble and Bellowing Boulder goes counter, damage, counter, damage, counter, damage.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Amphivore: a tripled composite runs its grafts top to bottom</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1353859961855148103#1 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.multiplier.order</sub>

<a id="r722.7b"></a>**722.7b** A bounded graft under a multiplier is repeated too. See rule 109.9j.

> *Example (non-normative): Amphivore triples a bounded "Create three" graft into nine Fireballs.* <sub>test: 14-water-a.test.ts::R110: Amphivore triples a BOUNDED [Switch1] graft</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Lost Guardian repeats a bounded graft too.* <sub>test: 17-earth-b.test.ts::R110: Lost Guardian repeats a BOUNDED [Switch1] graft too</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1353859961855148103#2 · Tests: 14-water-a.test.ts, 17-earth-b.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.multiplier.bounded</sub>

<a id="r722.7c"></a>**722.7c** Each copy of a targeted graft chooses its targets separately. See rule 110.

> *Example (non-normative): A targeted graft under Amphivore aims each of its three copies separately.* <sub>test: 14-water-a.test.ts::R110: a TARGETED graft under Amphivore aims each of its three copies separately</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R110 (its copy-targeting half) · Tests: 14-water-a.test.ts, 40-light-c.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.multiplier.targets</sub>

<a id="r722.7d"></a>**722.7d** A cost in a repeated graft is paid once for each copy. If the multiplied cost cannot be paid in full, none of it is paid, and the composite stays off the stack (722.6a). See rules 111.14, 722.6a.

> *Example (non-normative): With one card in hand, a doubled [Discard a card] cannot be paid: nothing is paid and nothing happens.* <sub>test: 17-earth-b.test.ts::R110: all or nothing — one card in hand cannot pay a doubled [Discard a card]</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1353859961855148103#4; RAQ 1353859961855148103#5 · Rulings: R334 · Replaces: R110 (its 'skip only that effect' reading of an unpayable multiplied cost narrowed by R334 to the whole composite) · Tests: 17-earth-b.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.multiplier.costs</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U17-7 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r722.7e"></a>**722.7e** A copy that cannot do part of its effect does the rest. Ralph grafted under a multiplier gives the host away and makes three 1/1s on the first pass only; the later passes cannot give it away, and the rest of the composite still runs every time. See rule 101.

> *Example (non-normative): Amphivore with Ralph grafted: the first pass gives the host away and makes three 1/1s, the later passes give nothing, and the other graft runs three times.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Amphivore with Ralph grafted</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1353859961855148103#3 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.multiplier.as-far-as-possible</sub>

<a id="r722.8"></a>**722.8.** A unit that has become a copy of a grafted unit runs the whole copied composite. More grafts may be added to it, but only below the copied grafts. See rule 710.

> *Example (non-normative): A Borrower that copied a Bellowing Boulder with Flame Juggle grafted runs the whole copied composite.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Borrower of Forms: a Borrower that copied a Bellowing Boulder</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A graft added to that Borrower resolves below the copied grafts.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Borrower of Forms: a graft added to a Borrower</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1372468222158180424#4; RAQ 1372468222158180424#5 · Rulings: R336 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.copies</sub>

<a id="r723"></a>
### 723. Virus

<a id="r723.1"></a>**723.1.** Virus is a timing icon. A Virus card can be applied as an augment from the hand during battle, as well as being played and augmented normally during deployment. See rule 207.5.

> *Example (non-normative): Aetherflux Golem augments the attacker from hand during battle; in deployment it may be played as a unit or augmented.* <sub>test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.virus.what — a Virus is applied as an augment from hand in battle, and in deployment it may be played or augmented normally</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.34; Manual p.34; Rulebook 2023 p.3 · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Key: effects.virus.what</sub>

<a id="r723.1a"></a>**723.1a** A Virus applied in battle is an augment: it gives its host its augment text or its type-line attributes (721.1), and an ability that triggers when a player applies an augment triggers on it. See rule 721.1.

> *Example (non-normative): Morphic Mentor's controller applies an augment in battle and the Mentor gets +2/+2; an enemy's augment does not count.* <sub>test: 17-earth-b.test.ts::Morphic Mentor: your battle augment gives +2/+2 until regroup; an enemy augment does not</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.34; card: Morphic Mentor · Tests: 17-earth-b.test.ts · Key: effects.virus.what.augment</sub>

<a id="r723.1b"></a>**723.1b** Virus changes when a card may be augmented, not what it may be augmented onto. In deployment a Virus is applied like any other augment. See rule 721.4.

> *Example (non-normative): In deployment Aetherflux Golem, a Virus, can augment your own unit but not an opponent unit.* <sub>test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.virus.what.timing-not-host — in deployment a Virus is offered onto your own unit only, like any augment</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.34 · Rulings: R89 · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Key: effects.virus.what.timing-not-host</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U06-7 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r723.2"></a>**723.2.** During a battle, a player who has priority may apply a Virus from their hand onto any unit in the battle's region, their own or an opponent's. See rule 703.

> *Example (non-normative): A player applies Smouldering Inferno from hand to the opponent's attacker; the Virus goes on the stack and the host is modded when it resolves.* <sub>test: 04-mods.test.ts::virus augment during battle: on the stack, donated to an enemy, text-only transfer</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.34; Manual p.34 · Rulings: R79 (its stack-host half) · Tests: 04-mods.test.ts, 370-cached-virus-in-battle.test.ts · Key: effects.virus.battle</sub>

<a id="r723.2a"></a>**723.2a** A Virus may also be applied in battle from the cache, while a permission to use it is live, at the cache's price (720.4b). With no live permission it cannot. See rules 403.3b, 720.4b.

> *Example (non-normative): A glimpsed Virus in the cache goes onto an enemy unit in battle, ignoring affinity.* <sub>test: 370-cached-virus-in-battle.test.ts::R311: a glimpsed Virus in the cache goes onto an ENEMY unit in battle</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A Virus whose prophecy is fulfilled is applied in battle for free.* <sub>test: 370-cached-virus-in-battle.test.ts::R311: a Virus whose prophecy is fulfilled augments in battle for FREE</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): An expired glimpse is nothing in battle.* <sub>test: 370-cached-virus-in-battle.test.ts::R311: an EXPIRED glimpse is still nothing in battle</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 3 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1537748882501668934#3 · Rulings: R311 · Replaces: R95 (its sentence that the base battle-augment rule refuses the cache corrected by R311) · Tests: 370-cached-virus-in-battle.test.ts, 369-cache-is-the-hand.test.ts · Key: effects.virus.battle.cache</sub>

<a id="r723.2b"></a>**723.2b** A Virus in a bin cannot be applied during battle by its Virus ability. From the bin it can be applied as an ordinary mod during deployment, and outside deployment only where another card opens a window: augmenting in battle under a card such as Rook (723.5), applying to a Modular card as it is played (724), or applying in the haste step under a card such as Slurpr (504.8a). See rules 405.8a, 723.5, 724, 504.8a, 720.2b.

> *Example (non-normative): Bumblecrab, a Virus, is offered from the hand in battle but not from the bin; in deployment it is offered from the bin.* <sub>test: 418-cr-zones.test.ts::cr:zones.bin.mods-from-bin.virus — a Virus card in the bin is offered as an augment in deployment, never in battle</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): With a Rook in the battle's region, a card is augmented out of the bin during battle.* <sub>test: 29-hybrids-wm-a.test.ts::Rook: augmenting from the BIN during battle takes the card out of the BIN, not the hand</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 3, 2 tests run · Printed: Manual p.34; Manual p.34; card: Rook; card: Spellbind; card: Slurpr · Tests: 418-cr-zones.test.ts, 29-hybrids-wm-a.test.ts, 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Key: effects.virus.battle.not-bin</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U17-14 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r723.2c"></a>**723.2c** A Virus applied to an opponent's unit is controlled by that opponent, with its ability (720.6a). A Virus whose text works against its host's controller therefore works against the opponent. See rule 720.6a.

> *Example (non-normative): Smouldering Inferno augmented onto an opposing unit forces it to sacrifice itself after combat.* <sub>test: 04-mods.test.ts::virus augment during battle: on the stack, donated to an enemy, text-only transfer</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.34; Manual p.34; Manual p.34 · Tests: 04-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.virus.battle.control</sub>

<a id="r723.3"></a>**723.3.** Applying a Virus in battle uses the stack. The Virus goes on the stack as an effect that targets its host, and it can be responded to, redirected and negated. See rules 110.10a, 703.

> *Example (non-normative): A Virus being applied to Graxxlid is an effect targeting Graxxlid, which Graxxlid can negate.* <sub>test: 16-earth-a.test.ts::Graxxlid: a Virus being applied to me IS an effect targeting me</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.34; Manual p.34 · Rulings: R88 · Tests: 16-earth-a.test.ts, 23-wood-a.test.ts, 04-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.virus.stack</sub>

<a id="r723.3a"></a>**723.3a** A Virus that is negated, or whose target has become invalid, is put into the bin and cannot be used as a Virus again. See rules 704.4a, 704.6f.

> *Example (non-normative): A Virus whose host leaves the stack first fizzles to the bin.* <sub>test: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts::R79: a virus whose host leaves the stack first fizzles to the bin</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Negating the Virus itself bins it.* <sub>test: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts::R79: negating the CARRIER erases it too; negating the VIRUS ITSELF bins it</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: Manual p.34; Manual p.34 · Tests: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts, 04-mods.test.ts · Key: effects.virus.stack.negated</sub>

<a id="r723.3b"></a>**723.3b** A Virus being applied is not a spell. An effect that negates spells, or counts the spells played, does not see it. See rule 700.1b.

> *Example (non-normative): A spell-only negation cannot reach a Virus, and a negated Virus does not mod.* <sub>test: 04-mods.test.ts::a virus is not a "spell effect" (negation scoping); a negated virus does not mod</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Origon does not negate a Virus applied in battle, and its first-spell count is untouched.* <sub>test: 105-semantics-playwatch.test.ts::Origon: a virus applied during battle is not a spell</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1537748882501668934#0 · Rulings: R37 · Tests: 04-mods.test.ts, 105-semantics-playwatch.test.ts · Key: effects.virus.stack.not-a-spell</sub>

<a id="r723.4"></a>**723.4.** During battle a Virus may be augmented onto a spell on the stack, the player's own or an opponent's. The spell gains only the Virus's attributes (721.4b). See rule 721.4b.

> *Example (non-normative): Chitin Shredder on Arc Lightning doubles its damage.* <sub>test: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts::R79: the powerful guy on a giant fireball</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A Virus can go onto an enemy spell.* <sub>test: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts::R79: you can hit an ENEMY spell</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R79 (its stack-host half), R79 (its stack-host half) · Tests: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts · Key: effects.virus.spell-host</sub>

<a id="r723.4a"></a>**723.4a** Spells, spell units and spell tokens on the stack are legal hosts for a Virus. See rule 723.4e.

> *Example (non-normative): A spell token on the stack is a legal host.* <sub>test: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts::R79: a spell TOKEN is a legal host too</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 2 tests run · Rulings: R79 (its stack-host half) · Tests: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts · Key: effects.virus.spell-host.which</sub>

<a id="r723.4b"></a>**723.4b** A spell carrying a Virus is modded, so it is {Unstable}: the spell and the Virus are erased instead of going to a bin, whether the spell resolves, fizzles or is negated. See rule 704.2c.

> *Example (non-normative): A spell that carried a Virus is erased, never binned.* <sub>test: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts::R79 ⚠: a spell that carried a virus is Unstable</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Negating the carrier erases it too.* <sub>test: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts::R79: negating the CARRIER erases it too</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: Manual p.35 · Rulings: R79 (its stack-host half) · Tests: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts, 91-modular.test.ts · Key: effects.virus.spell-host.erased</sub>

<a id="r723.4c"></a>**723.4c** A spell unit carrying a Virus is not erased when it resolves. It enters play with the Virus attached as an augment, and so has {Unstable}. See rule 303.

> *Example (non-normative): A spell unit carries its Virus into play as an augment mod.* <sub>test: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts::R79: a spell UNIT carries its virus into play as an augment mod</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R79 (its stack-host half), R79 (its stack-host half) · Tests: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts · Key: effects.virus.spell-host.spell-unit</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U17-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r723.4d"></a>**723.4d** A spell that has begun to resolve cannot have a Virus applied to it. See rule 703.6.

> *Example (non-normative): A resolving item cannot be responded to, negated or targeted.* <sub>test: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts::R78: a resolving item cannot be responded to, negated or targeted</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R79 (its stack-host half) · Tests: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts · Key: effects.virus.spell-host.resolving</sub>

<a id="r723.4e"></a>**723.4e** Triggered and activated abilities, Viruses, units being cast and Ambushes on the stack are not legal hosts for a Virus. See rule 723.4a.

> *Example (non-normative): A triggered ability on the stack is not offered as a Virus host, and is refused if asked for anyway.* <sub>test: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts::R79: only SPELLS are legal hosts</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U17-2 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r723.5"></a>**723.5.** A card can let other cards be augmented during battle as if they were Viruses. Rook: "You may augment cards from hand and bin during battle as if they were [Virus]." See rule 720.2b.

> *Example (non-normative): A non-Virus augment from hand during battle is refused without Rook and legal with it.* <sub>test: 29-hybrids-wm-a.test.ts::Rook: a NON-virus augment from HAND during battle</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Rook's bin augment takes the card out of the bin.* <sub>test: 29-hybrids-wm-a.test.ts::Rook: augmenting from the BIN during battle takes the card out of the BIN, not the hand</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: card: Rook · Tests: 29-hybrids-wm-a.test.ts · Key: effects.virus.permission</sub>

<a id="r723.5a"></a>**723.5a** Such a card gives the augmented card the Virus ability itself, so the augment may go onto an opponent's unit or onto a spell on the stack. See rule 723.4.

> *Example (non-normative): A Rook-enabled augment lands on an enemy unit during battle.* <sub>test: 136-triggers-and-modes.test.ts::R157 §26: a Rook-enabled augment lands on an ENEMY unit during battle</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A Rook-enabled augment reaches a spell on the stack.* <sub>test: 136-triggers-and-modes.test.ts::R157 §26: a Rook-enabled augment reaches a SPELL ON THE STACK</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R157 (its §26), R161 · Replaces: R95 (its OPEN question 2 default (Rook grants only the timing permission) reversed by R157 §26) · Tests: 136-triggers-and-modes.test.ts · Key: effects.virus.permission.confers</sub>

<a id="r723.5b"></a>**723.5b** Such a card reaches only the zones it names. Rook names the hand and the bin, so a non-Virus card in the cache cannot be augmented in battle through Rook. See rule 723.2a.

> *Example (non-normative): Rook prints "hand and bin", so the cache stays shut.* <sub>test: 29-hybrids-wm-a.test.ts::Rook: it prints "hand and bin", so the CACHE stays shut</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Rook · Rulings: R311 · Tests: 29-hybrids-wm-a.test.ts · Key: effects.virus.permission.zones</sub>

<a id="r723.5c"></a>**723.5c** Such a permission belongs to the controller of the card that grants it (the host's controller, when it is a mod), and works only in that card's region. See rule 720.6b.

> *Example (non-normative): Rook's permission is region-scoped and does not reach the opponent.* <sub>test: 29-hybrids-wm-a.test.ts::Rook: the permission is REGION-scoped, and does not reach the opponent</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Rook worn as an augment gives the permission to the host's controller.* <sub>test: 29-hybrids-wm-a.test.ts::Rook: the [Augment] half works, and the permission belongs to the HOST</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R95 (its Rook-grant half), R95 (its Rook-grant half) · Tests: 29-hybrids-wm-a.test.ts, 136-triggers-and-modes.test.ts · Key: effects.virus.permission.region</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U17-10 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r724"></a>
### 724. Modular

<a id="r724.1"></a>**724.1.** Modular is an attribute. A player may apply mods from their hand and/or bin to a Modular card as it is played, paying their costs. See rule 802.26.

> *Example (non-normative): Spellbind's mods are applied at cast time, paid for, and ride on the stack item.* <sub>test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::{Modular}: mods are applied at cast time, paid for, and ride on the stack item</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Spellbind · Tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts, 91-modular.test.ts · Key: effects.modular.what</sub>

<a id="r724.1a"></a>**724.1a** Spellbind is the only card that prints Modular.

> *Example (non-normative): Spellbind is the only card in the pool that prints Modular.* <sub>test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.modular.what.pool — Spellbind is the only card in the pool with Modular</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: card: Spellbind · Rulings: R105 · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Key: effects.modular.what.pool</sub>

<a id="r724.2"></a>**724.2.** Any card in the player's hand or bin whose cost they can pay may be applied to a Modular card: a graft, an augment, a Virus, or a card that can do nothing on a spell.

> *Example (non-normative): The Modular menu offers every card the player can pay for.* <sub>test: 91-modular.test.ts::R105: the {Modular} menu offers every card you can pay for</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A card in the bin is offered beside the hand; an unaffordable one is not.* <sub>test: 91-modular.test.ts::R105: a card in the BIN is offered beside the hand, and an unaffordable one is not</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R105, R105 · Tests: 91-modular.test.ts · Key: effects.modular.any-card</sub>

<a id="r724.2a"></a>**724.2a** A mod that does nothing on a spell is still a legal choice, and its cost is still paid. See rule 721.4b.

> *Example (non-normative): Sparkwraith's augment text applied to Spellbind is accepted and does nothing.* <sub>test: 91-modular.test.ts::R105: an [Augment]-TEXT mod is accepted and does nothing</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R105 · Tests: 91-modular.test.ts · Key: effects.modular.any-card.no-op</sub>

<a id="r724.2b"></a>**724.2b** Each mod's cost is paid as it is applied, while the Modular card is cast. Applying it is not playing it. See rule 720.3.

> *Example (non-normative): The mod is charged at cast, and applying it is not playing it.* <sub>test: 91-modular.test.ts::R105: "you still pay their costs"</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Spellbind · Tests: 91-modular.test.ts · Key: effects.modular.any-card.cost</sub>

<a id="r724.3"></a>**724.3.** The mods are chosen and paid for while the Modular card is being cast, before it reaches the stack, and they go on the stack with it. The caster may apply none. See rule 702.3b.

> *Example (non-normative): The caster may decline, and a non-Modular spell is never asked.* <sub>test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::{Modular}: the caster may decline, and a non-modular spell is never asked</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Spellbind · Rulings: R105 · Tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts · Key: effects.modular.when</sub>

<a id="r724.4"></a>**724.4.** A graft applied to a Modular spell adds its effect to the spell's ability as an extra part. See rule 722.4.

> *Example (non-normative): A graft mod contributes its effect as an extra part.* <sub>test: 91-modular.test.ts::R105: a GRAFT mod still contributes its [Switch] effect as an extra part</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A graft card in the bin is played again through Spellbind, happens, and is erased.* <sub>test: 91-modular.test.ts::R105: the flashback line</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R105 · Tests: 91-modular.test.ts · Key: effects.modular.effects</sub>
