<a id="r724.4a"></a>**724.4a** A type-line augment applied to a Modular spell gives its attributes to the spell's effect. See rule 721.4b.

> *Example (non-normative): {Powerful} turns a Spellbind-carried Twin Flame from 2 damage into 4.* <sub>test: 91-modular.test.ts::R105: a type-line [Augment] mod really donates</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R105 · Tests: 91-modular.test.ts · Key: effects.modular.effects.attributes</sub>

<a id="r724.4b"></a>**724.4b** Augment text and static abilities applied to a Modular spell do nothing, because a spell has no body for them to work on. See rule 721.4b.

> *Example (non-normative): Sparkwraith on Spellbind: a spell played while it rides the stack puts no counter anywhere.* <sub>test: 91-modular.test.ts::R105: an [Augment]-TEXT mod is accepted and does nothing</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R105, R105 · Tests: 91-modular.test.ts · Key: effects.modular.effects.text</sub>

<a id="r724.4c"></a>**724.4c** A grafted cost on a Modular spell's graft part must be paid if it can be. If it cannot, only that part is skipped, and the spell still resolves. See rule 722.6.

> *Example (non-normative): Spellbind carrying a grafted Immolate with no unit to sacrifice: the Immolate part is skipped and Spellbind still gives its rot. (illustrative)*

> *Example (non-normative): Spellbind carrying a grafted Immolate, with a unit to sacrifice: the cost is paid, the unit is sacrificed and a card is drawn. Declining is not offered.* <sub>test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.modular.effects.graft-cost — Spellbind carrying a grafted Immolate with a unit to sacrifice offers no decline, sacrifices the unit and draws</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Rulings: R334 · Replaces: R35 (its declinable and skippable grafted riders reversed by R334, except this Modular per-part skip) · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Key: effects.modular.effects.graft-cost</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U04-12 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r724.5"></a>**724.5.** A Modular card with any mod applied is modded, so it has {Unstable}: it and all of its mods are erased instead of going to a bin, whether it resolves, fizzles or is negated. See rules 720.7, 723.4b.

> *Example (non-normative): A graft card replayed from the bin by Spellbind is erased, so it cannot be used that way twice.* <sub>test: 91-modular.test.ts::R105: the flashback line</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A negated modded Spellbind is erased too.* <sub>test: 91-modular.test.ts::R105: a NEGATED modded Spellbind is erased too</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A mod applied through Modular and a Virus applied on the stack end the same way.* <sub>test: 91-modular.test.ts::R105 = R79</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 3 tests run · Printed: Manual p.35 · Rulings: R105 · Tests: 91-modular.test.ts, 43-dark-c.test.ts · Key: effects.modular.unstable</sub>

<a id="r724.5a"></a>**724.5a** A Modular card with no mod applied does not have {Unstable}, and goes to the bin like any other spell.

> *Example (non-normative): An unmodded Modular spell is binned like any other spell.* <sub>test: 91-modular.test.ts::R105: an UNMODDED {Modular} spell is not Unstable</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R105 · Tests: 91-modular.test.ts · Key: effects.modular.unstable.unmodded</sub>

## 8. Keywords

<a id="r800"></a>
### 800. General

*No rules drafted yet.*

<a id="r801"></a>
### 801. Keyword Actions

<a id="r801.1"></a>**801.1.** Card text uses some verbs with a fixed game meaning: these are keyword actions, defined in this section. Where a card prints reminder text for a keyword action, the printed reminder states its meaning, and it wins over any paraphrase of it. See rules 802, 803.

> *Example (non-normative): Premonition prints the reminder for glimpse, so the glimpse reminder a player is shown is that printed sentence, and our longer paraphrase is kept only as the rule behind it.* <sub>test: 429-cr-keyword-actions.test.ts::cr:keywords.actions.general — where a card prints the reminder for a keyword action, the reminder a player is shown is that printed sentence and not our paraphrase</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Rulings: R206 (its rule 1: printed text wins), R206 (its rule 1: printed text wins) · Tests: 429-cr-keyword-actions.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.general</sub>

<a id="r801.2"></a>**801.2.** A card is trashed when it enters a bin from any zone except the stack. See rule 405.4.

> *Example (non-normative): A card discarded from a hand enters a bin from the hand, so it is trashed.* <sub>test: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::R40: discarding from hand trashes, by the owner of the bin it enters</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A card that leaves a cache for a bin is trashed.* <sub>test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::R41: a card leaving the cache for a BIN is trashed (R40 classifies it automatically)</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R306, R40 (its bin-entry definition, for cards) · Replaces: R40 (its 2026-08-21 token amendment reversed by R306); R133 (its tokens-are-trashed half withdrawn by R306) · Tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts, 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.trash</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U18-2 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r801.2a"></a>**801.2a** Discarding a card, sacrificing it, milling it and a card dying into a bin are all ways of trashing it. See rules 801.3, 801.4, 801.5.

> *Example (non-normative): Milling a card from the deck trashes it, one trash per card.* <sub>test: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::R40: milling from the deck trashes one event per card</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A unit card that is sacrificed, or that dies, enters a bin from play and is trashed.* <sub>test: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::R40: sacrificing and dying both trash — the card enters a bin from PLAY</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R40 (its bin-entry definition, for cards) · Tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.trash.ways</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U18-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r801.2b"></a>**801.2b** A card that goes to a bin from the stack is not trashed, whether it resolved, was negated or failed to resolve. A card played for free during another effect's resolution and then put into the bin counts as coming from the stack. See rules 405.4a, 704.2a.

> *Example (non-normative): A spell going to the bin after it resolves is not trashed.* <sub>test: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::R40: a spell going to the bin after RESOLVING is not trashed (it comes from the stack)</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A negated spell going to the bin is not trashed.* <sub>test: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::R40: a NEGATED spell is not trashed either</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A spell Tides of the Cosmos plays for free off the deck goes to the bin afterwards and is not trashed.* <sub>test: 15-water-b.test.ts::R146: Tides plays an ORDINARY spell for free → the bin, and it is NOT a trash</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 3 tests run · Rulings: R40 (its bin-entry definition, for cards), R40 (its bin-entry definition, for cards), R146 · Tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts, 15-water-b.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.trash.not-from-stack</sub>

<a id="r801.2c"></a>**801.2c** Erasing a card is not trashing it: an erased card never enters a bin. See rules 407.1c, 801.6.

> *Example (non-normative): Banishment erases a unit: no death and no trash happen.* <sub>test: 145-erase-routes.test.ts::R172 (vii): Banishment still fires no 'died' and no 'trashed'</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R40 (its bin-entry definition, for cards) · Tests: 145-erase-routes.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.trash.not-erase</sub>

<a id="r801.2d"></a>**801.2d** A token is never trashed, because only a card can be trashed. A unit token that dies still enters the bin and still dies, but its trip through the bin is not a trash: no "when I am trashed" ability triggers for it, its own included. See rules 108.2e, 304.10a.

> *Example (non-normative): A token unit dying in battle does not raise the count of cards trashed in that battle.* <sub>test: 338-tokens-are-not-trashed.test.ts::R306: a token unit dying in battle does not bump the trashed ledger that Dropslime reads</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A token copy of Dropslime that dies does not trigger its own "When I am trashed".* <sub>test: 338-tokens-are-not-trashed.test.ts::R306: a token copy of an own-trash card does not fire its own when-I-am-trashed</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R306, R306, R306, R306 · Replaces: R40 (its 2026-08-21 amendment (tokens can be trashed) reversed by R306); R133 (its second half (tokens are trashed) withdrawn by R306); R137 (its token-symmetry argument amended by R306) · Tests: 338-tokens-are-not-trashed.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.trash.tokens</sub>

<a id="r801.2e"></a>**801.2e** The player whose bin the card enters is the player who trashes it. A unit that dies goes to its controller's bin, so its controller trashes it; when an effect sends the card to another player's bin, that player trashes it. See rules 405.3, 711.

> *Example (non-normative): A stolen unit that dies goes to the bin of the player who controls it, and that player trashes it.* <sub>test: 229-cosmic-and-control.test.ts::R250: a stolen unit that dies is trashed by its CONTROLLER, into the controller bin</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Pull Under deletes an enemy unit and puts it into the caster's bin: the caster trashes it, once.* <sub>test: 15-water-b.test.ts::Pull Under: an ENEMY unmodded victim is trashed by the CASTER, exactly once (R40, binTo)</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R40 (its trasher sentence, for a card that is not a mod), R250 (its §4, zones follow control), R250 (its §4, zones follow control) · Replaces: R244 (its §1 destination paragraph (a card goes to its owner's bin) reversed by R250) · Tests: 229-cosmic-and-control.test.ts, 15-water-b.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.trash.trasher</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U18-11 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r801.2f"></a>**801.2f** When a modded unit is recalled or cached, each nontoken mod it carried is left behind in a bin and is trashed there. The host's controller trashes it, not the mod's owner. See rules 410.4, 403.7.

> *Example (non-normative): A mod left in the bin when its host is recalled is trashed by the host's controller.* <sub>test: 224-mod-trash.test.ts::R244: a mod trashed on a recall is trashed by the host controller, not by its owner</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Caching the host attributes the left-behind mods the same way.* <sub>test: 224-mod-trash.test.ts::R244: a cached host attributes its left-behind mods the same way a recalled one does</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R244 (its attribution and mod-erase halves), R244 (its attribution and mod-erase halves), R244 (its attribution and mod-erase halves) · Replaces: R137 (its section 'The mods ride with it' reversed by R244) · Tests: 224-mod-trash.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.trash.mods-left-behind</sub>

<a id="r801.2g"></a>**801.2g** A nontoken mod that is erased together with its {Unstable} host is not trashed. The host's departure is the whole unit's; the mod has no trash of its own. See rules 405.4, 720.

> *Example (non-normative): A nontoken mod on an {Unstable} host that dies is erased with it and fires no trash ability.* <sub>test: 224-mod-trash.test.ts::R244: a nontoken mod erased with its Unstable host is not trashed at all</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R244 (its attribution and mod-erase halves) · Replaces: R137 (its section 'The mods ride with it' reversed by R244); R152 (its §2 (a nontoken mod on an Unstable host is trashed) superseded by R244); R153 (its step 4 (each nontoken mod is trashed) superseded by R244) · Tests: 224-mod-trash.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.trash.mods-erased-with-host</sub>

<a id="r801.2h"></a>**801.2h** An {Unstable} card that dies in play is erased instead of entering the bin, so it is not trashed. An {Unstable} card that goes to a bin from an inactive zone (a hand, the deck or a cache) enters the bin and is trashed. See rules 405.5, 400, 803. *(Engine differs, see F-U18-1.)*

> *Example (non-normative): Aberrant Statweaver (printed {Unstable}) discarded from a hand goes to the bin and is trashed: the hand is inactive.* <sub>test: 125-active-zone.test.ts::R145: a printed-Unstable card DISCARDED FROM HAND bins and TRASHES — hand is inactive</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Printed: card: Abyssal Evocation · Rulings: R145 (the Unstable glossary line it quotes), R145 · Replaces: R137 (STILL CURRENT as an owner ruling and NOT followed here: a dying {Unstable} card enters the bin, is trashed there and is only then erased. It records itself as a deliberate divergence from the printed reminder and from Caleb; under the authority order print and designer outrank it (D-U18-1, F-U18-1)) · Tests: 125-active-zone.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.trash.unstable-death</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U07-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r801.2i"></a>**801.2i** An effect that counts cards trashed counts only cards. A token dying never adds to the count.

> *Example (non-normative): Dropslime deals damage equal to the cards trashed this battle, and the tokens that died in it do not count.* <sub>test: 338-tokens-are-not-trashed.test.ts::R306: Dropslime deals damage for the CARDS trashed this battle and not for the tokens</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Dropslime · Rulings: R306 · Tests: 338-tokens-are-not-trashed.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.trash.count-cards-only</sub>

<a id="r801.3"></a>**801.3.** To discard a card is to put it from a hand into the bin. A discarded card is trashed. Discarding is not playing the card, and a cached card cannot be discarded. See rules 402.5, 403.4, 801.2.

> *Example (non-normative): A card discarded from a hand is trashed by the player whose bin it enters.* <sub>test: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::R40: discarding from hand trashes, by the owner of the bin it enters</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A card held in a cache offers no discard, and an attempt to discard it from there is refused.* <sub>test: 429-cr-keyword-actions.test.ts::cr:keywords.actions.discard — a discard from a hand puts nothing on the stack and is not played, and a cached card cannot be discarded</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Rulings: R40 (its bin-entry definition, for cards), R65 (its discard-me section), R311 (its "Discard me" bullet) · Tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts, 429-cr-keyword-actions.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.discard</sub>

<a id="r801.4"></a>**801.4.** To sacrifice a unit is for a player to choose a unit they control and put it into their bin. A sacrificed unit dies. See rules 111.3, 111.8.

> *Example (non-normative): Immolate sacrifices a unit to draw a card.* <sub>test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::Immolate: sacrifice a unit to draw a card</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.41 · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.sacrifice</sub>

<a id="r801.4a"></a>**801.4a** A player can sacrifice only something they control. An effect may make an opponent sacrifice something; that opponent sacrifices one of their own units and chooses which.

> *Example (non-normative): General Smof: after combat each present player sacrifices a unit of their own choice.* <sub>test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::General Smof: after combat, each present player sacrifices a unit of their choice</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.41; Manual p.41; Manual p.41 · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts, 429-cr-keyword-actions.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.sacrifice.control</sub>

<a id="r801.4b"></a>**801.4b** A player can sacrifice only a unit in the region where the effect or cost happens, never one of their units in another region. See rules 601.1e, 111.3.

> *Example (non-normative): Ghord's sacrifice makes each opponent in Ghord's region sacrifice a unit there, and reaches no other region.* <sub>test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Another set: a Ghord sacrifice reaches only the opponent units in its own region</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.41 · Designer: RAQ 1454169054402314362#0 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.sacrifice.region</sub>

<a id="r801.4c"></a>**801.4c** A player told to sacrifice a unit who has no unit in the region sacrifices nothing. See rule 101.5.

> *Example (non-normative): Cull's "each player sacrifices a unit" with nobody holding a unit in the region kills nothing.* <sub>test: 179-empty-collection-branches.test.ts::Cull — "each player sacrifices a unit" with nobody holding a unit here says so and kills nothing</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.41 · Tests: 179-empty-collection-branches.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.sacrifice.none-available</sub>

<a id="r801.5"></a>**801.5.** To delete a unit is to remove it from play into the bin, as when a unit dies. Unless the effect names another bin, it goes to the bin a dying unit would go to. See rules 301.5, 405.2, 405.3.

> *Example (non-normative): Throw off a Cliff deletes a unit with 4 or more defense: it goes to the bin, as a death.* <sub>test: 182-correctness-sample.test.ts::Throw off a Cliff: only defense>=4 is offered, and the target is DELETED (bin, a death)</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.13; card: Throw off a Cliff · Tests: 182-correctness-sample.test.ts, 429-cr-keyword-actions.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.delete</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U18-9 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r801.5a"></a>**801.5a** An effect that deletes a unit and names where it goes overrides the usual bin. Pull Under puts the deleted unit and all of its mods into its caster's bin, where they stay. See rule 801.2e.

> *Example (non-normative): Pull Under deletes the target; it and its mods land in the caster's bin, not erased and not in the owner's bin.* <sub>test: 15-water-b.test.ts::Pull Under: deletes the target; it and its mods land in YOUR bin (not erased, not owner-binned)</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Pull Under · Tests: 15-water-b.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.delete.named-bin</sub>

<a id="r801.6"></a>**801.6.** To erase a card is to take it out of the game: it goes to the erased pile. When card text says "erase", the erased pile is where the card goes. See rules 407.1, 407.2, 410.2.

> *Example (non-normative): Celestial Purge erases its target unit: it goes to no bin.* <sub>test: 14-water-a.test.ts::Celestial Purge: erases target unit (no bin)</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R219, R219 · Tests: 14-water-a.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.erase</sub>

<a id="r801.6a"></a>**801.6a** Erasing a unit is neither a death nor a trash. It is a despawn. See rules 407.1c, 410.2.

> *Example (non-normative): Banishment erases a unit: no death and no trash, but its despawn is seen.* <sub>test: 145-erase-routes.test.ts::R172 (vii): Banishment still fires no 'died' and no 'trashed'</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Rulings: R40 (its bin-entry definition, for cards), R172 (§1 and its what-did-not-widen note), R172 (§1 and its what-did-not-widen note) · Tests: 145-erase-routes.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.erase.not-death</sub>

<a id="r801.7"></a>**801.7.** To recall a card is to put it into a hand. Printed recalls take a card from play, from a bin, from the stack or from a cache. See rules 402.4, 410.2.

> *Example (non-normative): Vaporweave Eidolon recalls itself from play for [zero].* <sub>test: 15-water-b.test.ts::Vaporweave Eidolon: [zero]: recall me — a free activated self-recall</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Eldritch Reclaimer recalls a unit from its controller's bin to their hand.* <sub>test: 14-water-a.test.ts::Eldritch Reclaimer: recalls a unit from your bin to your hand, spawns 4/2</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Prismatic Observer recalls an enemy's cached card to its owner's hand.* <sub>test: 38-light-a.test.ts::Prismatic Observer: sacrifice to recall a cached card (either cache, in battle) and gain 3 life</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 3 tests run · Printed: card: Eldritch Reclaimer; card: Vaporweave Eidolon; card: Cosmic Reversal; card: Prismatic Observer · Tests: 15-water-b.test.ts, 14-water-a.test.ts, 38-light-a.test.ts, 429-cr-keyword-actions.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.recall</sub>

<a id="r801.7a"></a>**801.7a** A unit recalled from play goes to the hand of the player who controls it, not necessarily its owner, unless the effect names another hand. Recalling does not change who owns the card. See rules 102, 711.

> *Example (non-normative): A stolen unit that is recalled goes to the thief's hand, not its owner's.* <sub>test: 246-zones-follow-control.test.ts::R262 §1: a stolen unit recalled goes to the THIEF hand, not the owner</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Cosmic Reversal recalls a stolen spell unit to the seat that controls it.* <sub>test: 229-cosmic-and-control.test.ts::R250: a STOLEN spell unit is recalled to the seat that CONTROLS it</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 2 tests run · Rulings: R262, R262, R262 · Tests: 246-zones-follow-control.test.ts, 229-cosmic-and-control.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.recall.destination</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U07-10 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r801.7b"></a>**801.7b** A recalled {Unstable} unit goes to the hand as a card. {Unstable} changes only a move into a bin, so a recall is not affected by it. See rules 803, 410.4.

> *Example (non-normative): Recalling an {Unstable} unit puts the card in its hand; it is not erased.* <sub>test: 125-active-zone.test.ts::R145: RECALLING an Unstable unit puts the CARD IN HAND — Unstable never fires</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Abyssal Evocation · Tests: 125-active-zone.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.recall.unstable</sub>

<a id="r801.7c"></a>**801.7c** Recalling a card from a bin moves it from that bin to its player's hand. "Recall target unit in your bin" can reach only a card in that player's own bin. See rule 405.7.

> *Example (non-normative): Delver of Mysteries recalls a chosen spell from its controller's bin.* <sub>test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::Delver of Mysteries: recalls a chosen spell from the bin, then spawns 2/2</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Eldritch Reclaimer, cast with both players in the battle, offers a unit in its caster's own bin and never one in the opponent's bin.* <sub>test: 429-cr-keyword-actions.test.ts::cr:keywords.actions.recall.from-bin — Eldritch Reclaimer offers a unit in its own bin and never one in the opponent bin, even with both players in the battle</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Eldritch Reclaimer; card: Delver of Mysteries · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts, 429-cr-keyword-actions.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.recall.from-bin</sub>

<a id="r801.7d"></a>**801.7d** Recalling a spell effect on the stack negates it and puts the card into its controller's hand. A recalled spell token enters its controller's hand and is then erased. See rules 704.4, 410.5b.

> *Example (non-normative): Cosmic Reversal recalls the other spell effects on the stack to their controllers' hands.* <sub>test: 14-water-a.test.ts::Cosmic Reversal: recalls all other spell effects on the stack to hands</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Dream Lapse recalls a cast Fireball token: it enters the hand (Rider of the Tides hears it) and is erased.* <sub>test: 403-raq-fix-mods.test.ts::R335: Dream Lapse recalls a cast Fireball token</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: card: Cosmic Reversal · Rulings: R335 · Tests: 14-water-a.test.ts, 403-raq-fix-mods.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.recall.from-stack</sub>

<a id="r801.7e"></a>**801.7e** When an effect tells a player to recall a unit and they have none to recall, the recall does nothing, but the rest of the effect still happens unless it depends on the recall ("If you do"). See rule 101.5.

> *Example (non-normative): Recall ("Each player recalls a unit and loses 2 life"): a player with no unit to recall still loses 2 life.* <sub>test: 179-empty-collection-branches.test.ts::Recall — the life loss happens, the recall does not, and the card now says which</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Shoreline Specter: if the recall is declined, the life drain that follows "If you do" does not happen.* <sub>test: 182-correctness-sample.test.ts::Shoreline Specter: DECLINE the recall and the 2-life drain does not happen</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: card: Shoreline Specter · Rulings: R30, R30 · Tests: 179-empty-collection-branches.test.ts, 182-correctness-sample.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.recall.nothing-to-recall</sub>

<a id="r801.8"></a>**801.8.** To cache a card is to put it into a player's cache. A unit cached from play goes to its controller's cache unless the effect names another, and its mods go to the bin. See rules 403.1, 403.7, 410.5c.

> *Example (non-normative): A stolen unit that is cached goes to the thief's cache.* <sub>test: 246-zones-follow-control.test.ts::R262 §1: a stolen unit cached goes to the THIEF cache</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Grob caches a stolen unit into its controller's cache, as its text says.* <sub>test: 135-exchange-and-zones.test.ts::R157 §27: Grob caches a STOLEN unit into the CONTROLLER’s cache</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: card: Grob · Rulings: R262, R157 (§27) · Tests: 246-zones-follow-control.test.ts, 135-exchange-and-zones.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.cache</sub>

<a id="r801.8a"></a>**801.8a** Caching a card does not by itself let anyone use it. A cached card can be played or used as a mod only while a permission on it is live: a glimpse that cached it this turn, a fulfilled prophecy, or the text of the effect that cached it. See rules 403.3, 403.3a, 801.9.

> *Example (non-normative): Murkdrop Distiller caches a trashed card; its own text then lets its controller play it until end of turn.* <sub>test: 182-correctness-sample.test.ts::Murkdrop Distiller: a trashed card may be cached, and cached is where it goes</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Murkdrop Distiller · Rulings: R303 · Tests: 182-correctness-sample.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.cache.no-permission</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U18-8 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r801.9"></a>**801.9.** Glimpse N means: reveal the top N cards of the deck, cache one of them, and recycle the rest. See rules 403, 408.2a.

> *Example (non-normative): Oracle of Foretelling's Glimpse 5 caches one of the five revealed cards.* <sub>test: 14-water-a.test.ts::Oracle of Foretelling: Glimpse 5 caches ONE of the five</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Glimpse N reveals N, caches exactly one of the glimpser's choice and recycles the rest.* <sub>test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::R45: Glimpse N reveals N, caches exactly ONE of the glimpser's choice and recycles the rest</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: card: Premonition · Rulings: R45 · Tests: 14-water-a.test.ts, 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.glimpse</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U18-7 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r801.9a"></a>**801.9a** The player who glimpses chooses which of the revealed cards to cache.

> *Example (non-normative): Choosing the last revealed card caches it and recycles the two above it.* <sub>test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::R45: choosing the LAST revealed card recycles the two above it, in order</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R45 · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.glimpse.choice</sub>

<a id="r801.9b"></a>**801.9b** Glimpse 1 reveals the top card of the deck and caches it. There is no choice to make and nothing to recycle.

> *Example (non-normative): Glimpse 1 raises no decision.* <sub>test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::R45: Glimpse 1 raises no decision</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Visionary Construct · Rulings: R45 · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.glimpse.one</sub>

<a id="r801.9c"></a>**801.9c** "Glimpse 1, X times" is X separate glimpses of one card each, not one Glimpse X.

> *Example (non-normative): Glook discards X cards when activated and then glimpses 1, X times.* <sub>test: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts::R196 Glook "[once] Discard X cards: Glimpse 1, X times"</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Glook · Rulings: R45 · Tests: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.glimpse.repeated</sub>

<a id="r801.9d"></a>**801.9d** A glimpse reveals from the glimpser's own deck. When an effect makes another player glimpse ("Its controller Glimpses 3"), that player reveals from their own deck, not from the deck of the player who controls the effect. In live draft every player's deck is the one shared deck. See rules 401, 902.

> *Example (non-normative): Celestial Purge cast by one player erases an enemy unit; the unit's controller is the glimpser, chooses the card to cache and caches it in their own cache. (The test game uses one shared deck, so it does not show whose deck is read.)* <sub>test: 14-water-a.test.ts::Celestial Purge: erases target unit (no bin); its controller Glimpses 3</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): In constructed, a player who glimpses reveals the top of their own deck, caches from it and recycles the rest into their own pile; the other player's deck is untouched.* <sub>test: 429-cr-keyword-actions.test.ts::cr:keywords.actions.glimpse.whose-deck — in constructed a glimpse reads the deck of the glimpser and leaves the other deck untouched</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Printed: card: Dematerialize; card: Celestial Purge · Rulings: R157 (§18, its shared-deck sentence) · Tests: 14-water-a.test.ts, 429-cr-keyword-actions.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.glimpse.whose-deck</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U18-12 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r801.9e"></a>**801.9e** Until end of turn, the glimpser may play the cached card as if it were in their hand, ignoring affinity. See rules 403.3a, 403.3b.

> *Example (non-normative): A card with affinity its glimpser cannot meet can be played from the cache, for its mana only.* <sub>test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::R45: a card with no affinity is ILLEGAL from hand but LEGAL from cache, for mana only</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Premonition · Rulings: R45 · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.glimpse.permission</sub>

<a id="r801.9f"></a>**801.9f** A card played under a glimpse permission still costs its mana, and still obeys its printed timing. Only the affinity requirement is waived. See rules 403.3c, 403.3d.

> *Example (non-normative): A glimpsed card whose mana cannot be paid is refused.* <sub>test: 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts::R303: the glimpse waives the pips, NOT the mana — broke means refused</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A glimpsed {Battle} card cannot be played in deployment.* <sub>test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::R45: glimpse still obeys timing, and a short deck glimpses fewer</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R45, R45 · Tests: 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts, 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.glimpse.permission.cost-timing</sub>

<a id="r801.9g"></a>**801.9g** The same permission lets the glimpser apply the cached card as a mod, on the same terms (its mana, ignoring affinity): an augment or graft during deployment, and a {Virus} during battle. See rules 403.3b, 721, 722, 723.

> *Example (non-normative): A live glimpse grafts for the card's mana, ignoring affinity.* <sub>test: 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts::R303: a LIVE glimpse grafts for the card's mana, ignoring affinity</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A glimpsed {Virus} in the cache goes onto an enemy unit in battle.* <sub>test: 370-cached-virus-in-battle.test.ts::R311: a glimpsed Virus in the cache goes onto an ENEMY unit in battle, ignoring affinity</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 3 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1537748882501668934#3; RAQ 1537748882501668934#4 · Rulings: R303 · Tests: 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts, 370-cached-virus-in-battle.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.glimpse.permission.mods</sub>

<a id="r801.9h"></a>**801.9h** While the permission is live, a glimpsed card with a prophecy banner may be prophesied where it stands in the cache, in the same window and for the same cost as from the hand. Doing so uses up the glimpse permission. See rules 403.8, 801.14, 803.

> *Example (non-normative): A glimpsed card with a banner may be prophesied where it stands in the cache.* <sub>test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::R308: a GLIMPSED card with a banner may be prophesied where it stands in the cache</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R308, R308 · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.glimpse.permission.prophesy</sub>

<a id="r801.9i"></a>**801.9i** The permission ends at end of turn. The card stays in the cache, and it can no longer be played, prophesied or applied as a mod there. See rule 403.5.

> *Example (non-normative): An expired glimpse is not a graft, not an augment, not anything.* <sub>test: 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts::R303: an expired glimpse is not a graft, not an augment, not anything</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Premonition's permission dies with the turn; the card stays cached.* <sub>test: 14-water-a.test.ts::Premonition: Glimpse X where X is your water affinity; the permission dies with the turn, the card stays</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 3 tests run · Printed: card: Premonition · Rulings: R45, R303, R308 · Replaces: R190 (its Glimpse glossary row's "stays cached, inert" amended by R206; R303 later restored "inert" (D-U18-10)) · Tests: 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts, 14-water-a.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.glimpse.permission.ends</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U07-6 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r801.10"></a>**801.10.** To recycle a card is to put it on the bottom of the deck. A recycled card goes past the deck's mark into the recycle pile. See rules 408.1, 408.2, 106.6.

> *Example (non-normative): Tides of the Cosmos recycles the revealed cards it did not play.* <sub>test: 15-water-b.test.ts::Tides of the Cosmos: reveal 8, play up to two with total cost ≤ 8 for free, recycle the rest</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A recycled card stays behind the mark while the deck still has cards.* <sub>test: 300-recycle-mark.test.ts::R296 §1 a recycled card stays behind the mark while the deck still has cards</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 2 tests run · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.7; Manual p.16 · Rulings: R190 (its Recycle row), R296, R296 · Tests: 15-water-b.test.ts, 300-recycle-mark.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.recycle</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U07-12 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r801.11"></a>**801.11.** When two units fight, each deals damage equal to its power to the other. See rule 112.

> *Example (non-normative): Battle: two target units fight, dealing damage to each other.* <sub>test: 16-earth-a.test.ts::Battle: two target units fight (mutual power damage; both targets at cast)</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Fight; card: Eminence of the Barrens · Tests: 16-earth-a.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.fight</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U18-6 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r801.11a"></a>**801.11a** Each fighting unit is the source of the damage it deals, with its own current attributes. Attributes the fight spell itself has do not apply to that damage. See rules 112.6, 802.

> *Example (non-normative): A fighter that gained {Powerful} deals double damage.* <sub>test: 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts::R318: Fight — a fighter that GAINED Powerful deals double</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A {Powerful} virus on the Fight spell does not double either fighter's damage.* <sub>test: 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts::R318: Fight — a Powerful virus on the Fight spell does not double either fighter</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1402292180499955884#0 · Rulings: R318 · Tests: 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.fight.source</sub>

<a id="r801.11b"></a>**801.11b** Damage dealt in a fight is dealt by the units, not by the spell or ability that made them fight. Abilities that look for damage dealt by a spell effect do not see it. See rule 112.6.

> *Example (non-normative): Squish damage is the unit dealing it, so Ember of Life does not trigger; the designer's answer covers Fight and Battle the same way.* <sub>test: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Squish: Squish damage is the unit dealing it, so Ember of Life does not trigger</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Fight makes a 3-power unit deal 3 damage, and Ember of Life does not trigger; a spell dealing damage in the same setup does trigger it.* <sub>test: 429-cr-keyword-actions.test.ts::cr:keywords.actions.fight.not-spell-damage — the 3 damage Fight makes a unit deal does not trigger Ember of Life</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1402292180499955884#2 · Tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts, 429-cr-keyword-actions.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.fight.not-spell-damage</sub>

<a id="r801.11c"></a>**801.11c** A fight needs both of its units. If one of them is gone when the fight would happen, nothing happens: the remaining unit deals and is dealt no damage. The effect does not fizzle. See rules 704.6c, 101.5.

> *Example (non-normative): Fight that loses one of its two targets does nothing to the survivor.* <sub>test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ fizzles: Fight that loses one of its two targets does nothing to the survivor</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.43 · Designer: RAQ 1354013430805434389#1 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts, 429-cr-keyword-actions.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.fight.lost-one</sub>

<a id="r801.12"></a>**801.12.** Rockfall N means: each player chooses one of their units, and the source of the rockfall deals N damage to each chosen unit. See rule 112.

> *Example (non-normative): A Fast Pile of Rocks dies and rockfalls 4: each player picks one of their own units, and each takes exactly 4.* <sub>test: 182-correctness-sample.test.ts::A Fast Pile of Rocks: on MY death each player picks one of THEIR OWN units for exactly 4</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: A Fast Pile of Rocks; card: Meteor Shower · Tests: 182-correctness-sample.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.rockfall</sub>

<a id="r801.12a"></a>**801.12a** Rockfall chooses; it does not target. No targets are declared when it goes on the stack, and an effect that stops targeting cannot stop it. See rule 110.

> *Example (non-normative): Boon of Protection has nothing to negate when a Meteor Shower falls on its unit.* <sub>test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Meteor Shower: rockfall chooses rather than targets, so Boon of Protection has nothing to negate</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1353899470156206152#3; RAQ 1353899470156206152#3 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.rockfall.chooses</sub>

<a id="r801.12b"></a>**801.12b** Each player must choose a living unit of theirs in the region. A player with no unit there chooses none, and takes no part in that rockfall. See rule 601.1b.

> *Example (non-normative): Meteor Shower with no unit anywhere to hit announces each empty rockfall.* <sub>test: 93-engine-defects.test.ts::Meteor Shower with no unit anywhere to hit announces each empty rockfall</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1353899470156206152#4 · Tests: 93-engine-defects.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.rockfall.living-unit</sub>

<a id="r801.12c"></a>**801.12c** "Rockfall N, X times" is X rockfalls carried out one after another. Each player chooses again for each of them, and each rockfall is a separate source of damage. See rule 112.

> *Example (non-normative): Meteor Shower rockfalls 3 three times: each player picks each time, and the damage stacks up.* <sub>test: 17-earth-b.test.ts::Meteor Shower: rockfall 3 three times — each player picks, damage stacks up</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Meteor Shower · Designer: RAQ 1353899470156206152#4 · Rulings: R80, R80 · Tests: 17-earth-b.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.rockfall.repeated</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U18-4 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r801.13"></a>**801.13.** "Exchange" is printed in four senses, each read from its card: exchanging a unit in play for a unit card in a bin (Hooba-Mon, Necromorph), exchanging control of two units (Organic Exchange), exchanging control of a unit for a spell another player played (Hexbane Shiitake), and exchanging the base stats of two units (Body Swap). See rules 711, 106.8.

> *Example (non-normative): Organic Exchange swaps control of two units.* <sub>test: 24-wood-b.test.ts::Organic Exchange: control swaps and the attack slot passes to the exchanged unit</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Hexbane Shiitake gives itself away and takes control of an enemy spell.* <sub>test: 23-wood-a.test.ts::Hexbane Shiitake: exchanges the carrier for an enemy spell and retargets it ([once])</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Body Swap exchanges two units' base stats.* <sub>test: 26-metal-a.test.ts::Body Swap: exchanges the base stats of two target units until regroup</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 5 tests run · Printed: card: Necromorph; card: Organic Exchange; card: Body Swap; card: Hexbane Shiitake · Tests: 24-wood-b.test.ts, 23-wood-a.test.ts, 26-metal-a.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.exchange</sub>

<a id="r801.13a"></a>**801.13a** When a unit in play is exchanged for a unit card in a bin, the unit leaving play despawns and goes to the bin, where it is trashed, but it does not die. See rules 410.2a, 410.4d, 704.6c.

> *Example (non-normative): Necromorph's exchange fires no death trigger, but the unit despawns and is trashed.* <sub>test: 135-exchange-and-zones.test.ts::R157 §3: Necromorph’s exchange fires NO death trigger — but it despawns and it trashes</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Hooba-Mon exchanging an unmodded host: the host goes to the bin and stays there.* <sub>test: 42-dark-b.test.ts::R146 control: Hooba-Mon exchanges an UNMODDED host → it still BINS and stays there</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R157 (§3) · Tests: 135-exchange-and-zones.test.ts, 42-dark-b.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.exchange.unit-for-bin</sub>

<a id="r801.14"></a>**801.14.** To prophesy a card is to pay the cost on its prophecy banner and put it into the cache with its prophecy attached. Prophecy itself is 803. See rules 803, 403.8.

> *Example (non-normative): A glimpsed Vengeance is offered its prophecy in deployment.* <sub>test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::R308: the real card — a glimpsed Vengeance is offered its prophecy in deployment</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R42 (its cache-with-the-prophecy-attached definition), R308 · Replaces: R42 (its no-affinity cost corrected by R301; its window amended by R277; its source zone amended by R308) · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Key: keywords.actions.prophesy</sub>

<a id="r802"></a>
### 802. Attributes

<a id="r802.1"></a>**802.1. General.** Attributes are qualities a card can have that change how it engages in combat (see rule 204). See rule 204. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.12; Manual p.24 · Key: attr.general</sub>

<a id="r802.1a"></a>**802.1a** Cards with attributes carry reminder text, in italics, to help players remember what each attribute does. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.24; Manual p.24 · Key: attr.general.reminder</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U20-1 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.1b"></a>**802.1b** Attributes are combat attributes or non-combat attributes. Combat attributes are printed in gold. Non-combat attributes, such as Burst and Unstable, are printed in purple and generally have nothing to do with combat. See rules 204, 803. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.24; Manual p.25; Manual p.25 · Key: attr.general.kinds</sub>

<a id="r802.1c"></a>**802.1c** Combat attributes are shared by the units in the same column of a formation: while a unit is in a column, it has every combat attribute that any unit in that column has. See rules 603.1a, 602.

> *Example (non-normative): A token attacking in a column behind a Flying unit has Flying too.* <sub>test: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts::cr:combat.columns.definition.shared-attributes — Flying on the front unit of a column is shared</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.24; Rulebook 2023 p.12 · Rulings: R93 · Tests: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Key: attr.general.shared</sub>

<a id="r802.1d"></a>**802.1d** Attributes are not shared with the units to the left or right of a unit. They are shared only within its column. See rule 603.1a.

> *Example (non-normative): A unit attacking in the next column beside a Flying unit does not have Flying.* <sub>test: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts::cr:combat.columns.definition.shared-attributes — Flying on the front unit of a column is shared</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.24; Rulebook 2023 p.12 · Tests: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Key: attr.general.shared.not-sideways</sub>

<a id="r802.1e"></a>**802.1e** A unit has the attributes of its column for everything it does while it is in the column, not only for combat damage. Damage it deals with its abilities has those attributes too. See rule 112.6.

> *Example (non-normative): An ability of a unit in a column with a Blessed unit gains its controller life when it deals damage.* <sub>test: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts::R294 §1 the report</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Bellowing Boulder, in a column with a Deadly unit, pings with Deadly.* <sub>test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ dead unit: Bellowing Boulder in a column with a Deadly unit pings with Deadly</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1353895783266516992#5 · Rulings: R294, R294 · Tests: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts, 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Key: attr.general.shared.all-purposes</sub>

<a id="r802.1f"></a>**802.1f** Columns exist only during a battle. Outside a battle no unit is in a column, so no attribute is shared. See rules 602, 603.

> *Example (non-normative): Outside battle, a unit standing beside a Blessed unit gains nothing from it.* <sub>test: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts::R294 §3 outside battle there are no columns at all</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R294 · Tests: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts, 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Key: attr.general.shared.combat-only</sub>

<a id="r802.1g"></a>**802.1g** When a unit leaves a column, the other units in that column immediately lose the attributes it was sharing with them. See rules 603.1a, 608.2b.

> *Example (non-normative): A unit leaving a Swift column takes the Swift it shared with it.* <sub>test: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.substeps.column-attributes — a unit leaving a column takes the Swift it shared with it</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Once the Deadly unit leaves Bellowing Boulder's column, the Boulder's ping is not Deadly.* <sub>test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ dead unit: once the Deadly partner leaves the column, the Boulder ping is not Deadly</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: Manual p.24; Manual p.24; Rulebook 2023 p.12 · Designer: RAQ 1353895783266516992#5 · Tests: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts, 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Key: attr.general.shared.leaving</sub>

<a id="r802.1h"></a>**802.1h** Non-combat attributes are not shared in formation. A unit that is Unstable, or has Burst or Modular, does not give that attribute to the other units in its column. See rule 803.

> *Example (non-normative): A modded (and so Unstable) unit does not make its column-mate Unstable.* <sub>test: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts::R294 §5b a modded (therefore Unstable) unit does not make its column-mate Unstable</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: Manual p.25 · Rulings: R294 · Tests: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts · Key: attr.general.noncombat-not-shared</sub>

<a id="r802.1i"></a>**802.1i** A card either has an attribute or does not. Having the same attribute from more than one source has no extra effect.

> *Example (non-normative): Two sources granting Inverted to one unit invert its stat changes once, not twice.* <sub>test: 79-round17-layers.test.ts::R93 layer 5: {Inverted} applies ONCE however many sources grant it</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R19, R84 · Tests: 79-round17-layers.test.ts · Key: attr.general.present-or-not</sub>

<a id="r802.1j"></a>**802.1j** Four attributes change a unit's stats. Tough and Balanced apply in the fourth stat layer, Inverted in the fifth and Unaware in the sixth and last (see rule 206.4). See rules 206.4, 709.

> *Example (non-normative): Caleb's worked example: a 1/4 with Tough, Balanced and Inverted is a -6/0.* <sub>test: 79-round17-layers.test.ts::R93 layer 5: Caleb's worked example — a 1/4 Tough Balanced Inverted is a -6/0</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A unit with both Inverted and Unaware is read at its printed stats: Unaware applies last.* <sub>test: 92-unaware.test.ts::{Inverted} and {Unaware} on one unit: layer 6 goes last, so Bubb is a 5/6</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: Manual p.42 · Rulings: R19 · Tests: 79-round17-layers.test.ts, 92-unaware.test.ts · Key: attr.general.stat-attributes</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U16-2 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.1k"></a>**802.1k** A unit's stats are worked out through all the stat layers before it is checked for death. A unit whose defense would be 0 or less part-way through the calculation, but not at the end of it, does not die. See rules 206.4, 713.

> *Example (non-normative): A 1/1 with a -1/-1 counter and Inverted is a live 2/2, never a dead 0/0.* <sub>test: 79-round17-layers.test.ts::R93 layer 5: hitting 0 mid-calculation is not death</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Child of Aether, a 2/0 with Balanced, is a 2/2 and survives.* <sub>test: 08-cards2.test.ts::Child of Aether: Balanced (power & defense = max) keeps a 2/0 alive</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R93, R93 · Tests: 79-round17-layers.test.ts, 08-cards2.test.ts · Key: attr.general.stats-then-death</sub>

<a id="r802.1m"></a>**802.1m** When Tough and Balanced both apply to a unit, they apply one after the other, from top to bottom. If Tough is augmented onto a Balanced unit, or a Tough unit attacks with a Balanced unit behind it, the unit has its defense doubled, then its stats balanced. If Tough is applied to a Balanced unit, it has its stats balanced, then its defense doubled. Attributes granted by a unit's augments apply in the order the mods were gained, the first attached first, and attributes shared from its column apply from front to back. An attribute the unit has from more than one source takes the position of the first. See rules 206.4, 721. *(Engine differs, see F-U19-5.)*

> *Example (non-normative): A 3/1 augmented with Rampart Guardian (Tough) and then Child of Aether (Balanced) is a 3/3; augmented in the other order it is a 3/6.* <sub>test: 08-cards2.test.ts::R19: layer-4 application order — Tough→Balanced ≠ Balanced→Tough</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Child of Aether prints Balanced and is a 2/0. Augmented with Rampart Guardian (Tough), its defense is doubled (2/0), then its stats balanced: it is a 2/2. (illustrative; engine differs, F-U19-5: the engine balances first and makes it a 2/4)*

> *Example (non-normative): Rampart Guardian (0/4, Tough) attacks with Child of Aether (Balanced) behind it: its defense is doubled (0/8), then its stats balanced, and it is an 8/8.* <sub>test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.general.application-order — a Tough unit attacking with a Balanced unit behind it is doubled, then balanced: Rampart Guardian is an 8/8</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: partial, round 3, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.42; Manual p.42; Manual p.42; Manual p.42; Manual p.42; Manual p.42 · Rulings: R19 (its mod-stack and column order, and its duplicate rule; not its printed-first order), R19 (its mod-stack and column order, and its duplicate rule; not its printed-first order), R19 (its mod-stack and column order, and its duplicate rule; not its printed-first order) · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts, 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Key: attr.general.application-order</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U16-1, D-U19-12 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.1n"></a>**802.1n** A Pure card, and every card interacting with it, ignores all its other attributes in that interaction (see rule 802.25). This includes the attributes that change stats: in an interaction with a Pure card, Tough, Balanced, Inverted and Unaware do not apply. See rule 802.25. *(Engine differs, see F-U19-1, F-U19-2.)*

> *Example (non-normative): Rampart Guardian (a 0/4 with Tough) is dealt 5 damage by a Pure source. In that interaction it ignores Tough, so its defense is 4 and it dies. (illustrative; engine differs, F-U19-1: the engine keeps Tough on and it survives as a 0/8)*

> *Example (non-normative): An Unaware source dealing 3 damage to a Pure unit pumped from 2/3 to 4/5 does not read it at its printed 2/3: it survives, where a pumped non-Pure 2/3 dies.* <sub>test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.general.pure — Unaware is off in a Pure pairing outside combat: an Unaware source does not collapse a pumped Pure recipient to its printed stats</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 3, 0 tests run · Printed: card: Just a Unit; Manual p.42 · Rulings: R289 (its per-pairing switch, which turns a Pure pairing's Unaware off) · Tests: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Key: attr.general.pure</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U19-2 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.2"></a>**802.2. Flying.** Flying is a combat attribute. Its reminder text reads "Only flying units can block flying units."

> *Example (non-normative): A Flying 3/1 attacks; a ground unit may not block it, and a unit with Flying may.* <sub>test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.flying — Air Plant prints the reminder, and only a flying unit may block a Flying attacker</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: card: Air Plant; Manual p.24 · Our glossary (not a source): Flying · Tests: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Key: attr.flying</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U12-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.2a"></a>**802.2a** An attacking column that has Flying can't be blocked by a unit that does not have Flying. See rule 606.2c.

> *Example (non-normative): A ground 2/2 cannot block a column holding Ephemeral Skywalker (Flying).* <sub>test: 02-combat.test.ts::combat math: columns, flying, piercing overflow, deaths</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A plain ground unit is neither offered nor allowed as a blocker against a Flying column.* <sub>test: 40-light-c.test.ts::Just a Unit: {Pure} blocks a Flying column, and only it can</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: card: Greed Angel; Manual p.24 · Tests: 02-combat.test.ts, 40-light-c.test.ts, 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts · Key: attr.flying.blocking</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U19-5 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.2b"></a>**802.2b** Because Flying is shared, a unit attacking in the same column as a Flying unit has Flying too, and the whole column can't be blocked by units that do not have Flying (see rule 802.1). See rule 802.1.

> *Example (non-normative): A token attacking behind a Flying unit has Flying while it is in that column.* <sub>test: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts::cr:combat.columns.definition.shared-attributes — Flying on the front unit of a column is shared</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.24; Rulebook 2023 p.12 · Tests: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Key: attr.flying.column</sub>

<a id="r802.2c"></a>**802.2c** If the Flying unit leaves an attacking column before blockers are declared, the other units in that column lose Flying, and the column can then be blocked by units without Flying. See rules 802.1, 606.

> *Example (non-normative): A player attacks with Smoke Ghost (Flying) and a plain 1/1 token in one column; the opponent kills Smoke Ghost before combat and blocks the token with a unit that does not fly. (illustrative)*

> *Example (non-normative): Ephemeral Skywalker (Flying) attacks with a 1/1 token in one column; the Skywalker is destroyed before blocks, the token loses Flying, and Rune Channeler, which does not fly, blocks it.* <sub>test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.flying.removed — after the Flying unit leaves the attacking column, a ground unit may block the rest</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.12; Rulebook 2023 p.12; Manual p.24 · Tests: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Key: attr.flying.removed</sub>

<a id="r802.2d"></a>**802.2d** Flying does not restrict a block when the attacking column or the blocking unit includes a Pure card. A Pure unit can block a Flying column. See rule 802.25.

> *Example (non-normative): Just a Unit (Pure, no Flying) blocks a column holding Ephemeral Skywalker (Flying) and kills it.* <sub>test: 40-light-c.test.ts::Just a Unit: {Pure} blocks a Flying column, and only it can</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Just a Unit · Rulings: R61, R61 · Tests: 40-light-c.test.ts · Key: attr.flying.pure</sub>

<a id="r802.2e"></a>**802.2e** A unit without Flying is not able to block a Flying column, so an Alluring trigger cannot compel it to block that column (see rules 606.2e and 802.15). See rules 606.2e, 802.15.

> *Example (non-normative): A lured unit with no Flying, facing a Flying Alluring column, may leave that column unblocked.* <sub>test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::R84: a lured unit with no {Flying} is not able against a Flying column</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R84 · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Key: attr.flying.lured</sub>

<a id="r802.3"></a>**802.3. Deadly.** Deadly is a combat attribute. Its reminder text reads "Any damage from a deadly source will kill a unit."

> *Example (non-normative): Tidepool Terror (1/2 Deadly) is blocked by a 5/9; its 1 damage kills the blocker.* <sub>test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.deadly — Rotspore Herald prints the reminder, and 1 combat damage from a Deadly attacker kills a 5/9 blocker</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: card: Rotspore Herald; Manual p.25 · Our glossary (not a source): Deadly · Tests: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Key: attr.deadly</sub>

<a id="r802.3a"></a>**802.3a** A unit dealt any nonzero amount of damage by a Deadly source is destroyed, whatever its defense. A Deadly source that deals 0 damage destroys nothing.

> *Example (non-normative): A Deadly source dealing 2 noncombat damage destroys a 5/6.* <sub>test: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts::Deadly: 2 points of NON-COMBAT damage kills a 5/6 outright</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Zero damage from a Deadly source destroys nothing.* <sub>test: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts::Deadly: ZERO damage kills nothing</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: card: Rotspore Herald · Rulings: R21 (its nonzero-kill sentence) · Tests: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts · Key: attr.deadly.any-amount</sub>

<a id="r802.3b"></a>**802.3b** Deadly does not reduce the damage its source deals. A Deadly source deals all of its damage; Deadly changes only how much of it is lethal. See rule 608.6d.

> *Example (non-normative): A 10-power Deadly column blocked by a 1/1 deals all 10 to it.* <sub>test: 134-column-and-substep.test.ts::R157 §11 — a 10-power {Deadly} column deals all 10 to a 1/1 blocker</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R157 §11 · Tests: 134-column-and-substep.test.ts, 05-rulings.test.ts · Key: attr.deadly.no-cap</sub>

<a id="r802.3c"></a>**802.3c** In combat damage assignment, lethal damage for each unit a Deadly half-column deals damage to is 1 (see rule 608.6e). Once the front unit has been assigned at least 1, the dealing player may assign damage to the unit behind it. See rules 608.6e, 608.6b.

> *Example (non-normative): A Deadly and Piercing column over two blockers assigns 1 to each, and the rest may go to the player.* <sub>test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Excessive: Deadly + Piercing over two blockers</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1353888077625561108#3; RAQ 1353888077625561108#6 · Rulings: R23 · Replaces: R21 (its "auto-assignment ... sends everything past 1-per-blocker through" is only the default since R319 made the excess elective; its engine-call flag is resolved by the RAQ) · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 100-elective-assign.test.ts · Key: attr.deadly.combat-share</sub>

<a id="r802.3d"></a>**802.3d** A unit dealt combat damage by a Deadly source is destroyed in the same damage sub-step, before the next sub-step begins (see rule 608.7b). See rule 608.7b.

> *Example (non-normative): Paired with a Swift unit in its column, a Deadly unit kills what it hits before that unit can strike back. (illustrative)* <sub>test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.deadly.timing — a Deadly and Swift column kills its blocker in the Swift sub-step, before the blocker strikes</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.25 · Rulings: R21 (its same-sub-step kill) · Tests: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Key: attr.deadly.timing</sub>

<a id="r802.3e"></a>**802.3e** Deadly applies to all damage its source deals, not only combat damage, including damage dealt through spells and abilities. See rule 112.7.

> *Example (non-normative): A plain Deadly effect source destroys a unit it could never damage to death.* <sub>test: 206-deadly-everywhere.test.ts::R237: a plain {Deadly} effect source kills a unit</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R237, R21 (its effect-damage sentence) · Tests: 206-deadly-everywhere.test.ts, 82-attr-interactions.test.ts · Key: attr.deadly.noncombat</sub>

<a id="r802.3f"></a>**802.3f** A spell or a spell token can have Deadly. Damage it deals is then Deadly damage. See rules 302, 304.

> *Example (non-normative): With Rotspore Herald in the region, a Fireball 1 kills any unit it hits.* <sub>test: 206-deadly-everywhere.test.ts::R237: "a fireball 1 with deadly would kill any unit"</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Deadly donated to a spell on the stack kills through that spell.* <sub>test: 206-deadly-everywhere.test.ts::R237: a {Deadly} donated to a SPELL on the stack kills through the spell</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R237, R125 · Tests: 206-deadly-everywhere.test.ts · Key: attr.deadly.spells</sub>

<a id="r802.3g"></a>**802.3g** A source with both Deadly and Poisonous that deals damage to a unit both destroys it and puts the -1/-1 counters on it (see rule 112.10). See rules 112.10, 802.18.

> *Example (non-normative): Deadly and Poisonous effect damage still destroys the unit: the counter form is still damage.* <sub>test: 206-deadly-everywhere.test.ts::R237: {Deadly} + {Poisonous} effect damage still kills</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R237 · Tests: 206-deadly-everywhere.test.ts, 82-attr-interactions.test.ts · Key: attr.deadly.poisonous</sub>

<a id="r802.3h"></a>**802.3h** If all the damage a Deadly source would deal to a unit is prevented, no damage is dealt, and Deadly does not destroy the unit (see rule 112.11). See rules 112.11, 608.7a.

> *Example (non-normative): Prevention stops both the Deadly kill and the Poisonous counters.* <sub>test: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts::Deadly + Poisonous: PREVENTION still stops both halves</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A shielded blocker dealt combat damage by a Deadly column is not destroyed.* <sub>test: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.dealing.prevention — a shielded blocker dealt COMBAT damage gets no damage event, nothing marked, and no Deadly kill</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R98 (its prevented-damage-is-not-dealt rule) · Tests: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts, 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Key: attr.deadly.prevention</sub>

<a id="r802.3i"></a>**802.3i** Deadly has no effect on damage dealt to a player. See rule 112.5.

> *Example (non-normative): An unblocked Carapace Devourer (3/3, Deadly) costs the defending player exactly 3 life.* <sub>test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.deadly.players — an unblocked Deadly 3/3 costs the defending player exactly 3 life</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Rulings: R21 (its players sentence) · Tests: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Key: attr.deadly.players</sub>

<a id="r802.3j"></a>**802.3j** Deadly does not apply in an interaction with a Pure card (see rule 802.25). See rules 802.25, 608.6e.

> *Example (non-normative): Just a Unit (Pure) blocking a Deadly unit is not killed by 1 damage.* <sub>test: 40-light-c.test.ts::Just a Unit: {Pure} switches off Deadly</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A Pure recipient is not destroyed by a Deadly source's noncombat damage.* <sub>test: 290-pure-outside-combat.test.ts::§2 a Pure recipient: the source's Powerful and Deadly do nothing to it</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: card: Just a Unit · Rulings: R61, R289 (its per-pairing switch) · Tests: 40-light-c.test.ts, 290-pure-outside-combat.test.ts · Key: attr.deadly.pure</sub>

<a id="r802.4"></a>**802.4. Swift.** Swift is a combat attribute. Its reminder text reads "Swift units deal combat damage first."

> *Example (non-normative): Dune Drifter (2/1 Swift) is blocked by a 2/2; the blocker dies before it strikes, and the Drifter survives undamaged.* <sub>test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.swift — Rime Wraith prints the reminder, and a Swift 2/1 kills a 2/2 blocker before it can strike back</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: card: Rime Wraith; Manual p.25 · Our glossary (not a source): Swift · Tests: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Key: attr.swift</sub>

<a id="r802.4a"></a>**802.4a** A half-column that has Swift deals its combat damage in the Swift sub-step, before the normal and Sluggish sub-steps (see rule 608.2a). See rules 608.2, 608.2a.

> *Example (non-normative): Swift strikes first, then normal, then Sluggish.* <sub>test: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.substeps — Swift, then normal, then Sluggish</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Rime Wraith; Manual p.25 · Tests: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Key: attr.swift.schedule</sub>

<a id="r802.4b"></a>**802.4b** A unit destroyed by Swift damage in the Swift sub-step deals no combat damage in the later sub-steps. See rule 608.7b.

> *Example (non-normative): A Swift attacker kills a 2/2 blocker, which never strikes back.* <sub>test: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.overview.simultaneous — a Swift attacker deals its damage first</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.25; Manual p.25 · Tests: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Key: attr.swift.kill-first</sub>

<a id="r802.4c"></a>**802.4c** A half-column with both Swift and Sluggish deals combat damage twice: once in the Swift sub-step and once in the Sluggish sub-step, with normal damage from other units in between (see rule 608.2c). See rules 608.2c, 802.5.

> *Example (non-normative): A Swift and Sluggish column strikes in the Swift and Sluggish sub-steps, not in normal.* <sub>test: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.substeps.swift-and-sluggish</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.43; Manual p.43 · Designer: RAQ 1363298910528864318#2 · Rulings: R157 §5 · Tests: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts, 297-damage-substeps-are-steps.test.ts, 134-column-and-substep.test.ts · Key: attr.swift.with-sluggish</sub>

<a id="r802.4d"></a>**802.4d** A half-column that has dealt combat damage in the Swift sub-step does not deal combat damage in the normal sub-step, even if it has since lost Swift (see rule 608.2e). See rule 608.2e.

> *Example (non-normative): A column that dealt Swift damage deals no normal damage, even once its Swift unit is gone.* <sub>test: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Swift: a column that dealt Swift damage deals no normal damage</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1363298910528864318#1 · Rulings: R320 · Tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts · Key: attr.swift.struck</sub>

<a id="r802.4e"></a>**802.4e** When a Swift half-column strikes and another half-column will strike in a later sub-step, the combat damage step is split: the abilities that triggered on the Swift damage go on the stack and resolve, with priority, before normal damage is dealt (see rules 608.3b and 608.9c). See rules 608.3b, 608.9c.

> *Example (non-normative): A Swift-only battle gets one boundary between the Swift and normal sub-steps, not two.* <sub>test: 297-damage-substeps-are-steps.test.ts::R295 §3b an EMPTY sub-step opens no window</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Flowstone Arcanite's counters from the Swift step land at the boundary, in time to save an ally.* <sub>test: 21-fixes.test.ts::Flowstone Arcanite (R295): the Swift-step counters land at the boundary</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1540678747953569832#2; RAQ 1363298910528864318#0 · Rulings: R295 · Replaces: R31 (superseded: it resolved sub-step triggers at once as special actions, with no priority); R261 (narrowed by R295: its hold of combat-damage triggers until after combat now applies only to an unsplit step) · Our glossary (not a source): Swift · Tests: 297-damage-substeps-are-steps.test.ts, 21-fixes.test.ts · Key: attr.swift.split</sub>

<a id="r802.4f"></a>**802.4f** In an exchange involving a Pure card, Swift does not apply, so the exchange strikes in the normal sub-step (see rule 608.2d). See rules 608.2d, 802.25.

> *Example (non-normative): Dune Drifter (2/1, Swift) is blocked by Just a Unit (2/3, Pure): both strike in the normal sub-step, and the Drifter dies.* <sub>test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.swift.pure — a Swift attacker blocked by a Pure unit strikes in the normal sub-step, together with the blocker</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: card: Just a Unit · Rulings: R61 · Tests: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Key: attr.swift.pure</sub>

<a id="r802.5"></a>**802.5. Sluggish.** Sluggish is a combat attribute. Its reminder text reads "Sluggish units deal combat damage last."

> *Example (non-normative): Ambling Mountaintop (4/5 Sluggish) is blocked by a 5/4; the blocker strikes first and kills it, and is never struck.* <sub>test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.sluggish — Rime Wraith prints the reminder, and a Sluggish 4/5 dies to a 5/4 blocker before it can strike</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: card: Rime Wraith · Our glossary (not a source): Sluggish · Tests: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Key: attr.sluggish</sub>

<a id="r802.5a"></a>**802.5a** A half-column that has Sluggish deals its combat damage in the Sluggish sub-step, after the Swift and normal sub-steps (see rule 608.2a). See rules 608.2, 608.2a.

> *Example (non-normative): Swift strikes first, then normal, then Sluggish.* <sub>test: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.substeps — Swift, then normal, then Sluggish</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Rime Wraith · Tests: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Key: attr.sluggish.schedule</sub>

<a id="r802.5b"></a>**802.5b** Because a Sluggish half-column strikes in a later sub-step of a split step, abilities that triggered on the earlier sub-steps' damage resolve before it deals its damage (see rule 608.9c). See rules 608.9c, 608.3b.

> *Example (non-normative): Adversary of the Deep (Sluggish) grows from the 6 life lost in the normal sub-step before it strikes, and deals 8.* <sub>test: 297-damage-substeps-are-steps.test.ts::R295 §1 the report</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1540678747953569832#2 · Rulings: R295 · Tests: 297-damage-substeps-are-steps.test.ts · Key: attr.sluggish.after-triggers</sub>

<a id="r802.5c"></a>**802.5c** A half-column that has dealt combat damage in the normal sub-step does not deal combat damage in the Sluggish sub-step, even if it has since gained Sluggish. A half-column that dealt damage in the Swift sub-step and has gained Sluggish deals damage again in the Sluggish sub-step (see rule 608.2e). See rule 608.2e.

> *Example (non-normative): A plain column strikes in the normal sub-step, then gains Sluggish; it does not strike again.* <sub>test: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Swift: a column that dealt normal damage deals no Sluggish damage</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A Swift column strikes in the Swift sub-step, gains Sluggish, and strikes again in the Sluggish sub-step.* <sub>test: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Swift: a Swift column that gains Sluggish strikes again</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1363298910528864318#3; RAQ 1363298910528864318#2 · Rulings: R320 · Tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts · Key: attr.sluggish.after-normal</sub>

<a id="r802.5d"></a>**802.5d** In an exchange involving a Pure card, Sluggish does not apply, so the exchange strikes in the normal sub-step (see rule 608.2d). See rules 608.2d, 802.25.

> *Example (non-normative): Ambling Mountaintop (4/5, Sluggish) is blocked by Just a Unit (2/3, Pure): both strike in the normal sub-step.* <sub>test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.sluggish.pure — a Sluggish attacker blocked by a Pure unit strikes in the normal sub-step, together with the blocker</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: card: Just a Unit · Rulings: R61 · Tests: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Key: attr.sluggish.pure</sub>

<a id="r802.6"></a>**802.6. Tough.** Tough is an attribute. A Tough unit's defense is doubled.

> *Example (non-normative): Rampart Guardian (0/4, Tough) is a 0/8, and a unit it is augmented onto has its defense doubled.* <sub>test: 08-cards2.test.ts::Rampart Guardian: Tough doubles defense (layer 4), own and via augment</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.42; Manual p.35 · Our glossary (not a source): Tough · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts · Key: attr.tough</sub>

<a id="r802.6a"></a>**802.6a** Tough doubles a unit's defense after counters and other +X/+X changes to it have been applied. See rules 206.4, 802.1.

> *Example (non-normative): Rampart Guardian (0/4, Tough) with a +1/+1 counter is a 1/10.* <sub>test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Tough: a 0/4 Tough unit with a +1/+1 counter is a 1/10</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Rampart Guardian (0/4, Tough) with a -1/-1 counter has defense 6: the counter makes it 3, then Tough doubles it.* <sub>test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.tough.after-counters — a 0/4 Tough unit with a -1/-1 counter has defense 6: the counter applies first, then the doubling</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.42; Manual p.42 · Designer: RAQ 1362832912579559664#0 · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Key: attr.tough.after-counters</sub>

<a id="r802.6b"></a>**802.6b** Tough does not change a unit's power.

> *Example (non-normative): A 0/4 Tough unit with a -1/-1 counter is a -1/6: its power is not doubled. (illustrative)* <sub>test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.tough.power — a 0/4 Tough unit with a -1/-1 counter is a -1/6: its power is not doubled</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.42 · Rulings: R226 · Tests: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Key: attr.tough.power</sub>

<a id="r802.6c"></a>**802.6c** If an effect doubles a Tough unit's defense, the defense the unit then has is double what it had. The doubling is a stat change applied before Tough doubles the result, so if the unit later loses Tough, that change stays and is no longer doubled. See rules 709, 712.

> *Example (non-normative): Burgeon on a 1/10 Tough unit makes it 1/20 (a +0/+5 under Tough); if Monke then takes its Tough, it is a 1/10.* <sub>test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Tough: Burgeon on that 1/10 makes it 1/20, and losing Tough to Monke leaves 1/10</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Burgeon doubling Rampart Guardian's defense shows the doubled number, not four times its defense.* <sub>test: 140-layers-and-riders.test.ts::Burgeon doubling a {Tough} unit's defense gives the printed number</sub>
