<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1362832912579559664#1 · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 140-layers-and-riders.test.ts · Key: attr.tough.doubling</sub>

<a id="r802.7"></a>**802.7. Balanced.** Balanced is an attribute. Its reminder text reads "The power and defense of balanced units are equal to the greater of the two."

> *Example (non-normative): Child of Aether (2/0, Balanced) is a 2/2.* <sub>test: 08-cards2.test.ts::Child of Aether: Balanced (power & defense = max) keeps a 2/0 alive</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Brough · Our glossary (not a source): Balanced · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts · Key: attr.balanced</sub>

<a id="r802.7a"></a>**802.7a** Balanced compares the unit's power and defense after its counters and other stat changes, and after any attribute that applied before it, have been applied. See rules 206.4, 802.1.

> *Example (non-normative): A 1/4 with Tough and Balanced: Tough makes it 1/8, then Balanced makes it 8/8. (illustrative)*

> *Example (non-normative): A 1/3 with two +1/+1 counters and Balanced is a 5/5.* <sub>test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.balanced.after-changes — Balanced reads after counters: a 1/3 with two +1/+1 counters and Balanced is a 5/5</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.42 · Rulings: R93 · Tests: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Key: attr.balanced.after-changes</sub>

<a id="r802.8"></a>**802.8. Inverted.** Inverted is an attribute. Its reminder text reads "Invert the stat changes of inverted units. For example, -1/+2 would become +1/-2."

> *Example (non-normative): Its Dark Bubb's reminder, verbatim: a -1/+2 change on an Inverted unit becomes +1/-2.* <sub>test: 43-dark-c.test.ts::Its Dark Bubb: the printed reminder text, verbatim</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Its Dark Bubb; Manual p.25 · Our glossary (not a source): Inverted · Tests: 43-dark-c.test.ts · Key: attr.inverted</sub>

<a id="r802.8a"></a>**802.8a** Inverted inverts the net change to a unit's stats. An Inverted unit's power is its base power minus the net change to its power, and its defense is its base defense minus the net change to its defense. It is worked out on the total change, not on each change separately. See rule 206.4.

> *Example (non-normative): Malformed Monstrosity (10/9) with its -7/-7, in a column with Reality Bender, is a 17/16.* <sub>test: 79-round17-layers.test.ts::R93 layer 5: the owner's Malformed Monstrosity</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): With several sources changing its stats, an Inverted unit inverts the net change, not each source.* <sub>test: 43-dark-c.test.ts::Its Dark Bubb: MULTI-SOURCE — layer 5 negates the NET change, not each source on its own</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: Manual p.25; Manual p.25 · Rulings: R93, R93 · Tests: 79-round17-layers.test.ts, 43-dark-c.test.ts · Key: attr.inverted.net</sub>

<a id="r802.8b"></a>**802.8b** The changes Inverted inverts include those that Tough and Balanced make. Inverting Tough removes the defense Tough added; it does not halve the defense. See rules 802.6, 802.7.

> *Example (non-normative): A 1/4 with Tough and Balanced is an 8/8; with Inverted too it is a -6/0.* <sub>test: 79-round17-layers.test.ts::R93 layer 5: Caleb's worked example — a 1/4 Tough Balanced Inverted is a -6/0</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R93, R93 · Tests: 79-round17-layers.test.ts · Key: attr.inverted.attributes</sub>

<a id="r802.8c"></a>**802.8c** Setting a unit's base stats is not a stat change that Inverted inverts: the new base stats are what Inverted inverts from. See rule 206.5.

> *Example (non-normative): A unit made base 3/3 by Aberrant Statweaver, with no other changes, is a 3/3 whether or not it is Inverted.* <sub>test: 79-round17-layers.test.ts::R93 layer 5: a base REWRITE is the thing inverted FROM, never inverted itself</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R93 · Tests: 79-round17-layers.test.ts · Key: attr.inverted.base</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U19-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.8d"></a>**802.8d** If a unit has both Tough and Inverted, its defense is minus twice the net change to its defense from base. So it has 0 or less defense, and dies, unless that net change is a reduction, in which case its defense is twice the reduction. See rules 802.6, 713.

> *Example (non-normative): A 1/4 with Tough and Inverted is a 1/0, in either grant order, and dies.* <sub>test: 79-round17-layers.test.ts::R226: the TWO-attribute case, in either grant order</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A 1/3 with one -1/-1 counter, Tough and Inverted survives as a 2/2.* <sub>test: 79-round17-layers.test.ts::R226: the special case his wording misses</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Inverted on the front unit of a column and Tough on the back unit: both units have both attributes, and both die.* <sub>test: 79-round17-layers.test.ts::R226: the column wipe</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 3 tests run · Rulings: R226, R226 · Tests: 79-round17-layers.test.ts · Key: attr.inverted.tough</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U19-9 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.9"></a>**802.9. Unaware.** Unaware is an attribute. An Unaware card, and every card interacting with it, ignores all stat changes: each is read at the stats printed on it.

> *Example (non-normative): Bubb with two +1/+1 counters is still a 5/6. A 3/3 with four +1/+1 counters attacks into Bubb: it deals 3 and dies to 5.* <sub>test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.unaware — Unaware Bubb ignores its own counters, and a pumped 3/3 blocked by Bubb is read at its printed 3/3</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1402292180499955884#3 · Rulings: R106 · Replaces: R10 (superseded by R106; R10 counted targeting as interacting) · Our glossary (not a source): Unaware · Tests: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Key: attr.unaware</sub>

<a id="r802.9a"></a>**802.9a** An Unaware card's own power and defense are always the ones printed on it, for every purpose, including whether it has died. Counters, temporary changes, continuous effects and the other stat attributes do not change them. See rules 206.4, 713.

> *Example (non-normative): A +1/+1 counter on Bubb (5/6, Unaware) leaves it a 5/6.* <sub>test: 92-unaware.test.ts::a +1/+1 counter on Bubb leaves it a 5/6</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Bubb survives 100 -1/-1 counters.* <sub>test: 92-unaware.test.ts::Bubb would also survive 100 -1/-1 counters just fine</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Tough donated onto Bubb does nothing.* <sub>test: 92-unaware.test.ts::{Tough} donated onto Bubb does nothing</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A Robot token given Unaware by Bubb ignores its own +1/+1 counters and dies a 0/0.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Reconfigure vs Despawn: moving Bubb and its Growing Plague onto a Robot</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 4 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1353847640214999170#1 · Rulings: R106, R106 · Tests: 92-unaware.test.ts, 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 79-round17-layers.test.ts · Key: attr.unaware.self</sub>

<a id="r802.9b"></a>**802.9b** Setting a unit's base stats is a stat change too. An Unaware unit whose base stats an effect sets is still read at its printed stats. See rule 206.5.

> *Example (non-normative): Aberrant Statweaver ("your units are base 3/3") leaves Bubb a 5/6.* <sub>test: 92-unaware.test.ts::a base REWRITE is ignored too</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R157 §14, R106 · Tests: 92-unaware.test.ts · Key: attr.unaware.base</sub>

<a id="r802.9c"></a>**802.9c** When an Unaware card deals damage or is dealt damage, every card in that interaction is read at its printed stats: the other card as well as the Unaware one. See rule 112.6.

> *Example (non-normative): Unaware Bubb squishing a Robot 10 kills it: the Robot is read as its printed 0/0.* <sub>test: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Squish: Unaware Bubb squishing a Robot 10 kills it</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A Robot 10 squishing Unaware Bubb deals its printed defense, 0.* <sub>test: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Squish: a Robot 10 squishing Unaware Bubb</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Two units fight: Bubb reads a Robot 7 as a 0/0 and kills it.* <sub>test: 92-unaware.test.ts::two units FIGHT: Bubb reads a Robot 7 as a 0/0</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 3 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1402292180499955884#3; RAQ 1402292180499955884#4 · Rulings: R106 · Tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts, 92-unaware.test.ts · Key: attr.unaware.interaction</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U19-10 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.9d"></a>**802.9d** In combat, the interaction is the exchange between an attacking half-column and the half-column blocking it. If a unit on either side is Unaware, every unit on both sides deals and is dealt combat damage at its printed stats. See rules 608.5c, 608.6e.

> *Example (non-normative): Bubb blocks a 3/3 pumped to 5/5 and takes 3, the attacker's printed power.* <sub>test: 92-unaware.test.ts::Bubb blocks a pumped 3/3 and takes the attacker's PRINTED 3</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): An Unaware attacker reads its exchange the same way an Unaware blocker does.* <sub>test: 92-unaware.test.ts::an Unaware ATTACKER collapses the exchange the same way a blocker does</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): In an Unaware exchange the front blocker is priced at its printed defense, less marked damage.* <sub>test: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.assignment.lethal-defined — in an Unaware exchange</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 3 tests run · Rulings: R106, R106 · Tests: 92-unaware.test.ts, 05-rulings.test.ts, 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Key: attr.unaware.combat</sub>

<a id="r802.9e"></a>**802.9e** A unit dealt damage in such an interaction is destroyed if the damage is lethal for its printed defense, even if the stats it has outside the interaction would let it survive. See rule 713.

> *Example (non-normative): Bubb blocking a Robot token kills it, however many +1/+1 counters it has.* <sub>test: 92-unaware.test.ts::"Bubb blocking a Robot token would kill it</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Haboob's 1 damage kills any unit with a printed defense of 1.* <sub>test: 92-unaware.test.ts::"Haboob kills anything that has 1 defense printed at the card level"</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R106, R106 · Tests: 92-unaware.test.ts · Key: attr.unaware.death</sub>

<a id="r802.9f"></a>**802.9f** Outside such an interaction, an Unaware card does not change the stats of the other cards.

> *Example (non-normative): A Robot token that nobody Unaware is fighting is its full size.* <sub>test: 92-unaware.test.ts::NEGATIVE CONTROL: a Robot token that nobody Unaware is fighting is its full size</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R106 · Tests: 92-unaware.test.ts · Key: attr.unaware.outside</sub>

<a id="r802.9g"></a>**802.9g** A spell can be Unaware. A spell has no stats of its own, so its Unaware only makes the cards it deals damage to be read at their printed stats. See rule 302.

> *Example (non-normative): Haboob (an Unaware spell) deals 1 damage to each unit and kills every unit with a printed defense of 1.* <sub>test: 92-unaware.test.ts::"Haboob kills anything that has 1 defense printed at the card level"</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R106, R106 · Tests: 92-unaware.test.ts · Key: attr.unaware.spells</sub>

<a id="r802.9h"></a>**802.9h** Unaware does not stop a card being targeted. An effect can put counters or other stat changes on an Unaware card; they stay on it but do not change its stats while it is Unaware. See rule 110.

> *Example (non-normative): Poison with X = 6, targeting Bubb (a 5/6, Unaware), puts six -1/-1 counters on it; Bubb is still a 5/6. (illustrative)* <sub>test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.unaware.targets — Poison X=6 may target Unaware Bubb: six -1/-1 counters go on, and Bubb stays a 5/6</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A Robot 10 may Squish Unaware Bubb, targeting Bubb. The Robot, interacting with Unaware Bubb, is read at its printed 0/0, so it deals 0 and Bubb takes no harm.* <sub>test: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Squish: a Robot 10 squishing Unaware Bubb deals its printed defense, 0</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 3, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1402292180499955884#4 · Rulings: R281, R281 · Replaces: R10 (superseded by R106: it counted targeting as interacting); R206 (its Unaware row ("targeting is deliberately not implemented") amended by R281) · Tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts, 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Key: attr.unaware.targets</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U19-6 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.10"></a>**802.10. Powerful.** Powerful is a combat attribute. Its reminder text reads "Powerful sources deal double damage".

> *Example (non-normative): Chitin Shredder (1/2 Powerful) deals 3 effect damage as 6, and unblocked costs the defending player 2 life.* <sub>test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.powerful — Emberflame Enlightener prints the reminder, and a Powerful source deals double in combat and by effect</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: card: Emberflame Enlightener · Our glossary (not a source): Powerful · Tests: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Key: attr.powerful</sub>

<a id="r802.10a"></a>**802.10a** A Powerful half-column's combat damage is doubled once, as a whole, before it is divided among its recipients, whether they are units or a player. A unit without Powerful in a Powerful column has its damage doubled along with the rest (see rule 608.5b). See rule 608.5b.

> *Example (non-normative): Chitin Shredder (Powerful) deals double combat damage to a player.* <sub>test: 09-attrs.test.ts::Powerful: Chitin Shredder deals double combat damage to a player</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A vanilla unit in front of Chitin Shredder has its damage doubled too.* <sub>test: 09-attrs.test.ts::Powerful: column-shares</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1362838395298119912#2 · Rulings: R23 · Tests: 09-attrs.test.ts · Key: attr.powerful.combat</sub>

<a id="r802.10b"></a>**802.10b** If a modifier that adds to the damage also applies, the addition is made first and Powerful doubles the result (see rule 112.9). See rule 112.9.

> *Example (non-normative): A Powerful Bellowing Boulder's 1 damage with Conduit of Pain is (1+1)x2 = 4 to each unit.* <sub>test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Resonant: Conduit adds its 1 BEFORE Powerful doubles</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1362838395298119912#4 · Rulings: R316 · Replaces: R104 (applied Conduit of Pain after the doubling; replaced on this point by R316) · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts · Key: attr.powerful.additive</sub>

<a id="r802.10c"></a>**802.10c** Powerful also doubles damage its source deals through spells and abilities, to units and players alike. See rule 112.9.

> *Example (non-normative): Powerful doubles effect damage from a Powerful source.* <sub>test: 09-attrs.test.ts::Powerful: doubles effect damage from a Powerful source</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 3 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1362838395298119912#4; RAQ 1362838395298119912#3 · Rulings: R237 · Tests: 09-attrs.test.ts, 206-deadly-everywhere.test.ts · Key: attr.powerful.noncombat</sub>

<a id="r802.10d"></a>**802.10d** A spell can have Powerful. Damage a Powerful spell deals is doubled. See rule 302.

> *Example (non-normative): With Emberflame Enlightener in its region, a player's spell deals double damage.* <sub>test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::Emberflame Enlightener: your SPELLS gain {Powerful} too</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Emberflame Enlightener · Rulings: R94 · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts · Key: attr.powerful.spells</sub>

<a id="r802.10e"></a>**802.10e** When a spell makes a unit deal damage, as Squish, Fight and Battle do, the unit is the source: the unit's own Powerful, including Powerful it shares from its column, applies, and Powerful on the spell does not (see rule 112.6). See rule 112.6.

> *Example (non-normative): Squish makes a Powerful ally deal double its defense.* <sub>test: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Squish: the unit is the source</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A Powerful Squish does not double.* <sub>test: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Squish: a Powerful Squish does not double</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Squish on a 1/3 that shares Powerful from Chitin Shredder in its column deals 6.* <sub>test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.powerful.unit-source — Squish on a unit that shares Powerful from its column deals double</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1402292180499955884#0; RAQ 1402292180499955884#1 · Rulings: R318, R294 · Tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts, 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts, 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Key: attr.powerful.unit-source</sub>

<a id="r802.10f"></a>**802.10f** Powerful does not apply in an interaction with a Pure card (see rule 802.25). See rule 802.25.

> *Example (non-normative): A Pure source's own Powerful does not double its damage.* <sub>test: 290-pure-outside-combat.test.ts::§1 a Pure source: its own Powerful does not double</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Just a Unit · Rulings: R61 · Tests: 290-pure-outside-combat.test.ts · Key: attr.powerful.pure</sub>

<a id="r802.11"></a>**802.11. Vulnerable.** Vulnerable is an attribute. A Vulnerable unit is dealt double the damage that would be dealt to it.

> *Example (non-normative): Crumbling Ancient (Vulnerable) is dealt double the combat damage assigned to it.* <sub>test: 09-attrs.test.ts::Vulnerable: Crumbling Ancient marks double the combat damage it receives</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1372451771632320512#0 · Rulings: R23 · Our glossary (not a source): Vulnerable · Tests: 09-attrs.test.ts · Key: attr.vulnerable</sub>

<a id="r802.11a"></a>**802.11a** Because the damage is doubled when it is dealt, lethal damage for a Vulnerable unit, when assigning, is half its remaining defense, rounded up (see rule 608.6e). See rule 608.6e.

> *Example (non-normative): Arc Lightning (6 damage, Electric) on a Vulnerable 3/8: 4 of the 6 destroy it, and the other 2 may jump on.* <sub>test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Vulnerable: Arc Lightning on a Vulnerable 3/8</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A 10-power Piercing column blocked by a Vulnerable 3/7 assigns it 4 (half of 7, rounded up), and 6 go through.* <sub>test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.vulnerable.lethal — a Vulnerable 3/7 needs 4 (half of 7 rounded up), so a 10-power Piercing column sends 6 through</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A Vulnerable 3/8 with 2 damage marked needs 3, so a 10-power Piercing column sends 7 through.* <sub>test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.vulnerable.lethal — lethal is half the remaining defense: a Vulnerable 3/8 with 2 damage marked needs 3, so 7 of 10 pierce</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1372451771632320512#0 · Rulings: R120 (its lethal-floor arithmetic) · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Key: attr.vulnerable.lethal</sub>

<a id="r802.11b"></a>**802.11b** Damage assigned to a Vulnerable unit counts as that much of the source's damage; the unit is then dealt double that amount. Any damage the source keeps on a Vulnerable unit, including the rest of a column's damage, is doubled on that unit. See rules 608.6d, 608.7.

> *Example (non-normative): A Piercing attacker may put all 10 of its damage into a lone Vulnerable 3/8, which is dealt 20.* <sub>test: 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts::R319: a Piercing attacker may put all 10 into a lone Vulnerable 3/8</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1372451771632320512#4 · Rulings: R23 · Tests: 09-attrs.test.ts, 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts · Key: attr.vulnerable.receipt</sub>

<a id="r802.11c"></a>**802.11c** Piercing excess past a Vulnerable unit is measured in the source's damage before the doubling: only the source damage beyond what the unit needs is excess (see rule 802.16). See rule 802.16.

> *Example (non-normative): A 10-power Piercing column blocked by a Vulnerable 3/8 assigns 4 to it, and 6 goes to the player.* <sub>test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Vulnerable: a 10-power Piercing column into a Vulnerable 3/8 assigns 4</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1372451771632320512#3 · Rulings: R23 · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 09-attrs.test.ts, 82-attr-interactions.test.ts · Key: attr.vulnerable.piercing</sub>

<a id="r802.11d"></a>**802.11d** If a Powerful source deals damage to a Vulnerable unit, both apply: the source's damage is doubled, and the unit is dealt double that. See rule 112.9.

> *Example (non-normative): Powerful (source) and Vulnerable (receiver) both apply to one effect hit.* <sub>test: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts::Powerful (source) and Vulnerable (receiver) both apply to one effect hit</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R103 (its pricing order), R103 (its pricing order), R23 · Tests: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts · Key: attr.vulnerable.powerful</sub>

<a id="r802.11e"></a>**802.11e** A Pure Vulnerable unit, and a Vulnerable unit in an interaction with a Pure card, is not dealt double damage. See rule 802.25. *(Engine differs, see F-U19-3.)*

> *Example (non-normative): A Pure source hitting a Vulnerable unit deals only what it says.* <sub>test: 290-pure-outside-combat.test.ts::§2 a Pure recipient's own Vulnerable is off too</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Crumbling Ancient (Vulnerable) made Pure is dealt 2 by a 2-damage effect, not 4.* <sub>test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.vulnerable.pure — a Vulnerable unit that is itself Pure is dealt 2 by a 2-damage effect, not 4</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Just a Unit · Rulings: R61, R289 (its per-pairing switch) · Tests: 290-pure-outside-combat.test.ts, 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Key: attr.vulnerable.pure</sub>

<a id="r802.12"></a>**802.12. Feeble.** Feeble is an attribute. A Feeble unit can't block.

> *Example (non-normative): Spectrogenesis creates three Wisps (Feeble); none of them can block.* <sub>test: 08-cards2.test.ts::Spectrogenesis: three Wisps; Feeble means they cannot block</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): When a Feeble unit is refused as a blocker, the client names it.* <sub>test: 86-ui-block-refusal.test.ts::#77: {Feeble} — the unit that cannot block is the one that is named</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Bripp prints Feeble.* <sub>test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.feeble — Bripp prints Feeble, so the block-refusal guards that use it are not vacuous</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: card: Spectrogenesis · Rulings: R294 · Our glossary (not a source): Feeble · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts, 86-ui-block-refusal.test.ts, 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Key: attr.feeble</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U19-11 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.12a"></a>**802.12a** Whether a unit can block depends on its own Feeble only. A Feeble unit can't block even if it shares a column with units that are not Feeble, and Feeble that a unit would share from its column does not stop it blocking. See rules 802.1, 606.2.

> *Example (non-normative): The block check asks Feeble of the unit, not of its column.* <sub>test: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts::R294 §4 {Feeble} block legality is still the unit's own question</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R294, R294 · Tests: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts · Key: attr.feeble.own</sub>

<a id="r802.12b"></a>**802.12b** A Pure unit that is Feeble can block: Pure makes it ignore its own Feeble (see rule 802.25). See rule 802.25.

> *Example (non-normative): Just a Unit (Pure) granted Feeble can still be declared as a blocker.* <sub>test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.feeble.pure — a Pure unit granted Feeble is accepted as a blocker</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Just a Unit · Rulings: R61, R206 (its Feeble row) · Tests: 177-glossary-conformance.test.ts, 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Key: attr.feeble.pure</sub>

<a id="r802.12c"></a>**802.12c** A Feeble unit is not able to block, so an Alluring trigger that targets it cannot compel it to block (see rules 606.2e and 802.15). See rules 606.2e, 802.15.

> *Example (non-normative): A lured Feeble unit is not compelled to block the Alluring column.* <sub>test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::R84: a {Feeble} lured unit is not able, so it is not compelled</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R84 · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Key: attr.feeble.lured</sub>

<a id="r802.13"></a>**802.13. Evasive.** Evasive is an attribute. Its reminder text, printed under the type line, reads "Evasive units require two blockers." See rules 802.1, 606.2c.

> *Example (non-normative): Curio Drifter is Evasive.* <sub>test: 07-cards.test.ts::Curio Drifter: Evasive requires two blockers</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1460216519731577027#0 · Rulings: R84 · Our glossary (not a source): Evasive · Tests: 07-cards.test.ts · Key: attr.evasive</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U20-1 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.13a"></a>**802.13a** A column with Evasive cannot be blocked by a single unit. To block it, the defending player must place two units in front of it. See rules 606.2c, 602.

> *Example (non-normative): An Evasive Curio Drifter attacks. The defender may block it with two units placed in front of it, one behind the other, but not with one.* <sub>test: 07-cards.test.ts::Curio Drifter: Evasive requires two blockers</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1460216519731577027#0; RAQ 1460216519731577027#1 · Rulings: R84 · Tests: 07-cards.test.ts, 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts · Key: attr.evasive.two-blockers</sub>

<a id="r802.13b"></a>**802.13b** Evasive does not apply if either the Evasive column or the units blocking it include a Pure card. A single Pure unit can block an Evasive column on its own (see rule 802.25). See rule 802.25.

> *Example (non-normative): Just a Unit (Pure) blocks an Evasive column by itself.* <sub>test: 40-light-c.test.ts::Just a Unit: {Pure} blocks an Evasive column alone</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R61, R84 · Tests: 40-light-c.test.ts · Key: attr.evasive.pure</sub>

<a id="r802.14"></a>**802.14. Sneaky.** Sneaky is an attribute. Its reminder text, printed under the type line, reads "Sneaky units can't be blocked if attacking alone." See rules 802.1, 606.2c.

> *Example (non-normative): Whispering Mantid is Sneaky.* <sub>test: 08-cards2.test.ts::Whispering Mantid: Sneaky</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R20 · Our glossary (not a source): Sneaky · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts · Key: attr.sneaky</sub>

<a id="r802.14a"></a>**802.14a** An attacking column with Sneaky cannot be blocked if its unit is the only attacking unit in the attacking formation. See rule 606.

> *Example (non-normative): Whispering Mantid attacks alone and cannot be blocked. Attacking with another unit, it can be.* <sub>test: 08-cards2.test.ts::Whispering Mantid: Sneaky</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R20 · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts · Key: attr.sneaky.alone</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U20-2, D-U20-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.14b"></a>**802.14b** Spell tokens that go with an attack do not count as attacking units for Sneaky. A Sneaky unit attacking with only spell tokens beside it is attacking alone. See rule 604.2c.

> *Example (non-normative): Example (illustrative): A Sneaky unit attacks together with two Fireball spell tokens. It is still attacking alone and cannot be blocked.* <sub>test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.sneaky.spell-tokens — a Sneaky unit attacking with two riding Fireball spell tokens is still alone and cannot be blocked</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Rulings: R20 · Tests: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Key: attr.sneaky.spell-tokens</sub>

<a id="r802.14c"></a>**802.14c** Two Sneaky units attacking together are not alone. Both can be blocked.

> *Example (non-normative): Example (illustrative): Two Whispering Mantids attack in different columns. The defender may block either or both.* <sub>test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.sneaky.two-sneaky — two Whispering Mantids attacking in two columns are not alone, and both can be blocked</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Rulings: R20 · Tests: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Key: attr.sneaky.two-sneaky</sub>

<a id="r802.14d"></a>**802.14d** A side-block does not block a lone Sneaky attacker. The defending player may side-block beside it, and it stays unblocked (see rule 606.4e). See rule 606.4e.

> *Example (non-normative): A side-block beside a lone Sneaky attacker is allowed, and the Sneaky unit is still unblocked.* <sub>test: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts::cr:combat.blocks.side.blocks-nothing — a side-block beside a lone Sneaky attacker</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R321 · Tests: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts · Key: attr.sneaky.side-block</sub>

<a id="r802.14e"></a>**802.14e** A Pure unit ignores Sneaky, so it can block a lone Sneaky attacker (see rule 802.25). See rule 802.25.

> *Example (non-normative): Example (illustrative): A lone Sneaky unit attacks. The defender can block it with Just a Unit (Pure), and with no other unit.* <sub>test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.sneaky.pure — Just a Unit (Pure) can block a lone Sneaky attacker, and a plain unit cannot</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Rulings: R61 · Replaces: R76 (its 'able' sub-findings (a Pure blocker still sees through lone Sneaky) survive in R84; its Alluring rule was replaced by R84) · Tests: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Key: attr.sneaky.pure</sub>

<a id="r802.15"></a>**802.15. Alluring.** Alluring is an attribute. Its reminder text, printed under the type line, reads "When an alluring column attacks, target enemy can't attack and must block it this combat if able." See rules 802.1, 604.2e, 606.2e.

> *Example (non-normative): Tempest Wrangler is Alluring, and donates Alluring when applied as an augment.* <sub>test: 15-water-b.test.ts::Tempest Wrangler: {Alluring} 1/3</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R84 · Our glossary (not a source): Alluring · Tests: 15-water-b.test.ts · Key: attr.alluring</sub>

<a id="r802.15a"></a>**802.15a** When an attacking column with Alluring is declared, Alluring triggers. The trigger goes on the stack and targets one enemy unit, chosen by the attacking player from the enemy units in the battle region as the trigger is put on the stack. See rules 706, 110.

> *Example (non-normative): Two attacking columns, one Alluring, against one possible blocker: the Alluring trigger targets that blocker, which then must block the Alluring column.* <sub>test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::R84: the minimal form</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Rulings: R84, R84, R84 · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts, 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Key: attr.alluring.trigger</sub>

<a id="r802.15b"></a>**802.15b** Alluring does not stack. An attacking column with Alluring has one Alluring trigger, however many of its units have Alluring.

> *Example (non-normative): Two Alluring units attack in one column. Alluring triggers once.* <sub>test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::R84: {Alluring} does not stack</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R84, R84 · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Key: attr.alluring.one-per-column</sub>

<a id="r802.15c"></a>**802.15c** Each attacking column with Alluring has its own trigger. Two Alluring columns make two triggers, which may target the same unit or different units.

> *Example (non-normative): Two Alluring columns attack. Each triggers, and both triggers may target the same defending unit.* <sub>test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::R84: two Alluring COLUMNS are two triggers, and may name the same unit</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Two Alluring columns target two different units. Each of those units must block its column.* <sub>test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::R84: two Alluring columns naming DIFFERENT units compel both</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R84 · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Key: attr.alluring.per-column</sub>

<a id="r802.15d"></a>**802.15d** Alluring is shared by the units of its column, but the column's Alluring trigger comes from the unit that has Alluring itself, not from the units it is shared with. See rule 802.1.

> *Example (non-normative): Tempest Wrangler attacks in a column with a vanilla unit. The trigger is Tempest Wrangler's.* <sub>test: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts::R294 §4b {Alluring} still originates from the unit that prints it</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R294, R84 · Tests: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts · Key: attr.alluring.source</sub>

<a id="r802.15e"></a>**802.15e** When the Alluring trigger resolves, its target cannot attack: it cannot be declared as an attacker or sent to counterattack for the rest of the battle phase (see rule 604.2e). See rules 604.2e, 610.

> *Example (non-normative): A lured unit cannot be sent out to counterattack when blocks are declared.* <sub>test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::R84: a lured unit cannot be sent out to counterattack</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R84, R84 · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Key: attr.alluring.cannot-attack</sub>

<a id="r802.15f"></a>**802.15f** When the Alluring trigger resolves, its target must block the Alluring column in that battle round if it is able to. If the column is blocked at all, the target must be one of its blockers (see rule 606.2e). See rule 606.2e.

> *Example (non-normative): The defender has two units able to block and leaves the Alluring column unblocked by putting both on other columns. The declaration is refused: the lured unit must block the Alluring column.* <sub>test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::R84 UFAB</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1460216519731577027#2 · Rulings: R84, R84 · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Key: attr.alluring.must-block</sub>

<a id="r802.15g"></a>**802.15g** Whether the target is able to block the Alluring column depends only on that unit and that column. If the target could not block the column by itself (because the column is Evasive and needs two blockers, the target is Feeble, the column has Flying and the target does not, or the column is a lone Sneaky attacker), the defending player may leave the column unblocked, and the target may block another column. See rules 606.2b, 802.13.

> *Example (non-normative): A lone lured unit cannot block an Alluring and Evasive column by itself, so it need not block it, and it may block another column.* <sub>test: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Alluring: a lone lured unit cannot block an Evasive column</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1460216519731577027#0 · Rulings: R84, R84 · Tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts, 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Key: attr.alluring.able</sub>

<a id="r802.15h"></a>**802.15h** An Alluring and Evasive column can be blocked only by two units, one of which is the target. The defending player chooses between blocking it with the target and one other unit, and not blocking it at all; blocking it with two other units is not allowed. See rule 802.13.

> *Example (non-normative): The target is A and the defender also has B and C. A+B and A+C may block the column; B+C may not.* <sub>test: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Alluring: with three units, A+B or A+C may block the Evasive column, but never B+C</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): The defender has only A and B. They block the column with A+B, or leave it unblocked.* <sub>test: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Alluring: with two units, the lured one blocks the Evasive column with the other, or nobody blocks it</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1460216519731577027#1; RAQ 1460216519731577027#2 · Rulings: R84 · Tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts · Key: attr.alluring.evasive</sub>

<a id="r802.15i"></a>**802.15i** If, when the Alluring trigger would resolve, the unit with Alluring is no longer in an attacking column, or its column no longer has Alluring, the trigger does nothing.

> *Example (non-normative): The attacker's Alluring unit is killed while its trigger is on the stack. The trigger does nothing, and the targeted unit may attack and block freely.* <sub>test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::R84: killing the allurer while the trigger is ON the stack fizzles it</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R84, R84 · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Key: attr.alluring.allurer-gone</sub>

<a id="r802.15j"></a>**802.15j** Once the Alluring trigger has resolved, removing the unit with Alluring does not undo it: its target still cannot attack. If the Alluring column ceases to exist, the duty to block it ends with it.

> *Example (non-normative): After the trigger resolves, the Alluring attacker is killed in the attack window. The lured unit may block another column, but it still cannot be sent to counterattack.* <sub>test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::R84: killing the allurer AFTER it resolves frees the block but not the attack</sub>

<a id="r802.15k"></a>**802.15k** If two Alluring triggers have targeted the same unit, it cannot block both columns. Blocking either of those columns with it satisfies both triggers, and the other column may then be blocked by other units or left unblocked.

> *Example (non-normative): Example (illustrative): Two Alluring columns both target unit A. A blocks the first column. The second column may be blocked by B alone, or left unblocked.* <sub>test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.alluring.two-duties — one unit lured by two columns blocks one of them, and the other column may be blocked by another unit or left unblocked</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U20-4 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.15m"></a>**802.15m** An Alluring trigger from a lone Sneaky attacker compels no unit, because no unit is able to block that attacker (see rule 802.14), unless its target is Pure. See rule 802.14.

> *Example (non-normative): A lone Sneaky and Alluring unit attacks. The defender declares no blocks, and that is legal.* <sub>test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::R84: a lone {Sneaky} + {Alluring} attacker is not a stuck state</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R84, R84 · Replaces: R76 (first found the lone Sneaky + Alluring case; its Alluring rule was replaced by R84, which keeps this 'able' sub-finding) · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Key: attr.alluring.lone-sneaky</sub>

<a id="r802.15n"></a>**802.15n** An Alluring column that contains a Pure card does not trigger at all (see rule 802.25). See rule 802.25.

> *Example (non-normative): An Alluring column with Just a Unit in it attacks. No Alluring trigger is put on the stack.* <sub>test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::R84 + R61: an Alluring column that is itself {Pure} never even triggers</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R61, R84 · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Key: attr.alluring.pure-column</sub>

<a id="r802.15p"></a>**802.15p** A Pure unit ignores the attributes that would stop it blocking, so a Pure target is able to block any Alluring column: it must block even a Flying Alluring column, and it satisfies an Evasive Alluring column by itself. See rule 802.25.

> *Example (non-normative): A lured Pure unit must block a Flying Alluring column.* <sub>test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::R84 + R61: a {Pure} lured unit is able against a Flying Alluring column</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A lured Pure unit blocks an Evasive Alluring column alone.* <sub>test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::R84 + R61: a {Pure} lured unit discharges an EVASIVE Alluring column alone</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R61, R61 · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Key: attr.alluring.pure-target</sub>

<a id="r802.15q"></a>**802.15q** The Alluring trigger is a triggered ability. It can be negated while it is on the stack, and an effect that makes triggered abilities cost more to trigger (Crevice Lurker) applies to it: if that cost is not paid, the trigger does not happen. See rules 111.10f, 706.

> *Example (non-normative): Crevice Lurker is in play. The attacker declines to pay for the Alluring trigger, and nothing is lured.* <sub>test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ trigger-like attributes: Crevice Lurker taxes the Alluring trigger</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Containment Protocol negates a waiting Alluring trigger.* <sub>test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ trigger-like attributes: Containment Protocol negates a waiting Alluring trigger</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U15-1 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.16"></a>**802.16. Piercing.** Piercing is an attribute. Its reminder text reads "Excess damage from piercing sources is dealt to the recipient's controller." See rules 802.1, 608.

> *Example (non-normative): Protective Adaptations gives a unit +1/+1 and Piercing until regroup.* <sub>test: 14-water-a.test.ts::Protective Adaptations: the target also gains piercing until regroup</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Protective Adaptations; Rulebook 2023 p.11 · Replaces: R7 (Piercing half ('automatic, not elective') reversed by R319); R103 (its 'automatic, not elective' half reversed by R340); R319 (its closing note that noncombat Piercing is automatic reversed by R340) · Our glossary (not a source): Piercing · Tests: 14-water-a.test.ts · Key: attr.piercing</sub>

<a id="r802.16a"></a>**802.16a** Excess damage, for Piercing, is the damage a source deals to a unit beyond that unit's lethal damage. A unit's lethal damage is worked out after Powerful has doubled the source's damage; it is reduced for a Vulnerable unit, which is dealt double what reaches it; it is 1 if the source has Deadly; and damage already dealt to the unit counts towards it, including damage dealt to it earlier by the same effect (see rule 608.6e). See rules 608.6e, 802.3, 802.10, 802.11.

> *Example (non-normative): A Powerful Piercing source deals 3 to a 1/1. The 3 is doubled to 6; 1 is lethal; 5 is excess.* <sub>test: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts::Piercing + Powerful: the excess is what is left after the doubling</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A 10-power Piercing column is blocked by a Vulnerable 3/8. Lethal damage is 4, which is dealt as 8; the other 6 is excess.* <sub>test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Vulnerable: a 10-power Piercing column into a Vulnerable 3/8 assigns 4 and 6 goes to the player</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): One effect names the same unit twice with Piercing. The unit is given its lethal damage once, and the rest of both hits is excess.* <sub>test: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts::Piercing: a unit named twice in one batch is overkilled ONCE</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 3 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1372451771632320512#3 · Rulings: R103 (its order of operations), R103 (its order of operations), R103 (its order of operations), R103 (its order of operations), R23 · Tests: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts, 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 09-attrs.test.ts · Key: attr.piercing.excess</sub>

<a id="r802.16b"></a>**802.16b** A half-column with Piercing that deals combat damage to the units of the opposing half-column must assign lethal damage to each of those units, front to back. Any of its damage that is not assigned to a unit is dealt to the player who controls those units. See rules 608.6, 608.8.

> *Example (non-normative): A Piercing column with 10 power is blocked by a 1/2 in front of a 1/3. It must assign 2 to the front unit and 3 to the back unit; the other 5 may be dealt to the defending player.* <sub>test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Excessive: Piercing pays lethal to the front AND the back, and only the rest reaches the player</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1353888077625561108#4; RAQ 1353888077625561108#5 · Rulings: R114 (its designer line), R319 (its combat ruling) · Replaces: R7 ('Piercing is automatic, not elective' reversed by R319); R114 ('its leftover is returned to the caller and hits the face' amended by R319: only what no unit is given goes to the controller) · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Key: attr.piercing.combat</sub>

<a id="r802.16c"></a>**802.16c** Excess is elective. After each unit has been assigned its lethal damage, the dealing player may assign any part of the remaining damage to those units, including all of it, and only the damage no unit is assigned is dealt to the player. See rule 608.6c.

> *Example (non-normative): A 10-power Piercing attacker is blocked by a lone Vulnerable 3/8. The attacker may put all 10 into it (dealt as 20), and none reaches the player.* <sub>test: 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts::R319: a Piercing attacker may put all 10 into a lone Vulnerable 3/8</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A Piercing split may keep part of the excess on the back unit and send the rest to the player.* <sub>test: 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts::R319: a Piercing split may keep part of the excess on the back unit and send the rest</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1353888077625561108#5; RAQ 1372451771632320512#4 · Rulings: R319 (its combat ruling) · Replaces: R7 ('Piercing is automatic, not elective' reversed by R319); R21 ('a Deadly Piercing column sends everything past 1-per-blocker through' amended by R319: that is the default only) · Tests: 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts · Key: attr.piercing.elective</sub>

<a id="r802.16d"></a>**802.16d** An unblocked attacking half-column with Piercing deals its combat damage to the defending player, as any unblocked half-column does. See rule 608.4a.

> *Example (non-normative): An unblocked Piercing column hits the defending player.* <sub>test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Piercing: an unblocked Piercing column hits the player</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1365594171867664445#0 · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts · Key: attr.piercing.unblocked</sub>

<a id="r802.16e"></a>**802.16e** If an attacking half-column with Piercing is blocked but no blocking unit is left in front of it when it strikes, all of its damage is excess and is dealt to the defending player. A blocked half-column without Piercing deals no damage in that case (see rule 608.4c). See rules 608.4c, 606.3a.

> *Example (non-normative): A Piercing column's only blocker dies before damage. The column is still blocked, and its full power is dealt to the defending player.* <sub>test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Piercing: a Piercing column whose blocker died before damage puts its full power into the player</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): The same position without Piercing deals nothing to the player.* <sub>test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Piercing: a blocked NON-Piercing column whose blocker died deals nothing to the player</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1365594171867664445#1 · Rulings: R13 (its conclusion), R185 · Replaces: R13 (its reason ('piercing excess is automatic per R7') corrected by R319; its ⚠ resolved by the RAQ) · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 02-combat.test.ts · Key: attr.piercing.dead-block</sub>

<a id="r802.16f"></a>**802.16f** A blocking half-column with Piercing deals excess combat damage to the attacking player only if there is an attacking unit in front of it when it strikes. If no attacking unit is in front of it (its attackers are all gone, or it is a side-block), it deals no combat damage at all (see rules 608.4e and 608.4f). See rules 608.4e, 608.4f.

> *Example (non-normative): A Piercing blocking column with an attacker in front of it deals its excess to the attacking player.* <sub>test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Piercing: a defending Piercing column with an attacker in front of it carries its excess to the attacker</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A Piercing side-blocker deals no combat damage to the attacking player.* <sub>test: 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts::R321 a Piercing side-blocker deals no combat damage to the attacking player</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 3 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1365594171867664445#3 · Rulings: R72 (its attackers-gone half), R321 · Replaces: R72 (its no-side-block note replaced by R321) · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts, 64-formation-collapse.test.ts · Key: attr.piercing.defending</sub>

<a id="r802.16g"></a>**802.16g** If the Piercing source also has Deadly, lethal damage is 1 for each unit, so all damage beyond 1 for each unit may be excess. See rule 802.3.

> *Example (non-normative): A Deadly and Piercing column is blocked by two units. It assigns 1 to each, and the rest may go to the player.* <sub>test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Excessive: Deadly + Piercing over two blockers</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A 10-power Deadly and Piercing column is blocked by one unit: 1 kills it and the other 9 may pierce.* <sub>test: 134-column-and-substep.test.ts::R157 §11 — {Deadly} + {Piercing}: 1 kills the blocker and the other 9 pierce</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1353888077625561108#6 · Rulings: R103 (its order of operations) · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 134-column-and-substep.test.ts, 82-attr-interactions.test.ts · Key: attr.piercing.deadly</sub>

<a id="r802.16h"></a>**802.16h** Damage prevention on a unit does not change how much must be assigned to it before there is excess. Excess is worked out as though the unit were unprotected. See rules 608.6g, 708.

> *Example (non-normative): A Piercing column is blocked by a shielded 0/5 in front of a 5/6. It must assign 5 to the shielded unit and 6 to the unit behind; the rest may go to the player.* <sub>test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Excessive: with Piercing, 5 to the shielded Tomb</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A Piercing effect hits a shielded unit. The shield changes what is dealt to the unit, never what pierces.* <sub>test: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts::Piercing vs a damage-shielded unit</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1353888077625561108#10 · Rulings: R103 (its order of operations) · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 82-attr-interactions.test.ts · Key: attr.piercing.prevention</sub>

<a id="r802.16i"></a>**802.16i** Piercing excess is dealt as part of the same damage as the rest, at the same time. It is not a triggered ability, and no player can act between the damage dealt to the units and the excess dealt to the player.

> *Example (non-normative): A Piercing effect deals 5 to a 1/1. The unit's 1 and the 4 to its controller are dealt together, with nothing on the stack in between.* <sub>test: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts::Piercing: 5 effect damage to a 1/1 kills it and the other 4 hit its controller</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R103 (its not-a-trigger ruling), R340 · Our glossary (not a source): Piercing · Tests: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts · Key: attr.piercing.same-damage</sub>

<a id="r802.16j"></a>**802.16j** Piercing applies to noncombat damage too. A Piercing source that deals noncombat damage to a unit must deal that unit its lethal damage first. The dealing player may then keep any of the excess on that unit; the rest of the excess is dealt to that unit's controller. See rule 112.7.

> *Example (non-normative): Squish makes Bubb, in a column with Good Whale (Piercing), deal 6 to a 1/1. The dealing player may keep all 6 on the 1/1, or send up to 5 to its controller.* <sub>test: 405-raq-noncombat-piercing.test.ts::R340 Squish: Bubb with Good Whale's Piercing</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A non-Piercing source's overkill stays on the unit, and no question is asked.* <sub>test: 405-raq-noncombat-piercing.test.ts::R340 control: no Piercing, no question</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1402292180499955884#5 · Rulings: R340, R340, R340 · Replaces: R103 (its 'automatic, not elective' half reversed by R340); R319 (its closing note that noncombat Piercing is unchanged (automatic) reversed by R340) · Tests: 405-raq-noncombat-piercing.test.ts, 82-attr-interactions.test.ts · Key: attr.piercing.noncombat</sub>

<a id="r802.16k"></a>**802.16k** For noncombat damage, the dealing player is the controller of the source unit, even if another player controls the spell that made it deal damage (for Squish, Fight and Battle the unit is the source; see rule 112.6). If the source is not a unit in play (a spell, or a unit that has left play), the controller of the effect decides. See rule 112.6.

> *Example (non-normative): A Battle makes an opponent's Piercing unit fight. The opponent, who controls that unit, places its excess.* <sub>test: 405-raq-noncombat-piercing.test.ts::R340 Battle: the question belongs to the Piercing unit's controller, not the caster</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Rulings: R340, R340 · Tests: 405-raq-noncombat-piercing.test.ts, 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Key: attr.piercing.noncombat-chooser</sub>

<a id="r802.16m"></a>**802.16m** Each unit's excess is dealt to that unit's controller. If one effect deals Piercing damage to units controlled by different players, each player is dealt the excess from their own units.

> *Example (non-normative): A Piercing effect damages units on both sides. Each unit's excess goes to that unit's controller.* <sub>test: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts::Piercing in a BATCH: each unit's excess goes to THAT unit's controller</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Protective Adaptations · Tests: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts · Key: attr.piercing.recipients</sub>

<a id="r802.16n"></a>**802.16n** A unit in a column with a Piercing unit has Piercing while that column exists, for the noncombat damage it deals as well as for combat damage (see rule 802.1). See rule 802.1.

> *Example (non-normative): Bubb, in a column with Good Whale, squishes with Piercing: the excess reaches the player.* <sub>test: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Squish: Bubb in a column with Good Whale squishes with Piercing</sub>

<a id="r802.16p"></a>**802.16p** If Piercing combat damage that would be dealt to a player is dealt to a unit instead (as Oorblak's ability does), that unit is dealt its lethal damage and the rest is still Piercing excess. That excess is dealt to the player, and it is not redirected again (see rule 608.8c). See rule 608.8c. *(Engine differs, see F-U12-1.)*

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U20-15 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.17a"></a>**802.17a** When an Electric source deals a unit more than its lethal damage, the excess may be dealt to a unit adjacent to that unit instead. The unit the excess jumps to is dealt the lethal damage it needs, and any excess beyond that may jump again, to a unit adjacent to it. See rules 603.2, 802.16.

> *Example (non-normative): Arc Lightning (6, Electric) hits a Vulnerable 3/8. 4 kill it (dealt as 8), and the other 2 may jump to an adjacent unit.* <sub>test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Vulnerable: Arc Lightning on a Vulnerable 3/8</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Envoy of Lightning · Designer: RAQ 1372451771632320512#0 · Replaces: R4 ('excess passes immediately along the chosen path' amended by R317: each hop is optional, and a dead end is dealt) · Tests: 05-rulings.test.ts, 387-raq-combat.test.ts · Key: attr.electric.jump</sub>

<a id="r802.17b"></a>**802.17b** The excess never jumps to a unit it has already been dealt to in that chain.

> *Example (non-normative): Electric excess follows a non-overlapping path chosen by the controller.* <sub>test: 05-rulings.test.ts::R4: electric excess follows a controller-chosen non-overlapping path, atomically</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R206 (its Electric row) · Our glossary (not a source): Electric · Tests: 05-rulings.test.ts · Key: attr.electric.no-revisit</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U20-7 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.17c"></a>**802.17c** The Electric source's controller chooses where the excess goes at each jump. *(Engine differs, see F-U20-1.)*

> *Example (non-normative): Arc Lightning's caster, who controls the source, is asked where the excess goes.* <sub>test: 05-rulings.test.ts::R4: electric excess follows a controller-chosen non-overlapping path, atomically</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R4 (its who-chooses and atomic halves), R317 (its optional-hop and dead-end ruling) · Tests: 05-rulings.test.ts · Key: attr.electric.chooser</sub>

<a id="r802.17d"></a>**802.17d** Each jump is optional. At any jump, the source's controller may instead keep all the remaining excess on the unit it has reached; it is then all dealt to that unit and goes no further. This is so even when there is only one unit to jump to.

> *Example (non-normative): Arc Lightning hits a Vulnerable 3/8 with a unit beside it. Its controller keeps all 6 on the 3/8 (dealt as 12), and nothing jumps.* <sub>test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Vulnerable: Electric "can be"</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1372451771632320512#1 · Rulings: R317 (its optional-hop and dead-end ruling) · Replaces: R4 ('excess passes immediately along the chosen path' amended by R317) · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts · Key: attr.electric.optional</sub>

<a id="r802.17e"></a>**802.17e** Excess that has no unit to jump to is dealt to the last unit it reached; it is not lost. If the source also has Piercing, that excess is Piercing excess instead (see rule 802.16). See rule 802.16q.

> *Example (non-normative): Arc Lightning hits a lone Vulnerable 3/8 with nothing beside it. All 6 land on it, dealt as 12.* <sub>test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Vulnerable: Electric damage with nowhere to jump is still dealt</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U20-8 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.17f"></a>**802.17f** Adjacency for Electric is adjacency in a formation (see rule 603.2). A unit that is not in a formation has no adjacent unit, so Electric excess dealt to it has nowhere to jump. See rule 603.2b.

> *Example (non-normative): Example (illustrative): During the deployment phase no unit is in a formation, so an Electric spell's excess stays on the unit it hit.* <sub>test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.electric.adjacency — outside a battle no unit is adjacent, so Electric excess stays on the unit it hit and nothing is asked</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 0 tests run · Printed: card: Envoy of Lightning · Engine: engine.ts:adjacentInFormation · Tests: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Key: attr.electric.adjacency</sub>

<a id="r802.17g"></a>**802.17g** The whole Electric chain is part of one damage event. No formation changes happen while the excess is distributed. See rule 112.8.

> *Example (non-normative): An Electric chain of three units is dealt in one damage event; the units it kills die together afterwards.* <sub>test: 05-rulings.test.ts::R4: electric excess follows a controller-chosen non-overlapping path, atomically</sub>

<a id="r802.17h"></a>**802.17h** Lethal damage along the chain is worked out as it is for Piercing (see rule 802.16): a Vulnerable unit needs only half, and damage already dealt to it by the same effect counts. See rule 802.16a.

<a id="r802.17i"></a>**802.17i** Envoy of Lightning makes "your spell effects with a single target" Electric. A spell effect has a single target if it was cast with exactly one target.

<a id="r802.18"></a>**802.18. Poisonous.** Poisonous is an attribute. Its reminder text reads "Poisonous sources damage units in the form of -1/-1 counters." See rule 802.1.

> *Example (non-normative): Noxious Sporefiend is Poisonous.* <sub>test: 09-attrs.test.ts::Poisonous: Noxious Sporefiend deals combat damage as permanent -1/-1 counters</sub>

<a id="r802.18a"></a>**802.18a** Damage a Poisonous source deals to a unit is put on that unit as that many -1/-1 counters instead of being marked on it. See rule 112.5.

> *Example (non-normative): Noxious Sporefiend deals 2 combat damage to a unit; the unit gets two -1/-1 counters and no marked damage.* <sub>test: 09-attrs.test.ts::Poisonous: Noxious Sporefiend deals combat damage as permanent -1/-1 counters</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Poisonous effect damage becomes -1/-1 counters, and can kill.* <sub>test: 09-attrs.test.ts::Poisonous: effect damage becomes -1/-1 counters and can kill</sub>

<a id="r802.18b"></a>**802.18b** Poisonous damage is damage dealt. Abilities that trigger when a unit is dealt damage trigger on it (see rule 112.10). See rule 112.10.

> *Example (non-normative): Noxious Sporefiend deals 2 to Awoken Tomb, which gets two -1/-1 counters and makes its 2/2.* <sub>test: 206-deadly-everywhere.test.ts::R237: an un-prevented {Poisonous} hit fires "whenever I am dealt damage"</sub>

<a id="r802.19"></a>**802.19. Resonant.** Resonant is an attribute. Its reminder text, printed under the type line, reads "Whenever a resonant source deals damage to a unit, it deals that much damage to that unit's controller." See rule 802.1.

> *Example (non-normative): Resonant Form's combat damage to a unit also hits that unit's controller.* <sub>test: 09-attrs.test.ts::Resonant: Resonant Form combat damage to a unit also hits its controller</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1362838395298119912#1 · Rulings: R315 (its trigger ruling) · Our glossary (not a source): Resonant · Tests: 09-attrs.test.ts · Key: attr.resonant</sub>

<a id="r802.19a"></a>**802.19a** Resonant is a triggered ability of the Resonant source. When the source deals damage to a unit, the trigger goes on the stack, and when it resolves the source deals that much damage to that unit's controller. See rule 706.

> *Example (non-normative): The Resonant trigger from combat damage waits on the stack after combat, as its source's trigger, and can be negated.* <sub>test: 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts::R315: the Resonant rider waits on the stack after combat</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A Resonant effect deals 1 to a unit; the trigger then deals 1 to its controller as damage from the source.* <sub>test: 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts::R315: effect damage riders too</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1362838395298119912#2 · Rulings: R315 (its trigger ruling) · Tests: 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts · Key: attr.resonant.trigger</sub>

<a id="r802.19b"></a>**802.19b** The damage Resonant deals to the controller is not combat damage, even when the damage that triggered it was (see rule 608.8b). See rules 608.8b, 112.7.

> *Example (non-normative): Oorblak, which takes combat damage that would be dealt to its controller, does not take Resonant's extra damage; the player does.* <sub>test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Resonant: the extra damage is not combat damage</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1362838395298119912#0 · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts · Key: attr.resonant.not-combat</sub>

<a id="r802.19c"></a>**802.19c** "That much damage" is the damage the unit was dealt: after Vulnerable doubled it and after any prevention. If all of the damage to the unit is prevented, Resonant does not trigger. See rules 802.11, 112.11.

> *Example (non-normative): Example (illustrative): A Resonant source deals 2 to a Vulnerable unit, which is dealt 4. The Resonant trigger deals 4 to that unit's controller.* <sub>test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.resonant.amount — a Resonant source dealing 2 to a Vulnerable unit, which is dealt 4, makes a Resonant trigger that deals 4 to its controller</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Rulings: R315 (its trigger ruling), R315 (its trigger ruling) · Tests: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Key: attr.resonant.amount</sub>

<a id="r802.19d"></a>**802.19d** Resonant's damage is damage from the Resonant source, so everything that changes that source's damage applies to it: an allied Conduit of Pain adds 1 to it, and Powerful doubles it, even though the damage that triggered it was already doubled. See rules 802.10, 112.9.

> *Example (non-normative): A Powerful Resonant 2/4 deals 4 combat damage to a unit, and then 8 to that unit's controller.* <sub>test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Resonant: a Powerful Resonant 2/4 deals 4 combat damage</sub>

<a id="r802.19e"></a>**802.19e** When both apply to Resonant's damage, an added amount (Conduit of Pain's 1) is added before Powerful doubles (see rule 112.9). See rule 112.9.

<a id="r802.20"></a>**802.20. Thieving.** Thieving is an attribute. Its reminder text, printed under the type line, reads "Whenever a thieving source deals combat damage to an opponent, draw a card." See rule 802.1.

Its controller draws a card.* <sub>test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.thieving.piercing — a Thieving and Piercing column blocked by a 1/1 deals 3 of excess to the defending player, and its controller draws a card</sub>

<a id="r802.21"></a>**802.21. Reaping.** Reaping is an attribute. Its reminder text, printed under the type line, reads "When a reaping source kills one or more units, draw a card. It loses reaping until regroup." See rule 802.1.

> *Example (non-normative): Flame of History is a Reaping spell: "I deal 1 damage to any target."* <sub>test: 07-cards.test.ts::Flame of History: Reaping</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R283 · Replaces: R184 (its premise that Reaping prints no reminder, and its per-body payout, corrected by R283) · Our glossary (not a source): Reaping · Tests: 07-cards.test.ts · Key: attr.reaping</sub>

<a id="r802.21a"></a>**802.21a** When a Reaping source kills one or more units, its controller draws one card, however many units it killed.

> *Example (non-normative): Flame of History kills a unit and its controller draws a card.* <sub>test: 07-cards.test.ts::Flame of History: Reaping</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Seismomancy kills a unit by damage and draws exactly once.* <sub>test: 156-reaping-and-formation.test.ts::Seismomancy: a kill by DAMAGE still pays {Reaping} exactly once</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R283 · Replaces: R184 (its per-body payout amended by R283: one draw per kill) · Tests: 07-cards.test.ts, 18-earth-c.test.ts, 263-reaping-counts-the-kill.test.ts · Key: attr.reaping.draw</sub>

<a id="r802.21b"></a>**802.21b** A unit counts as killed by a Reaping source however the source killed it: by damage, by -1/-1 counters, by changing its stats, or by destroying it outright.

> *Example (non-normative): Invasive Reassignment swaps a 0/4 into a 4/0, which dies. Reaping draws a card.* <sub>test: 156-reaping-and-formation.test.ts::Invasive Reassignment: a kill by a STAT SWAP pays {Reaping}</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Noxious Demise kills a 1/1 with a -1/-1 counter. Reaping draws a card.* <sub>test: 156-reaping-and-formation.test.ts::Noxious Demise: a kill by a -1/-1 COUNTER pays {Reaping}</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Invasive Reassignment kills nobody, and nothing is drawn.* <sub>test: 156-reaping-and-formation.test.ts::Invasive Reassignment: a swap that kills NOBODY draws nothing</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 3 tests run · Rulings: R184 (its kill-rider half), R21 (its Deadly half) · Tests: 156-reaping-and-formation.test.ts · Key: attr.reaping.any-kill</sub>

<a id="r802.21c"></a>**802.21c** After a Reaping source's kill has drawn a card, the source loses Reaping until regroup. *(Engine differs, see F-U20-4.)*

> *Example (non-normative): Example (illustrative): If a unit had Reaping and killed a blocker in the first battle round, it would draw a card and then have no Reaping in the second round.*

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Rulings: R283 · Key: attr.reaping.loses</sub>
