<a id="r802.22"></a>**802.22. Blessed.** Blessed is an attribute. Its reminder text reads "Damage dealt by a blessed source causes its controller to gain that much life." See rule 802.1.

> *Example (non-normative): Godray deals 3 damage to any target, and Blessed gains its controller 3.* <sub>test: 40-light-c.test.ts::Godray: 3 damage to any target</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Blessed Thing; card: Godray · Our glossary (not a source): Blessed · Tests: 40-light-c.test.ts · Key: attr.blessed</sub>

<a id="r802.22a"></a>**802.22a** When a Blessed source deals damage, its controller gains that much life. This applies to combat and noncombat damage, and to damage dealt to units and to players.

> *Example (non-normative): A Blessed column's combat damage to a player gains its controller that much life.* <sub>test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::R48 {Blessed}: combat damage to a player gains too</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A Blessed column's combat damage to a unit gains its controller that much life as well.* <sub>test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::R48 {Blessed}: combat damage to a UNIT gains as well</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A Blessed effect's damage gains its controller exactly that much life.* <sub>test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::R48 {Blessed}: effect damage gains its controller exactly that much life</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 3 tests run · Printed: card: Blessed Thing · Tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts, 44-hybrids-ld-a.test.ts · Key: attr.blessed.gain</sub>

<a id="r802.22b"></a>**802.22b** The life is gained at the same time as the damage is dealt. It is not a triggered ability and does not use the stack, and it is gained before it is checked whether any player has reached 0 life.

> *Example (non-normative): A player at low life is dealt lethal damage by an opponent at the same moment their own Blessed source deals damage. They gain the life first, and survive if it is enough.* <sub>test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::R48 {Blessed}: the gain lands BEFORE the lethal check</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R48, R48 · Tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts · Key: attr.blessed.simultaneous</sub>

<a id="r802.22c"></a>**802.22c** A Blessed source cannot kill its own controller with its own damage: damage it deals to its own controller is matched by the life that player gains at the same time.

> *Example (non-normative): Godray aimed at a player damages them and heals its controller on the same check.* <sub>test: 40-light-c.test.ts::Godray: aimed at a player it damages AND heals on the same check</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R48 · Tests: 40-light-c.test.ts, 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Key: attr.blessed.own-damage</sub>

<a id="r802.22d"></a>**802.22d** Blessed applies only to damage dealt. A kill without damage, and damage that is prevented, gain no life. See rule 112.11.

> *Example (non-normative): Noxious Demise carrying a Blessed Thing virus kills a unit with a -1/-1 counter. No life is gained.* <sub>test: 156-reaping-and-formation.test.ts::{Blessed} does not fire on a non-damage kill</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R98 (its prevention ruling) · Tests: 156-reaping-and-formation.test.ts · Key: attr.blessed.damage-only</sub>

<a id="r802.22e"></a>**802.22e** A unit in a column with a Blessed unit has Blessed while that column exists, so damage its abilities deal gains its controller life too (see rule 802.1). See rule 802.1.

> *Example (non-normative): A unit attacking in a column with Flzzz (Blessed) uses an ability to deal 1 damage. Its controller gains 1 life.* <sub>test: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts::R294 §1 the report</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R294 · Tests: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts · Key: attr.blessed.column</sub>

<a id="r802.22f"></a>**802.22f** Blessed does not apply in an interaction involving a Pure card (see rule 802.25). See rule 802.25.

> *Example (non-normative): A Pure Blessed source deals damage, and its controller gains nothing.* <sub>test: 290-pure-outside-combat.test.ts::§4 a Pure {Blessed} source gains nothing</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Just a Unit · Rulings: R61 · Tests: 290-pure-outside-combat.test.ts · Key: attr.blessed.pure</sub>

<a id="r802.23"></a>**802.23. Afflicting.** Afflicting is an attribute. Its reminder text reads "When an afflicting source kills one or more units, those units' controllers gain a rot." See rules 802.1, 112.13.

> *Example (non-normative): Umbral Decay is an Afflicting spell that puts two -1/-1 counters on target unit.* <sub>test: 42-dark-b.test.ts::Umbral Decay: two -1/-1 counters</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Umbral Decay · Our glossary (not a source): Afflicting · Tests: 42-dark-b.test.ts · Key: attr.afflicting</sub>

<a id="r802.23a"></a>**802.23a** When an Afflicting source kills one or more units, each player who controlled one of those units gains one rot.

> *Example (non-normative): Umbral Decay kills a unit with its counters. That unit's controller gains a rot.* <sub>test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::R48 {Afflicting}: a -1/-1 COUNTER kill gives the dead unit's controller a rot</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Umbral Decay's target survives, shrunk. Nobody gains a rot.* <sub>test: 42-dark-b.test.ts::Umbral Decay: a survivor just shrinks, and nobody gains a rot</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: card: Umbral Decay · Tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts, 42-dark-b.test.ts · Key: attr.afflicting.rot</sub>

<a id="r802.23b"></a>**802.23b** A player gains one rot for each kill, however many of their units the source killed at once.

> *Example (non-normative): An Afflicting source kills two units of one player at once. That player gains one rot.* <sub>test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::R48 {Afflicting}: ONE rot per controller per kill event</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R48 · Tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts · Key: attr.afflicting.one-rot</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U20-12 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.23c"></a>**802.23c** A unit counts as killed by an Afflicting source however the source killed it: by damage, by -1/-1 counters, by changing its stats, or by destroying it outright.

> *Example (non-normative): A -1/-1 counter kill by an Afflicting source gives a rot.* <sub>test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::R48 {Afflicting}: a -1/-1 COUNTER kill gives the dead unit's controller a rot</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Umbral Decay's counter kill gives a rot and draws nothing.* <sub>test: 156-reaping-and-formation.test.ts::Umbral Decay: an {Afflicting} counter-kill rots and draws NOTHING</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R48, R184 (its kill-rider half) · Tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts, 156-reaping-and-formation.test.ts · Key: attr.afflicting.any-kill</sub>

<a id="r802.23d"></a>**802.23d** Afflicting applies to kills by combat damage as well. An Afflicting column that kills units in combat gives their controllers rot.

> *Example (non-normative): An Afflicting column kills a blocker in combat. The blocker's controller gains a rot.* <sub>test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::R48 {Afflicting}: a plain COMBAT kill counts too</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Printed: card: Umbral Decay · Rulings: R48 (its Afflicting half) · Tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts, 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Key: attr.afflicting.combat</sub>

<a id="r802.23e"></a>**802.23e** Afflicting does not apply in an interaction involving a Pure card (see rule 802.25). See rule 802.25.

> *Example (non-normative): Example (illustrative): An Afflicting column kills Just a Unit (Pure) in combat. Its controller gains no rot.* <sub>test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.afflicting.pure — an Afflicting column that kills Just a Unit gives its controller no rot</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: card: Just a Unit · Rulings: R61 · Tests: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Key: attr.afflicting.pure</sub>

<a id="r802.24"></a>**802.24. Lethal.** Lethal is an attribute. Its reminder text reads "Any combat damage from a lethal unit will kill a player." See rule 802.1.

> *Example (non-normative): Gublin is Lethal.* <sub>test: 44-hybrids-ld-a.test.ts::Gublin: {Lethal}</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Gublin · Our glossary (not a source): Lethal · Tests: 44-hybrids-ld-a.test.ts · Key: attr.lethal</sub>

<a id="r802.24a"></a>**802.24a** If a column with Lethal deals any combat damage to a player, however little, that player is killed (see rule 104). See rule 104.1.

> *Example (non-normative): Gublin (1/4) attacks unblocked and deals 1 combat damage to the defending player, who is killed.* <sub>test: 44-hybrids-ld-a.test.ts::Gublin: {Lethal}</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Any combat damage from a Lethal unit kills the player.* <sub>test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::R48 {Lethal}: any combat damage from a lethal unit kills the player</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: card: Gublin · Tests: 44-hybrids-ld-a.test.ts, 37-attrs-wight.test.ts · Key: attr.lethal.kills</sub>

<a id="r802.24b"></a>**802.24b** Lethal applies only to combat damage dealt to a player. It does not change noncombat damage, or damage dealt to units.

> *Example (non-normative): Example (illustrative): A Lethal unit blocked by a 2/2 kills it as any unit would; Lethal does nothing to the blocker.* <sub>test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.lethal.combat-only — a Lethal unit blocked by a 2/2 kills it as any unit would, and the defending player is untouched</sub>

<a id="r802.25"></a>**802.25. Pure.** Pure is an attribute. Its reminder text reads "Pure cards and cards they are interacting with ignore all other attributes." See rule 802.1.

> *Example (non-normative): Just a Unit is Pure.* <sub>test: 40-light-c.test.ts::Just a Unit: the exchange is attribute-blind in BOTH directions</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Just a Unit · Our glossary (not a source): Pure · Tests: 40-light-c.test.ts · Key: attr.pure</sub>

<a id="r802.25a"></a>**802.25a** A Pure card ignores its own other attributes too. See rule 802.12.

> *Example (non-normative): An Alluring column that is itself Pure ignores its own Alluring and never triggers.* <sub>test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::R84 + R61: an Alluring column that is itself {Pure} never even triggers</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Example (illustrative): A Pure unit that is also Feeble can block.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Just a Unit · Rulings: R61 · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Key: attr.pure.own</sub>

<a id="r802.25b"></a>**802.25b** In combat, an interaction is one attacking half-column and the blocking half-column paired with it. If either contains a Pure card, the attributes of both are ignored for that exchange. See rule 608.4.

> *Example (non-normative): A Pure unit blocks a column; the exchange is attribute-blind in both directions.* <sub>test: 40-light-c.test.ts::Just a Unit: the exchange is attribute-blind in BOTH directions</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Just a Unit · Rulings: R61, R61 · Tests: 40-light-c.test.ts · Key: attr.pure.combat-interaction</sub>

<a id="r802.25c"></a>**802.25c** In a combat exchange involving a Pure card, neither side has Piercing, Deadly, Powerful, Poisonous, Resonant, Blessed, Afflicting or Thieving, and a Vulnerable unit in it is not dealt double. Neither side has Swift or Sluggish, so both strike in the normal sub-step (see rule 608.2d). See rules 608.2d, 608.6e.

> *Example (non-normative): Just a Unit switches off a Deadly attacker's Deadly.* <sub>test: 40-light-c.test.ts::Just a Unit: {Pure} switches off Deadly</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A printed Swift column blocked by a Pure unit strikes in the normal sub-step.* <sub>test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::R117 threads {Pure}</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R61, R61, R61 · Tests: 40-light-c.test.ts, 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Key: attr.pure.combat-damage</sub>

<a id="r802.25d"></a>**802.25d** When blocks are declared, a Pure card in either the attacking column or the units blocking it switches off Flying, Evasive and the lone Sneaky attacker's protection for that column, and a Pure unit's own Feeble does not stop it blocking. See rules 802.2, 802.12, 802.13, 802.14.

> *Example (non-normative): Just a Unit can block a Flying column, and only it can among the defender's units.* <sub>test: 40-light-c.test.ts::Just a Unit: {Pure} blocks a Flying column, and only it can</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Just a Unit blocks an Evasive column alone.* <sub>test: 40-light-c.test.ts::Just a Unit: {Pure} blocks an Evasive column alone</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R61, R61, R61 · Tests: 40-light-c.test.ts · Key: attr.pure.blocking</sub>

<a id="r802.25e"></a>**802.25e** Pure does not change stats. A Pure unit is destroyed by damage equal to its defense, and Tough, Balanced and Inverted still apply in an interaction involving a Pure card. See rules 802.6, 802.7, 802.8.

> *Example (non-normative): Example (illustrative): A Tough 0/4 (defense 8) blocks a column containing Just a Unit. It still has 8 defense in that exchange.* <sub>test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.pure.stat-attributes — a Tough 0/4 still has 8 defense blocking a 5-power Just a Unit, and survives</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Rulings: R61, R289 (its per-pairing ruling) · Our glossary (not a source): Pure · Tests: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Key: attr.pure.stat-attributes</sub>

<a id="r802.25f"></a>**802.25f** In combat, Unaware still applies in an exchange involving a Pure card: if an Unaware card is in the exchange, every unit in it is read at its printed stats. See rule 802.9.

Both sides of the exchange still use their printed stats.* <sub>test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.pure.unaware-combat — Bubb (Unaware) blocking a buffed Just a Unit: both sides are read at printed stats</sub>

<a id="r802.25g"></a>**802.25g** Outside combat, an interaction is one effect and one recipient of its damage. Pure applies to each such pairing separately.

> *Example (non-normative): One batch damages two recipients; only the pairing with the Pure unit is attribute-blind.* <sub>test: 290-pure-outside-combat.test.ts::§3 one batch, two recipients</sub>

<a id="r802.25k"></a>**802.25k** During a battle, a unit in a column with a Pure unit has Pure for noncombat damage too, as a source and as a recipient (see rule 802.1). See rule 802.1.

> *Example (non-normative): Example (illustrative): A unit stands in a column with Just a Unit. A Powerful spell deals 1 damage to it: it is dealt 1, not 2.* <sub>test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.pure.column — a unit attacking in a column with Just a Unit is dealt 1, not 2, by a Powerful effect dealing 1</sub>

<a id="r802.26"></a>**802.26. Modular.** Modular is an attribute. Its reminder text reads "You can apply mods to a modular card from your hand and/or bin as it is played. You still pay their costs." See rule 720.

> *Example (non-normative): Spellbind is a Modular spell.* <sub>test: 43-dark-c.test.ts::Spellbind: {Modular} carrier</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Spellbind · Our glossary (not a source): Modular · Tests: 43-dark-c.test.ts · Key: attr.modular</sub>

<a id="r802.26a"></a>**802.26a** As a Modular card is played, its controller may apply mods to it from their hand and from their bin, paying each mod's cost. The mods go onto the stack with the card (see rule 702.3b). See rule 702.3b.

> *Example (non-normative): Mods are applied to a Modular spell as it is cast, paid for, and ride on the stack with it.* <sub>test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::{Modular}: mods are applied at cast time</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): The caster may decline to apply any mod.* <sub>test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::{Modular}: the caster may decline</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 4 tests run · Printed: card: Spellbind · Tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts, 91-modular.test.ts, 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Key: attr.modular.when</sub>

<a id="r802.26b"></a>**802.26b** Any card in the player's hand or bin whose cost they can pay may be applied to a Modular card, including a card that will do nothing as a mod there. No other condition restricts what may be applied.

> *Example (non-normative): The menu offers every card the player can pay for: a graft, a Virus, a non-Virus augment, and a card that can do nothing.* <sub>test: 91-modular.test.ts::R105: the {Modular} menu offers every card you can pay for</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A card in the bin is offered beside the hand, and one the player cannot pay for is not.* <sub>test: 91-modular.test.ts::R105: a card in the BIN is offered beside the hand</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R105, R105, R105 · Tests: 91-modular.test.ts · Key: attr.modular.anything</sub>

<a id="r802.26c"></a>**802.26c** Applying a mod to a Modular card is not playing that mod (see rule 701.2). See rule 701.2.

> *Example (non-normative): The mod is charged as the Modular spell is cast, and applying it is not playing it.* <sub>test: 91-modular.test.ts::R105: "you still pay their costs"</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1537748882501668934#0 · Rulings: R37 · Tests: 91-modular.test.ts · Key: attr.modular.not-played</sub>

<a id="r802.26d"></a>**802.26d** A graft mod applied to a Modular spell adds its graft effect to the spell as an extra part, and the spell and its grafted effects resolve as one. See rule 722.

> *Example (non-normative): A graft mod contributes its [Switch] effect as an extra part of Spellbind.* <sub>test: 91-modular.test.ts::R105: a GRAFT mod still contributes its [Switch] effect as an extra part</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.33 · Rulings: R105 · Tests: 91-modular.test.ts · Key: attr.modular.graft</sub>

<a id="r802.26e"></a>**802.26e** A mod whose type line grants attributes as an augment gives those attributes to the Modular spell's effect. See rule 721.

> *Example (non-normative): A Powerful mod applied to Spellbind carrying Twin Flame turns its 2 damage into 4.* <sub>test: 91-modular.test.ts::R105: a type-line [Augment] mod really donates</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R105 · Tests: 91-modular.test.ts · Key: attr.modular.attributes</sub>

<a id="r802.26f"></a>**802.26f** An augment mod's text-box ability does nothing on a Modular spell: a spell cannot gain static or triggered abilities that way.

> *Example (non-normative): An [Augment]-text mod applied to Spellbind is accepted and does nothing.* <sub>test: 91-modular.test.ts::R105: an [Augment]-TEXT mod is accepted and does nothing</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R105 · Tests: 91-modular.test.ts · Key: attr.modular.text-augment</sub>

<a id="r802.26g"></a>**802.26g** A Modular card with a mod applied is modded, so it is Unstable: when it leaves the stack, whether it resolved, failed to resolve or was negated, it and its mods are erased instead of going to a bin. An unmodded Modular card goes to the bin as usual. See rules 803, 405.

> *Example (non-normative): A graft card in the bin is applied to Spellbind, resolves with it, and is erased, so it cannot be applied this way again.* <sub>test: 91-modular.test.ts::R105: the flashback line</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A negated modded Spellbind is erased too.* <sub>test: 91-modular.test.ts::R105: a NEGATED modded Spellbind is erased too</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): An unmodded Modular spell is binned like any other spell.* <sub>test: 91-modular.test.ts::R105: an UNMODDED {Modular} spell is not Unstable</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 3 tests run · Printed: Manual p.35 · Rulings: R105, R105 · Tests: 91-modular.test.ts · Key: attr.modular.unstable</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U20-14 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.26h"></a>**802.26h** Modular is not shared with the other units of a column. See rule 802.1. *(Engine differs, see F-U20-3.)*

> *Example (non-normative): Example (illustrative): If a unit printed Modular, the other units in its column would not gain Modular.*

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Rulings: R294 · Tests: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts · Key: attr.modular.not-shared</sub>

<a id="r803"></a>
### 803. Other Keyword Abilities

<a id="r803.1"></a>**803.1.** Some keywords are not combat attributes. Burst and Unstable are printed in purple text and are called non-combat attributes: they describe a card, and generally have nothing to do with combat. The other keywords in this section (Haste, Battle, [once], Ambush and Prophecy) are timing marks, limits and ways to play a card. See rules 802, 720, 204.5.

> *Example (non-normative): A modded Chitin Shredder attacks in a column with a vanilla unit: the vanilla unit shares its Powerful, but it does not become Unstable.* <sub>test: 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts::cr:keywords.abilities.non-combat — Burst and Unstable are not combat attributes: a column shares Powerful but not Unstable</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.25; Manual p.25 · Tests: 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.non-combat</sub>

<a id="r803.1a"></a>**803.1a** Non-combat attributes are not shared in formation. A unit with Burst or Unstable does not give it to the other units in its column. See rules 712.8e, 802.1.

> *Example (non-normative): A modded unit is Unstable; a unit in the same column is not, and when it dies it goes to the bin.* <sub>test: 125-active-zone.test.ts::R145: Unstable is NOT shared in formation</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A modded unit does not make its column-mate Unstable.* <sub>test: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts::R294 §5b a modded (therefore Unstable) unit does not make its column-mate Unstable</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: Manual p.25 · Rulings: R145, R294 · Tests: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts, 125-active-zone.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.non-combat.not-shared</sub>

<a id="r803.2"></a>**803.2.** Haste is a timing keyword. A card with Haste can be played during the haste step as well as during deployment. See rules 207.3, 504.

> *Example (non-normative): Tidal Menace, a {Haste} 7/2, can be played in the haste step.* <sub>test: 15-water-b.test.ts::Tidal Menace: {Haste} 7/2</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Tidal Menace, a {Haste} unit, is also offered and played during deployment.* <sub>test: 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts::cr:keywords.abilities.haste — a Haste card is also offered and playable during deployment, not only in the haste step</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.13; Manual p.13; Manual p.13 · Rulings: R206 (its Haste row) · Tests: 15-water-b.test.ts, 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.haste</sub>

<a id="r803.2a"></a>**803.2a** Printed text that names the "mana step" means the haste step. See rule 504.1.

> *Example (non-normative): Dispatch Courier lets its controller play a unit in the haste step as if it had Haste.* <sub>test: 26-metal-a.test.ts::Dispatch Courier: "play a unit during the mana step as if it had [Haste]"</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.3; card: Dispatch Courier · Rulings: R97, R97 · Tests: 26-metal-a.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.haste.mana-step</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U05-1 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r803.2b"></a>**803.2b** An effect can let a card without Haste be played in the haste step "as if it had [Haste]", as Dispatch Courier does. This changes only when the card may be played. See rules 504.7, 803.3a.

> *Example (non-normative): With a Dispatch Courier in play, a deploy-timing unit is offered and accepted in the haste step, and the Courier's once-each-turn budget is charged.* <sub>test: 26-metal-a.test.ts::Dispatch Courier: "play a unit during the mana step as if it had [Haste]"</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Without a Dispatch Courier, a deploy-timing unit is not offered in the haste step.* <sub>test: 26-metal-a.test.ts::Dispatch Courier: no Courier, no OFFER</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 2 tests run · Printed: card: Dispatch Courier · Rulings: R97 · Tests: 26-metal-a.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.haste.grants</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U05-4 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r803.3"></a>**803.3.** Battle is a timing keyword. A card with Battle can be played only while its player is in battle with another player. It cannot be played during deployment. See rules 207.4, 505.

> *Example (non-normative): A fulfilled prophecy on a {Battle} card does not let it be played at deployment: its Battle timing still applies.* <sub>test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::R42: normal TIMING still applies</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.13; Manual p.13; Manual p.13; Rulebook 2023 p.3; Rulebook 2023 p.3 · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.battle</sub>

<a id="r803.3a"></a>**803.3a** Gaining Haste does not let a Battle card be played outside battle. A Battle unit or Battle spell unit that an effect lets be played "as if it had [Haste]" still cannot be played in the haste step. See rules 207.4a, 504.2a.

> *Example (non-normative): Dispatch Courier's grant does not let a {Battle} unit be played in the haste step.* <sub>test: 26-metal-a.test.ts::Dispatch Courier: a {Battle} unit stays a battle card even with the grant</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Nor does it let a {Battle} spell unit be played there.* <sub>test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Dispatch Courier: a Battle spell unit is not playable in the haste step either</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1464899726796390433#0; RAQ 1465292396664193171#0; RAQ 1465292396664193171#1 · Tests: 26-metal-a.test.ts, 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.battle.haste</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U05-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r803.3b"></a>**803.3b** A [Battle] icon printed in front of one ability or play mode, rather than as the card's timing, governs that line only. An activated ability marked [Battle] can be activated only during battle; an Ambush marked [Battle] can be played during battle even if the card itself has no Battle timing (803.6b). See rules 207.8, 203.5.

> *Example (non-normative): Grox's [Battle] ability cannot be activated outside battle.* <sub>test: 43-dark-c.test.ts::Grox: R49 — the printed [Battle] marker is enforced at ACTIVATION</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.40; card: Grox · Rulings: R49 (its ability-timing marker paragraph), R49 (its ability-timing marker paragraph) · Tests: 43-dark-c.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.battle.per-line</sub>

<a id="r803.4"></a>**803.4.** [once] is a keyword that limits an ability: an ability marked [once] can be activated or triggered only once per turn, tracked for each card. Its rules are in 109.9. See rule 109.9.

> *Example (non-normative): Unstable Apparition's [once] trigger fires once in a turn and again the next turn.* <sub>test: 33-trigger-fixes.test.ts::Unstable Apparition: [once] resets each turn</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R113, R9 · Tests: 33-trigger-fixes.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.once</sub>

<a id="r803.5"></a>**803.5.** Burst is a non-combat attribute printed on spell tokens. When a player casts a spell token with Burst, they cast every spell token of the same name that they control in that region at the same time. It is all or nothing. See rules 304.11g, 702.7b.

> *Example (non-normative): Casting one Fireball in the battle region casts every Fireball its controller has there.* <sub>test: 03-stack.test.ts::Fireball goes to the stack in battle, Burst casts them all at once</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.15; Manual p.15; Manual p.15; Rulebook 2023 p.4; Rulebook 2023 p.4; card: Fireball · Rulings: R16 (its name-grouping half, as amended by R81), R309 · Replaces: R16 (its fixed entity-id stacking order replaced by R309); R81 (its entity-id order sentence replaced by R309) · Tests: 03-stack.test.ts, 69-damage-batch.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.burst</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U21-4 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r803.5a"></a>**803.5a** Spell tokens with different names are separate Burst groups. A player with a Poison and a Fireball may cast one, let it resolve, and then cast the other. See rule 304.11g.

> *Example (non-normative): Casting a Fireball casts the other Fireballs and leaves a Poison alone.* <sub>test: 69-damage-batch.test.ts::R81: Burst casts all your tokens OF THAT NAME, and leaves the others alone</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R81 (its name-grouping half), R81 (its name-grouping half) · Tests: 69-damage-batch.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.burst.by-name</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U21-10 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r803.5b"></a>**803.5b** Spell tokens cast together by Burst are still individual spells. They are played at the same time. See rule 304.11g.

> *Example (non-normative): Two Fireballs cast together go on the stack as two items, each with its own target.* <sub>test: 358-burst-order.test.ts::R309: the caster picks each Fireball in RESOLVE order and aims it</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.15; Manual p.15; Rulebook 2023 p.4 · Tests: 358-burst-order.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.burst.individual</sub>

<a id="r803.5c"></a>**803.5c** Each spell token in a Burst group chooses its own targets. The tokens do not have to share a target. See rule 110.

> *Example (non-normative): Each Fireball is aimed as it is picked.* <sub>test: 358-burst-order.test.ts::R309: the caster picks each Fireball in RESOLVE order and aims it</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R81 (its name-grouping half), R16 (its name-grouping half, as amended by R81) · Tests: 358-burst-order.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.burst.targets</sub>

<a id="r803.5d"></a>**803.5d** A Burst group goes on the stack all at once. Its caster chooses the order one token at a time, in the order the tokens will resolve, and aims each as it is chosen; the token chosen first resolves first. The other players receive priority only when the whole group is on the stack. A lone token is not ordered. See rule 703.4b.

> *Example (non-normative): The Fireball picked first ends on top of the stack.* <sub>test: 358-burst-order.test.ts::R309: the caster picks each Fireball in RESOLVE order and aims it</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A single Fireball is cast without an ordering question.* <sub>test: 358-burst-order.test.ts::R309: a lone token is not asked to be ordered</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 2 tests run · Rulings: R309, R309, R309 · Replaces: R16 (its fixed entity-id stacking order replaced by R309); R81 (its entity-id order sentence replaced by R309) · Tests: 358-burst-order.test.ts, 358-burst-order-ui.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.burst.order</sub>

<a id="r803.6"></a>**803.6.** Ambush is a keyword that lets a unit card be played during battle with the effect "Recall target ally, put me into their position in play." See rule 203.1.

> *Example (non-normative): Mirage Walker's Ambush recalls an ally and takes its formation slot.* <sub>test: 14-water-a.test.ts::Mirage Walker: ambush [4bb] recalls an ally and takes its formation slot (R22)</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Good Whale; Manual p.40; Manual p.40 · Tests: 14-water-a.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.ambush</sub>

<a id="r803.6a"></a>**803.6a** An Ambush is paid for with the cost printed beside the keyword, not the card's own cost: that mana is spent and its affinity pips are required. See rules 203.2, 203.3.

> *Example (non-normative): Lurking Slimebeast's Ambush [3b] costs 3 mana and needs one water pip.* <sub>test: 14-water-a.test.ts::Lurking Slimebeast: [Battle] Ambush [3b] = 3 mana at one water pip (R22)</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): With four fire mana and no water pip, Lurking Slimebeast cannot be played as an Ambush [3b]; with one water and three fire it can, and exactly 3 mana is spent.* <sub>test: 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts::cr:keywords.abilities.ambush.cost — 4 mana with no water pip cannot Ambush [3b]; 1 water and 3 fire can, and spend exactly 3</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Printed: card: Lurking Slimebeast · Rulings: R22, R301 (its Ambush comparison), R301 (its Ambush comparison) · Tests: 14-water-a.test.ts, 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.ambush.cost</sub>

<a id="r803.6b"></a>**803.6b** An Ambush can be played only during battle. The [Battle] icon in front of the keyword lets the card be played as an Ambush during battle even if the card itself has no Battle timing. See rules 203.5a, 803.3b.

> *Example (non-normative): Good Whale, a deploy-timing unit, is played as an Ambush in battle into the attacking column.* <sub>test: 08-cards2.test.ts::Good Whale: the parked Ambush mode works</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): During deployment, Lurking Slimebeast can be played normally, but its Ambush is neither offered nor accepted.* <sub>test: 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts::cr:keywords.abilities.ambush.timing — an Ambush is neither offered nor accepted during deployment</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.40; Manual p.40; Manual p.40 · Rulings: R22 (its during-battle half) · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts, 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.ambush.timing</sub>

<a id="r803.6c"></a>**803.6c** The target of an Ambush must be an ally of the Ambush's controller in the battle region. An opponent's unit is never a legal target, even through an effect that redirects targets. See rule 110.

> *Example (non-normative): The client offers an Ambush only against the same ally the Ambush effect would accept.* <sub>test: 243-ally-and-enemy-scope.test.ts::R265 §4a the ambush legality gate asks for the same ally the ambush effect will</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): An Ambush offers the attacking ally, but not an enemy unit in the battle region nor an ally that stayed home.* <sub>test: 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts::cr:keywords.abilities.ambush.target — the Ambush menu holds only allies of the caster in the battle region</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): An opposing Enigmatic Warder tries to redirect an Ambush onto itself: the Ambush still recalls its own ally, and the Warder stays in play.* <sub>test: 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts::cr:keywords.abilities.ambush.target — a redirect (Enigmatic Warder) cannot move an Ambush onto a unit of the opponent</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1355466429788328066#4 · Rulings: R22 · Tests: 243-ally-and-enemy-scope.test.ts, 49-playtest-round6.test.ts, 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.ambush.target</sub>

<a id="r803.6d"></a>**803.6d** An Ambush is a targeted effect on the stack. Players can respond to it before it resolves. See rule 703.

> *Example (non-normative): The ally can be removed in response, and then the Ambush fizzles.* <sub>test: 08-cards2.test.ts::Ambush fizzles when the target is removed</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.40 · Rulings: R22 · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.ambush.stack</sub>

<a id="r803.6e"></a>**803.6e** When an Ambush resolves, the target ally is recalled and the ambushing unit is put directly into the ally's position in play: into its formation slot if it was in formation, attacking or blocking, and otherwise into the battle region outside formation. See rules 801.7, 801.7a.

> *Example (non-normative): Orblish Horroth ambushing a blocker takes the blocker's formation slot.* <sub>test: 08-cards2.test.ts::Orblish Horroth: Ambush swaps into the blocker</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Mirrorback Ambusher recalls an ally and takes its position.* <sub>test: 19-hybrids.test.ts::Mirrorback Ambusher: Ambush [2be] recalls an ally and takes its position (R22)</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: Manual p.40 · Rulings: R22, R22 · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts, 14-water-a.test.ts, 19-hybrids.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.ambush.resolution</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U21-1 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r803.6f"></a>**803.6f** If, as the Ambush resolves, its target is gone or is no longer an ally of the Ambush's controller, the Ambush fizzles: nothing is recalled, and the ambushing card is put into the bin. Its controller loses both units. See rules 704.6e, 405.2b.

> *Example (non-normative): An Ambush whose target was removed fizzles and its ambusher goes to the bin.* <sub>test: 08-cards2.test.ts::Ambush fizzles when the target is removed</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): An Ambush whose ally changed sides before it resolved recalls nothing.* <sub>test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ valid targets: an Ambush whose ally changed sides before it resolves recalls nothing</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: Manual p.40; Manual p.40; Manual p.40 · Designer: RAQ 1355466429788328066#2 · Rulings: R22 · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts, 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.ambush.fizzle</sub>

<a id="r803.6g"></a>**803.6g** Ambushing a unit that is the target of another effect saves it. The other effect does not change targets to the ambushing unit; it fails to resolve (fizzles). See rule 704.

> *Example (non-normative): (illustrative) A Fireball aimed at a 2/2 is answered by an Ambush on that 2/2. The 2/2 returns to its hand; the Fireball fizzles and the ambusher is not hit.*

> *Example (non-normative): A Fireball is aimed at a unit, and its controller answers with an Ambush on that unit. The unit returns to its hand; the Fireball fizzles, and the ambusher takes no damage.* <sub>test: 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts::cr:keywords.abilities.ambush.saves — ambushing the target of a Fireball saves it; the Fireball fizzles and does not hit the ambusher</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.40; Manual p.40; Manual p.40; Manual p.40 · Tests: 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.ambush.saves</sub>

<a id="r803.6h"></a>**803.6h** An Ambush on the stack counts as a spell effect, so an effect that negates spell effects can negate it. A negated Ambush puts its ambushing card into the bin. See rules 700.1a, 704.4a.

> *Example (non-normative): Nothyr, which negates only nonspell effects, cannot target an Ambush on the stack: an Ambush is on the spell side.* <sub>test: 114-literal-dark.test.ts::Nothyr: an AMBUSH stays out of reach</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Void Mandible negates an Ambush on the stack: the ambusher never takes the slot and its target is not recalled.* <sub>test: 119-play-and-token-events.test.ts::Void Mandible: an AMBUSH is a card played too</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Dreadwave Devourer, which negates a target spell effect, can target an Ambush on the stack; negated, the ambusher goes to its bin and its target is not recalled.* <sub>test: 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts::cr:keywords.abilities.ambush.spell-effect — Dreadwave Devourer, which negates a target spell effect, negates an Ambush; the ambusher goes to the bin</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 2 tests run · Rulings: R22, R22 · Tests: 114-literal-dark.test.ts, 119-play-and-token-events.test.ts, 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.ambush.spell-effect</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U21-7 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r803.6i"></a>**803.6i** A card in the cache under a live permission can be played as an Ambush, as it could from the hand. Under a fulfilled prophecy it is free; under a glimpse its controller pays the Ambush mana but ignores the affinity. See rules 702.2d, 403.3c.

> *Example (non-normative): A glimpsed Ambush card ambushes out of the cache, paying the Ambush mana and ignoring affinity.* <sub>test: 370-cached-virus-in-battle.test.ts::R311: a glimpsed Ambush card ambushes out of the cache</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R311, R311 · Tests: 370-cached-virus-in-battle.test.ts, 369-cache-is-the-hand.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.ambush.cache</sub>

<a id="r803.6j"></a>**803.6j** An effect that plays a card for free, such as Tides of the Cosmos, may play an Ambush card as an Ambush. The Ambush cost is not paid, and a limit on the card's cost reads its main cost, not its Ambush cost. See rule 701.2c.

> *Example (non-normative): Tides of the Cosmos plays Mirrorback Ambusher as an Ambush: the ally leaves play and the ambusher stands in its place.* <sub>test: 404-raq-fix-tides.test.ts::R337: an Ambush card played by Tides as an Ambush takes an ally place</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): With 3 of the Tides budget left, Lurking Slimebeast (main cost 4, Ambush 3) is not offered but Mirage Walker (main cost 3, Ambush 4) is, and playing it as an Ambush spends no mana.* <sub>test: 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts::cr:keywords.abilities.ambush.tides — the Tides budget reads the MAIN cost, and an Ambush via Tides pays nothing</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1396955380000755795#2 · Rulings: R337, R337 · Tests: 404-raq-fix-tides.test.ts, 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.ambush.tides</sub>

<a id="r803.7"></a>**803.7.** Prophecy is a keyword printed on a card's banner as a cost and a condition. A card with a Prophecy banner may be prophesied: its controller pays the banner's cost, and the card moves to the cache with its prophecy attached. See rules 203.4, 801.14, 403.

> *Example (non-normative): A card with no banner cannot be prophesied.* <sub>test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::R42: a card with no banner cannot be prophesied at all</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R42 (its cache-and-release half), R301 · Replaces: R42 (window amended by R277; source zone amended by R308; no-affinity cost corrected by R301) · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.prophecy</sub>

<a id="r803.7a"></a>**803.7a** An effect can give a card a prophecy as it caches the card. The prophecy works as a printed one does once the card is in the cache. See rule 403.

> *Example (non-normative): Grob caches a unit with 'One Battle Passes' attached, and the prophecy is fulfilled once a battle has passed.* <sub>test: 39-light-b.test.ts::Grob: on attack, up to one unit's controller caches it with 'One Battle Passes'</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A unit cached with a granted prophecy carries it in the cache and it counts forward.* <sub>test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::R46: a cached unit can carry a granted prophecy (Grob / Waxen Witness)</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 2 tests run · Printed: card: Waxen Witness; card: Grob · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts, 39-light-b.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.prophecy.granted</sub>

<a id="r803.7b"></a>**803.7b** A card may be prophesied only during deployment. A card whose prophecy condition ends in a [Haste] icon may also be prophesied during the haste step. See rule 504.9.

> *Example (non-normative): Prophesying is refused in planning, in the haste step and in battle.* <sub>test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::R42: prophesying is a DEPLOYMENT action</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A banner marked [Haste] may be prophesied in the haste step.* <sub>test: 257-prophecy-release-timing.test.ts::R277: a banner marked [Haste] may be prophesied during the haste step</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R42 (its deployment-only window, as widened by R277), R277 (its prophesy-window half), R277 (its prophesy-window half) · Replaces: R42 (its deployment-only window amended by R277) · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts, 257-prophecy-release-timing.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.prophecy.window</sub>

<a id="r803.7c"></a>**803.7c** A card is prophesied from its controller's hand. It may be prophesied from the bin only if the card says so, and from the cache only while a glimpse permission on it is live; a card prophesied in the cache stays where it is. See rules 403.8, 801.9h.

> *Example (non-normative): Only a card that says so may be prophesied from the bin.* <sub>test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::R42: only a card that SAYS SO may be prophesied from the bin</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A glimpsed card with a banner may be prophesied where it stands in the cache.* <sub>test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::R308: a GLIMPSED card with a banner may be prophesied where it stands in the cache</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: card: Angel of Anguish · Rulings: R42 (its source-zone half, as amended by R308), R308 · Replaces: R42 (its source zone amended by R308) · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.prophecy.from</sub>

<a id="r803.7d"></a>**803.7d** Prophesying costs the banner's cost: its mana is spent and its affinity pips are required. See rules 203.2, 111.12.

> *Example (non-normative): Mana without the banner's affinity does not buy a prophecy.* <sub>test: 313-prophecy-affinity.test.ts::R301 §2: mana without the affinity does not buy a prophecy</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R301 · Replaces: R42 (its "plain mana number, no affinity" clause corrected by R301); R277 (its no-affinity aside superseded by R301) · Tests: 313-prophecy-affinity.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.prophecy.cost</sub>

<a id="r803.7e"></a>**803.7e** A prophecy's condition counts forward from the moment the card is prophesied. "Two Turns Pass" means two turns after the card was prophesied, not two turns of the game.

> *Example (non-normative): "One Turn Passes" counts from the prophesying, not from turn 1.* <sub>test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::R43: "One Turn Passes" counts from the PROPHESYING</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R43, R43 · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.prophecy.forward</sub>

<a id="r803.7f"></a>**803.7f** In a 1v1 game, both battles of a turn count toward "One Battle Passes". See rule 505.

> *Example (non-normative): A prophecy made after both battle rounds of a turn ignores those rounds, and the next turn's first completed battle round fulfils "One Battle Passes".* <sub>test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::R43: "One Battle Passes"</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Rulings: R43 · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.prophecy.battles</sub>

<a id="r803.7g"></a>**803.7g** Once a prophecy's condition has been met, the prophecy stays fulfilled, even if the state that met it goes away.

> *Example (non-normative): A card prophesied on "your life is 5 or less" stays playable after its controller gains life back.* <sub>test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::R44: a fulfilled prophecy LATCHES</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R44, R44 · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.prophecy.latch</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U21-5 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r803.7h"></a>**803.7h** Once the prophecy is fulfilled, the card may be played from the cache for free, ignoring affinity, as if it were in its controller's hand. See rules 403.3c, 111.13.

> *Example (non-normative): A released prophecy costs nothing and needs no affinity.* <sub>test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::R42: a released prophecy is FREE and ignores affinity</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R42 (its cache-and-release half), R301 · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts, 313-prophecy-affinity.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.prophecy.release</sub>

<a id="r803.7i"></a>**803.7i** A fulfilled prophecy changes what the card costs, not when it may be played. The card is played at its own printed timing, and a [Haste] icon in the banner does not move the release. See rule 504.9a.

> *Example (non-normative): A fulfilled {Battle} card is refused at deployment.* <sub>test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::R42: normal TIMING still applies</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A fulfilled prophecy on a battle card is offered at a battle window.* <sub>test: 257-prophecy-release-timing.test.ts::R277: a fulfilled prophecy on a battle card is offered at a BATTLE window</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R42 (its cache-and-release half), R277 (its release half), R277 (its release half) · Replaces: R206 (its Prophecy row (release at the banner's [Haste]) corrected by R279) · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts, 257-prophecy-release-timing.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.prophecy.release-timing</sub>

<a id="r803.7j"></a>**803.7j** An X spell released by a fulfilled prophecy is cast with X = 0. A variable bracketed cost on it is a cost, not its X, and is still paid. See rule 702.6c.

> *Example (non-normative): A fulfilled prophecy releases an X spell for X = 0: no X is asked and no mana paid.* <sub>test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::R111: a fulfilled prophecy releases an X spell for X = 0</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R111, R111 · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.prophecy.x</sub>

<a id="r803.7k"></a>**803.7k** A card whose prophecy is fulfilled may also be grafted or augmented from the cache, for free and ignoring affinity. Until the prophecy is fulfilled, the card cannot be played, grafted or augmented from the cache at all. See rules 403.3a, 403.3c, 720.

> *Example (non-normative): An unfulfilled prophecy cannot be grafted.* <sub>test: 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts::R303: an UNFULFILLED prophecy cannot be grafted</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A fulfilled prophecy grafts for free.* <sub>test: 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts::R303: a FULFILLED prophecy still grafts for free</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R303, R303, R303 · Tests: 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.prophecy.mods</sub>

<a id="r803.7m"></a>**803.7m** A condition that counts units dying, such as Vengeance's "13 Units Die", counts only the deaths its controller witnessed: deaths in a region where that player was present. A player is present in their own region, and in an enemy region once they have attacked into it, until regroup. See rules 601, 604.3a.

> *Example (non-normative): A death is counted only by the players who were in its region.* <sub>test: 314-prophecy-units-die.test.ts::R302 §2: a death is counted only by the seats that were in the region</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): An attack puts the attacker in the region, so both players see every death in that battle.* <sub>test: 314-prophecy-units-die.test.ts::R302 §3: combat puts the attacker in the region</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R302, R302, R302 · Tests: 314-prophecy-units-die.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.prophecy.units-die</sub>

<a id="r803.7n"></a>**803.7n** An effect that plays a card for free, such as Tides of the Cosmos, may play a card with a Prophecy banner as a Prophecy: the card is cached with its prophecy attached, and the banner cost is not paid. See rule 701.2c.

> *Example (non-normative): A card played by Tides as a Prophecy is cached with its banner, for free, and not binned.* <sub>test: 404-raq-fix-tides.test.ts::R337: a card played by Tides as a Prophecy is cached with its banner</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Designer: RAQ 1396955380000755795#2 · Rulings: R337 · Tests: 404-raq-fix-tides.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.prophecy.tides</sub>

<a id="r803.8"></a>**803.8.** Unstable is a non-combat attribute. If an Unstable card would enter a bin from an active zone (play or the stack), it is erased instead. See rules 405.5, 407, 803.8a.

> *Example (non-normative): Aberrant Statweaver, printed {Unstable}, dies into the erased pile, not the bin.* <sub>test: 17-earth-b.test.ts::Aberrant Statweaver: printed {Unstable}</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Printed: card: Abyssal Evocation; Manual p.25 · Rulings: R145, R145 · Tests: 17-earth-b.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.unstable</sub>

<a id="r803.8a"></a>**803.8a** Unstable applies only to a card leaving an active zone. The active zones are play and the stack. An Unstable card that goes to a bin from a hand, the deck, a bin or the cache is put into the bin normally, and is trashed. See rules 400.2a, 405.5.

> *Example (non-normative): A printed-Unstable card discarded from the hand is binned and trashed.* <sub>test: 125-active-zone.test.ts::R145: a printed-Unstable card DISCARDED FROM HAND</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A printed-Unstable card binned from the cache is binned and trashed.* <sub>test: 125-active-zone.test.ts::R145: a printed-Unstable card binned from the CACHE</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R145, R145, R145 · Tests: 125-active-zone.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.unstable.active-zone</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U21-6, D-U21-9 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r803.8b"></a>**803.8b** A card may print Unstable on its type line. Oorblak and Aberrant Statweaver do. See rule 204.

> *Example (non-normative): Oorblak, unmodded, is erased when it dies.* <sub>test: 17-earth-b.test.ts::Oorblak: printed {Unstable}</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: card: Aberrant Statweaver; card: Oorblak · Tests: 17-earth-b.test.ts, 125-active-zone.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.unstable.printed</sub>

<a id="r803.8c"></a>**803.8c** An effect may give a card Unstable. It is often given to cards played from the bin, so that they cannot be used more than once: Abyssal Evocation and Spell Excavation give the spells they let you play from the bin Unstable until regroup. See rule 405.9a.

> *Example (non-normative): A spell played from the bin under Abyssal Evocation is erased after it resolves, never re-binned.* <sub>test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::Abyssal Evocation: a bin-played spell is {Unstable}</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A spell played under Spell Excavation is erased rather than re-binned.* <sub>test: 15-water-b.test.ts::Spell Excavation: GRANTS the bin play until regroup</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: card: Abyssal Evocation; Manual p.25 · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts, 15-water-b.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.unstable.granted</sub>

<a id="r803.8d"></a>**803.8d** Unstable given "until regroup" lasts until regroup, even after the permission that came with it has ended. A spell unit played under such a grant passes it to the unit it puts into play. See rule 506.

> *Example (non-normative): A bin-played spell unit's body carries the Unstable stamp and is erased, not binned, when it dies.* <sub>test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::Abyssal Evocation: a bin-played SPELL UNIT stamps its BODY</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A bin-played spell unit body is still Unstable in the second battle round, after the permission to play spells from the bin has ended, and stops being Unstable at regroup.* <sub>test: 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts::cr:keywords.abilities.unstable.until-regroup — the stamp outlives the in-this-battle permission into round 2, and ends at regroup</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Rulings: R96, R96 · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts, 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.unstable.until-regroup</sub>

<a id="r803.8e"></a>**803.8e** A card is Unstable for as long as it is modded. When a modded card dies or is erased, it and all of its mods are erased. See rules 410.4b, 720.

> *Example (non-normative): A modded host exchanged out of play by Hooba-Mon is erased with its mods, which reach the erased pile.* <sub>test: 42-dark-b.test.ts::R152: the mods reach the public ERASED pile with the Unstable body (R65)</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.35; Manual p.35; Rulebook 2023 p.15 · Tests: 42-dark-b.test.ts, 37-attrs-wight.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.unstable.modded</sub>

<a id="r803.8f"></a>**803.8f** A spell is modded, and so Unstable, when a Virus is applied to it on the stack or a mod is applied to it through {Modular}. When it leaves the stack it is erased with its mods. See rules 704.2c, 723, 802.26.

> *Example (non-normative): Either way, the virus window or the {Modular} window, the carrier and the mod are erased.* <sub>test: 91-modular.test.ts::R105 = R79: the {Modular} window and the virus window agree</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): An unmodded {Modular} spell is binned like any other spell.* <sub>test: 91-modular.test.ts::R105: an UNMODDED {Modular} spell is not Unstable</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R79 (its virus-on-a-spell half), R105 · Replaces: R79 (its spell-token exclusion bullet superseded by R89) · Tests: 91-modular.test.ts, 125-active-zone.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.unstable.modded-spell</sub>

<a id="r803.8g"></a>**803.8g** A copy of a modded unit is not Unstable when it is made, because it has no mods of its own. A mod attached to it afterwards makes it Unstable in the usual way. See rule 710.2a.

> *Example (non-normative): A Borrower of Forms that copied a modded unit is not Unstable and dies to the bin.* <sub>test: 26-metal-a.test.ts::R336: copying a MODDED unit inherits the mods TEXT, and the copy is NOT {Unstable}</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A fresh Borrower of Forms that copied a modded unit is not Unstable; a mod attached to it afterwards makes it Unstable.* <sub>test: 403-raq-fix-mods.test.ts::R336: a Borrower that copied a modded unit dies to the bin</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A mod attached to Borrower of Forms after it resolved makes it Unstable.* <sub>test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Borrower of Forms: a mod attached to it after it resolved makes it Unstable</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 3 tests run · Designer: RAQ 1372468222158180424#1; RAQ 1372468222158180424#3 · Replaces: R118 (its ruling 2 Unstable half reversed by R336) · Tests: 403-raq-fix-mods.test.ts, 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 26-metal-a.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.unstable.copy</sub>

<a id="r803.8h"></a>**803.8h** Moving a mod moves its Unstable with it. The unit the mod leaves stops being Unstable when its last mod is gone, unless something else makes it Unstable; the unit it moves to becomes Unstable. See rule 720.

> *Example (non-normative): A moved augment takes Unstable and its static with it.* <sub>test: 151-copy-and-moved-mods.test.ts::R178 Rotbeast: a moved augment takes {Unstable}</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R178 (its §4 owner ruling on moving mods), R178 (its §4 owner ruling on moving mods) · Replaces: R178 (its §4 bounded-budget claim corrected by R331) · Tests: 151-copy-and-moved-mods.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.unstable.moved-mod</sub>

<a id="r803.8i"></a>**803.8i** Unstable replaces where the card goes, not its death. An Unstable unit that is destroyed still dies: its death triggers and other abilities that watch for a unit dying see it. See rules 713.8, 801.2h.

> *Example (non-normative): (illustrative) A modded unit dies in combat. A "whenever a unit dies" ability triggers, then the unit and its mods are erased.*

> *Example (non-normative): A modded unit is destroyed. A whenever-another-unit-dies ability triggers, then the unit is erased, not binned.* <sub>test: 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts::cr:keywords.abilities.unstable.still-dies — a modded (Unstable) unit that is destroyed still dies: a death watcher triggers, then it is erased</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Rulings: R69 (its §2: Unstable replaces the bin, not the death), R69 (its §2: Unstable replaces the bin, not the death), R145 · Replaces: R69 (its Unstable death order amended by R137; its token-trash subsection reversed by R306) · Tests: 42-dark-b.test.ts, 43-dark-c.test.ts, 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.unstable.still-dies</sub>

<a id="r803.8j"></a>**803.8j** Unstable does not stop a unit from being recalled. A recalled Unstable unit goes to the hand as a card; if it was modded, its mods are put into the bin. See rule 801.7b.

> *Example (non-normative): Recalling an Unstable unit puts the card in its hand, and nothing is erased.* <sub>test: 125-active-zone.test.ts::R145: RECALLING an Unstable unit puts the CARD IN HAND</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.35; Manual p.35; Manual p.35 · Rulings: R145 · Tests: 125-active-zone.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.unstable.recall</sub>

<a id="r803.8k"></a>**803.8k** An Unstable card that leaves the stack for a bin, because it resolved, fizzled or was negated, is erased instead. See rules 704.2c, 406.4.

> *Example (non-normative): Aberrant Statweaver negated off the stack is erased.* <sub>test: 125-active-zone.test.ts::R145: Aberrant Statweaver negated off the stack is ERASED</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A printed-Unstable virus whose host dies fizzles to the erased pile.* <sub>test: 125-active-zone.test.ts::R145: a printed-Unstable virus whose HOST DIES</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R145, R145 · Tests: 125-active-zone.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.unstable.stack</sub>

<a id="r803.8m"></a>**803.8m** An effect that itself says to put a card into a bin overrides Unstable. Pull Under ("Delete target unit. If you do, put it and all of its mods into your bin.") leaves a modded unit and its mods in that bin. See rule 101.

> *Example (non-normative): Pull Under deletes the target, and it and its mods land in the caster's bin, not erased.* <sub>test: 15-water-b.test.ts::Pull Under: deletes the target; it and its mods land in YOUR bin</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R137 (its Pull Under section), R137 (its Pull Under section) · Tests: 15-water-b.test.ts · Key: keywords.abilities.unstable.card-says-bin</sub>
