## 9. Multiplayer and Formats

<a id="r900"></a>
### 900. General

<a id="r900.1"></a>**900.1.** There are four game modes: live draft, constructed, cube draft and team draft. See rules 100, 901, 902. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.6; Manual p.6; Manual p.6; Manual p.6; Manual p.6 · Key: formats.general.modes</sub>

<a id="r900.1a"></a>**900.1a** The 2023 Rulebook calls cube draft "pre-draft": players draft a complete deck of at least 30 cards before the game begins, then play constructed games with it. See rule 902. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.1; Manual p.6 · Key: formats.general.modes.pre-draft</sub>

<a id="r900.2"></a>**900.2.** A game is played in one of these player setups: 1v1, free-for-all (FFA), teams, or archenemy. See rule 100. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.6; Manual p.6; Manual p.6; Manual p.6; Manual p.6 · Key: formats.general.setups</sub>

<a id="r900.2a"></a>**900.2a** A 1v1 game is played between two players. It is the recommended setup for a first game. See rules 903, 904.

> *Example (non-normative): Every game the client creates is a 1v1 game: two seats, two regions.* <sub>test: 412-cr-general.test.ts::cr:concepts.general.digital-scope</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.6; Rulebook 2023 p.1 · Tests: 412-cr-general.test.ts · Key: formats.general.setups.one-v-one</sub>

<a id="r900.2b"></a>**900.2b** Free-for-all is described in 903. Team games and archenemy are described in 904. See rules 903, 904. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.6 · Key: formats.general.setups.multiplayer</sub>

<a id="r900.3"></a>**900.3.** A 1v1 game counts as a team game: each player is their own team. Free-for-all is not a team game. See rule 904.

> *Example (non-normative): With The Silent in play, two spells you have played this battle make your next spell cost [4] more, while your opponent still pays the printed cost: in 1v1 your team is you alone.* <sub>test: 433-cr-formats.test.ts::cr:formats.general.one-v-one-is-team — with The Silent out, each player is billed only for the spells that player has played, as a one-player team</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.20; Rulebook 2023 p.5 · Tests: 433-cr-formats.test.ts · Key: formats.general.one-v-one-is-team</sub>

<a id="r900.4"></a>**900.4.** Where the players sit sets which regions neighbour each other. See rules 601, 904.3. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.11; Manual p.19 · Key: formats.general.seating</sub>

<a id="r900.4a"></a>**900.4a** In 1v1 the players sit across from each other. Each has one neighbouring region. See rule 601.

> *Example (non-normative): A 1v1 game has two regions. An attack names no region: it is always fought in the opponent region, the only neighbouring one.* <sub>test: 433-cr-formats.test.ts::cr:formats.general.seating.one-v-one — a two-player game has two regions, one per player, and an attack is fought in the one other region with no region to choose</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.11; Manual p.19 · Tests: 433-cr-formats.test.ts · Key: formats.general.seating.one-v-one</sub>

<a id="r900.4b"></a>**900.4b** In a game of more than two players the players sit in a circle, so each player has a player to their left and a player to their right. Each player has two neighbouring regions. See rule 601. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.11; Manual p.11; Manual p.19 · Key: formats.general.seating.circle</sub>

<a id="r900.5"></a>**900.5.** Battle normally resolves one region at a time, in the order of 601. Once players are comfortable with the game, they may resolve at the same time any regions that have no player in common. See rules 601, 505.

> *Example (non-normative): With an attack and a counterattack, the battle in the defending region runs to its end before the counterattack battle begins in the other region.* <sub>test: 433-cr-formats.test.ts::cr:formats.general.simultaneous-regions — battle is in one region at a time: the first round ends in the defending region before the counterattack starts in the other</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.21; Manual p.21; Manual p.21 · Tests: 433-cr-formats.test.ts · Key: formats.general.simultaneous-regions</sub>

<a id="r900.6"></a>**900.6.** The client plays 1v1 live draft and 1v1 constructed only. It has no free-for-all, team, archenemy, cube-draft or team-draft games, and no intent cards. Rules 903, 904 and 905, and the parts of 902 about cube draft and team draft, describe the printed game, which the client does not enforce. See rule 100.

> *Example (non-normative): Every game the engine creates has exactly two seats, two regions and two packs.* <sub>test: 412-cr-general.test.ts::cr:concepts.general.digital-scope</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A card text that would misbehave only with a third player cannot be reached: the engine is 1v1 by construction.* <sub>test: 168-three-card-divergences.test.ts::R197 §3a Cinder Scuttler</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R27 (the "Project decisions" block recorded under it), R197 (its §3 two-seat measurement, which stands) · Tests: 412-cr-general.test.ts, 168-three-card-divergences.test.ts · Key: formats.general.digital-scope</sub>

<a id="r901"></a>
### 901. Constructed

<a id="r901.1"></a>**901.1.** In constructed, each player brings their own deck, built before the game, and plays from it. See rules 103, 401.

> *Example (non-normative): A constructed game takes one deck per seat.* <sub>test: 34-constructed.test.ts::createGame constructed: per-seat decks</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.6; Manual p.16 · Designer: RAQ 1451507918171013252#1 · Tests: 34-constructed.test.ts · Key: formats.constructed.what</sub>

<a id="r901.2"></a>**901.2.** A constructed deck has at least 30 cards. No source sets a maximum.

> *Example (non-normative): A 29-card deck is refused.* <sub>test: 34-constructed.test.ts::checkDeck: min 30, max 2 copies</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.6; Manual p.16; Rulebook 2023 p.1 · Tests: 34-constructed.test.ts, 433-cr-formats.test.ts · Key: formats.constructed.deck-size</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U22-7 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r901.3"></a>**901.3.** A constructed deck may hold at most 2 copies of any one card. See rule 901.8.

> *Example (non-normative): A third copy of a card makes the deck illegal.* <sub>test: 34-constructed.test.ts::checkDeck: min 30, max 2 copies</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.6; Manual p.16 · Tests: 34-constructed.test.ts, 433-cr-formats.test.ts · Key: formats.constructed.copies</sub>

<a id="r901.4"></a>**901.4.** Constructed has no shared deck and no packs. See rules 103, 401, 409.

> *Example (non-normative): A constructed game starts with an empty shared deck and two empty packs.* <sub>test: 433-cr-formats.test.ts::cr:formats.constructed.no-packs — a constructed game has no shared deck and no packs</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.16; Manual p.10 · Tests: 433-cr-formats.test.ts · Key: formats.constructed.no-packs</sub>

<a id="r901.5"></a>**901.5.** In constructed, the draw step and the draft step are taken together as one draw phase: each player draws 4 cards from their own deck, then puts 2 cards from their hand on the bottom of their deck. See rules 503, 408.

> *Example (non-normative): Turn 1 of a constructed game: each player has 4 cards, draws 4, and the put-back of 2 is pending.* <sub>test: 34-constructed.test.ts::createGame constructed: per-seat decks, opening 4 + draw 4, bottoming open</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): On turn 2 the draw phase opens again: 4 more cards, and 2 to put back.* <sub>test: 34-constructed.test.ts::turn 2 reopens the draw phase</sub>

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.6; Manual p.16; Manual p.16 · Designer: RAQ 1451507918171013252#1 · Tests: 34-constructed.test.ts · Key: formats.constructed.draw-phase</sub>

<a id="r901.5a"></a>**901.5a** The player chooses the 2 cards and puts them on the bottom in any order. Because every card put on the bottom of a deck goes into the recycle pile, which is shuffled before it is drawn from again, the order has no effect on play. See rule 408.

> *Example (non-normative): Nothing moves until the 2 cards go back, and they go back in the order given.* <sub>test: 34-constructed.test.ts::nothing moves until the 2 cards go back</sub>

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.6 · Rulings: R296, R296 · Tests: 34-constructed.test.ts · Key: formats.constructed.draw-phase.order</sub>

<a id="r901.5b"></a>**901.5b** For state checks the draw of 4 and the put-back of 2 are one step: a player's units are not checked for death while that player still has 2 cards to put back, so they are judged on the hand that remains. See rules 503, 713.

> *Example (non-normative): Dreadspawn Horror with 1 card in hand: drawing 4 does not kill it, and after the put-back it is a 4/2.* <sub>test: 380-no-action-ends-dead.test.ts::R313 constructed: drawing 4 does not kill before the 2 go back</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): With 3 cards in hand it reaches 5 and dies once its controller has put 2 back.* <sub>test: 380-no-action-ends-dead.test.ts::R313 constructed: 3 cards in hand nets to 5</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R313, R313 · Tests: 380-no-action-ends-dead.test.ts · Key: formats.constructed.draw-phase.one-step</sub>

<a id="r901.6"></a>**901.6.** A player in a constructed game may make a resource of any element, whether or not their deck holds a card of that element. See rules 106, 502.

> *Example (non-normative): All seven elements stay legal for a resource, whatever the deck holds.* <sub>test: 34-constructed.test.ts::deckElements: it is a PRESENTATION default</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R99, R99 · Tests: 34-constructed.test.ts · Key: formats.constructed.any-element</sub>

<a id="r901.7"></a>**901.7.** Card text that refers to a constructed format applies in a constructed game. See rule 503.

> *Example (non-normative): Worldbender in constructed: the player skips the draw-4-put-2-back, the hand gains 3 cards, and the player loses 3 life.* <sub>test: 28-metal-c.test.ts::Worldbender in constructed</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Worldbender in a live draft: the hand gains 3 cards and life is untouched.* <sub>test: 28-metal-c.test.ts::Worldbender in a live draft</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Printed: card: Worldbender · Tests: 28-metal-c.test.ts · Key: formats.constructed.card-text</sub>

<a id="r901.7a"></a>**901.7a** The matches of a cube draft are constructed games, so such text applies in them too. See rule 902. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.39; card: Worldbender · Key: formats.constructed.card-text.cube</sub>

<a id="r901.7b"></a>**901.7b** The client has a testing mode called "shared", which is not a format. Card text that asks whether the game is constructed treats a shared game as constructed. See rule 900.

> *Example (non-normative): Worldbender in shared takes the constructed branch: three cards and 3 life.* <sub>test: 137-multiplier-and-mode.test.ts::Worldbender in 'shared': the default mode takes the CONSTRUCTED branch</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R157 (its §2, which stands), R162 (its 'shared' is constructed half, which stands) · Tests: 137-multiplier-and-mode.test.ts · Key: formats.constructed.card-text.shared-mode</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U22-10 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r901.8"></a>**901.8.** Single Card Duel is a variant of constructed that the client offers. Each player picks a single card before the game, and their deck is 30 copies of that card. See rule 901.3.

> *Example (non-normative): A Single Card Duel deck is 30 copies of the one card chosen, and a constructed game starts with it.* <sub>test: 433-cr-formats.test.ts::cr:formats.constructed.single-card — a duel deck is 30 copies of one card, and a constructed game accepts it</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Rulings: R298, R298 · Tests: 433-cr-formats.test.ts · Key: formats.constructed.single-card</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U22-8 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r901.8a"></a>**901.8a** A Single Card Duel deck is the one exception to the limit of 2 copies of a card. See rule 901.3.

> *Example (non-normative): Thirty copies of one card fail the ordinary deck check but are accepted as a Single Card Duel deck.* <sub>test: 433-cr-formats.test.ts::cr:formats.constructed.single-card.copies — the duel deck breaks the two-copy cap: checkDeck refuses it, checkSingleDeck and createGame accept it</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Rulings: R298 · Tests: 433-cr-formats.test.ts · Key: formats.constructed.single-card.copies</sub>

<a id="r901.8b"></a>**901.8b** A Single Card Duel has no draw phase. Each turn, each player simply draws 2 cards; nothing is put back. The opening hand is still 4 cards. See rule 503.

> *Example (non-normative): Each player starts turn 1 with 6 cards (4 + 2) and nothing to put back, and draws exactly 2 more on turn 2.* <sub>test: 433-cr-formats.test.ts::cr:formats.constructed.single-card.no-draw-phase — opening 4, a flat 2 each turn, nothing put back</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Rulings: R298, R298 · Tests: 433-cr-formats.test.ts · Key: formats.constructed.single-card.no-draw-phase</sub>

<a id="r901.8c"></a>**901.8c** If neither player's card can make a unit, the game is not played. It is a draw: each player is told the other's card, and both choose again. A card can make a unit if it is a unit or spell-unit card, or if it creates a unit token. See rule 104.

> *Example (non-normative): A unit card and Self-Assembly (which creates a Robot unit token) can make a unit; a spell that creates no unit cannot.* <sub>test: 433-cr-formats.test.ts::cr:formats.constructed.single-card.no-units — makesUnits is true for a unit and a unit-token maker, false for a spell that makes none</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Rulings: R298, R298 · Tests: 433-cr-formats.test.ts · Key: formats.constructed.single-card.no-units</sub>

<a id="r902"></a>
### 902. Draft and Cube

<a id="r902.1"></a>**902.1.** In live draft, the players share one deck, built from the chosen elements, and draft cards from it during the game. See rules 103, 401, 409.

> *Example (non-normative): A live draft deals each seat a hand and a pack from one shared deck.* <sub>test: 20-draft.test.ts::createGame draft: 6-card hands</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.6; Manual p.6; Rulebook 2023 p.1 · Tests: 20-draft.test.ts · Key: formats.draft.live-draft</sub>

<a id="r902.1a"></a>**902.1a** Live draft is the standard Algomancy format, and 1v1 live draft is the format suggested for learning the game. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.1; Manual p.10 · Key: formats.draft.live-draft.standard</sub>

<a id="r902.2"></a>**902.2.** A live draft uses 3 elements for 2–3 players and 4 elements for 4–6 players. For 6 or more players, a cube draft with all 5 elements is recommended instead of a live draft. See rules 105, 103.

> *Example (non-normative): A standard 1v1 live draft is built from exactly 3 elements.* <sub>test: 412-cr-general.test.ts::cr:concepts.starting.live-draft.elements</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.11; Manual p.11; Manual p.11 · Tests: 412-cr-general.test.ts · Key: formats.draft.elements</sub>

<a id="r902.2a"></a>**902.2a** In casual games, players take turns choosing the elements, or assign them randomly. The printed rules defer the competitive procedure to Algomancy.io. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.11; Manual p.11 · Key: formats.draft.elements.choosing</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U22-6 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r902.3"></a>**902.3.** In live draft each player begins with 16 cards to draft from: a 6-card hand (the 4-card starting hand plus the first turn's 2 draws) and a 10-card pack. See rules 103, 503.

> *Example (non-normative): A new live draft deals 6-card hands and 10-card packs, with the draft step open.* <sub>test: 20-draft.test.ts::createGame draft: 6-card hands (opening 4 + turn-1 draws), 10-card packs</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.11; Manual p.11 · Designer: RAQ 1451507918171013252#0 · Tests: 20-draft.test.ts · Key: formats.draft.sixteen</sub>

<a id="r902.4"></a>**902.4.** The draft step is described in 503, and the pack, its refresh every N+1 turns and an eliminated player's pack in 409. See rules 503, 409.

> *Example (non-normative): Turns 2 and 3 draw 2 and reopen the draft step; the packs refresh on turn 4.* <sub>test: 20-draft.test.ts::turns 2-3 draw 2 and re-open the draft step</sub>

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Printed: Manual p.16; Manual p.16 · Tests: 20-draft.test.ts · Key: formats.draft.draft-step</sub>

<a id="r902.5"></a>**902.5.** The client lets a live draft be created with custom rules. Custom rules change the deal and nothing else: they never change how a card works.

> *Example (non-normative): A custom deal changes the draft for the same seed.* <sub>test: 296-custom-draft-deal.test.ts::BL-43 §1a control</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): A custom deal is ignored outside a live draft.* <sub>test: 296-custom-draft-deal.test.ts::BL-43 §1c a custom deal is ignored outside a live draft</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R292, R292 · Tests: 296-custom-draft-deal.test.ts · Key: formats.draft.custom</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U22-9 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r902.5a"></a>**902.5a** Pack size may be set from 3 to 15 cards (standard 10). Every pack is dealt and refreshed at that size, and the draft step leaves exactly that many cards in the pack. See rules 409, 503.

> *Example (non-normative): Packs of 5: 5 at the deal, the draft commit leaves 5, and the turn-4 refresh deals 5.* <sub>test: 296-custom-draft-deal.test.ts::BL-43 §2a pack size</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 1 test run · Rulings: R292, R292 · Tests: 296-custom-draft-deal.test.ts, 433-cr-formats.test.ts · Key: formats.draft.custom.pack-size</sub>

<a id="r902.5b"></a>**902.5b** The number of elements may be set from 2 to 7 (standard 3). The pool is every deck card whose elements all lie within the chosen set. Two elements default to fire and wood. See rule 105.

> *Example (non-normative): Two elements: fire and wood by default, or a chosen pair; 113 cards.* <sub>test: 296-custom-draft-deal.test.ts::BL-43 §2c two elements</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R292, R292 · Tests: 296-custom-draft-deal.test.ts, 433-cr-formats.test.ts · Key: formats.draft.custom.elements</sub>

<a id="r902.5c"></a>**902.5c** The opening hand may be set from 1 to 15 cards (standard 6), the draws per turn after turn 1 from 0 to 5 (standard 2), and the starting life from 1 to 99 (standard 30). See rules 103, 503.

> *Example (non-normative): Opening hand, draws per turn and starting life each follow the custom rules.* <sub>test: 296-custom-draft-deal.test.ts::BL-43 §2b opening hand, draws per turn and starting life</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R292, R292 · Tests: 296-custom-draft-deal.test.ts · Key: formats.draft.custom.numbers</sub>

<a id="r902.5d"></a>**902.5d** With "simple cards only", the pool holds only cards with the silver (Simple) complexity symbol. See rule 209.

> *Example (non-normative): Simple cards only leaves out exactly the cards that are not simple.* <sub>test: 297-custom-rules-resolve.test.ts::BL-43 resolve §3 Simple cards only leaves out exactly the cards that are not simple</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R292 · Tests: 297-custom-rules-resolve.test.ts · Key: formats.draft.custom.simple</sub>

<a id="r902.5e"></a>**902.5e** Cards may be banned by name, and an advanced card filter may be set: only cards that match it are in the pool. A banned or filtered-out card is nowhere in the game.

> *Example (non-normative): An excluded card is nowhere in the game, at the deal or after a fuzzed game.* <sub>test: 296-custom-draft-deal.test.ts::BL-43 §3 an excluded card is nowhere in the game</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Bans and the card filter add up.* <sub>test: 297-custom-rules-resolve.test.ts::BL-43 resolve §5 bans and the card filter add up</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R292, R292 · Tests: 296-custom-draft-deal.test.ts, 297-custom-rules-resolve.test.ts · Key: formats.draft.custom.bans</sub>

<a id="r902.5f"></a>**902.5f** Custom rules do not change the pack refresh: it still comes every N+1 turns. See rule 409.

> *Example (non-normative): With packs of 5 the turn-4 refresh still comes, and deals 5.* <sub>test: 296-custom-draft-deal.test.ts::BL-43 §2a pack size</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R292 · Tests: 296-custom-draft-deal.test.ts · Key: formats.draft.custom.refresh</sub>

<a id="r902.5g"></a>**902.5g** A custom pool must hold at least 2 × hand + 4 × pack + 6 × draws cards (64 for the standard game). Custom rules below that floor are refused before the game is created. When the elements are to be chosen later, every set of that size must pass.

> *Example (non-normative): The standard game needs 64 cards, the beginner deal 44.* <sub>test: 296-custom-draft-deal.test.ts::BL-43 §5 minPool</sub>

> *Example (non-normative): Too small a pool is refused with a message that names the fix.* <sub>test: 297-custom-rules-resolve.test.ts::BL-43 resolve §8 too small a pool is refused</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 2 tests run · Rulings: R292, R292 · Tests: 296-custom-draft-deal.test.ts, 297-custom-rules-resolve.test.ts · Key: formats.draft.custom.floor</sub>

<a id="r902.5h"></a>**902.5h** Custom rules are not printed rules. Packs of other than 10 cards are not in the printed rules, and the client's Beginner preset (two elements, simple cards only, packs of 5) is the client's own softening of the Quick Start.

> *Example (non-normative): The Beginner preset sends two elements, simple cards and packs of 5.* <sub>test: 298-custom-rules-ui.test.ts::BL-43 ui §2 the Beginner preset</sub>

<sub>Basis: Owner call · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 1 test run · Rulings: R292, R292 · Tests: 298-custom-rules-ui.test.ts · Key: formats.draft.custom.not-printed</sub>

<a id="r902.6"></a>**902.6.** Cube draft is a format for large groups (6 to 10 or more players). The players draft decks before the game, then use them to play constructed matches, often in a 1v1 tournament bracket. See rule 901. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.39; Manual p.39; Manual p.39; Manual p.6 · Key: formats.draft.cube</sub>

<a id="r902.6a"></a>**902.6a** The cube is all of the game cards, hybrids included, shuffled together: 320 cards from one box. For more than 8 players, two complete sets are used (640 cards). *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.39; Manual p.39; Manual p.39; Manual p.39 · Key: formats.draft.cube.the-cube</sub>

<a id="r902.6b"></a>**902.6b** To draft, deal each player a pack of 10 cards. Then repeat these steps 15 times, until each player has a 30-card deck: (1) each player draws 2 cards from the cube; (2) players may combine their hands with their packs; (3) each player chooses 10 cards from their combined hand and pack and passes them, as a new pack, clockwise to their neighbour. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.39; Manual p.39; Manual p.39; Manual p.39; Manual p.39; Manual p.39; Manual p.39 · Key: formats.draft.cube.procedure</sub>

<a id="r902.6c"></a>**902.6c** Players then play constructed matches with the 30-card decks they drafted. See rules 901, 901.7. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.39 · Key: formats.draft.cube.decks</sub>

<a id="r902.7"></a>**902.7.** A traditional cube draft may be used instead. Each player is dealt three packs of 13 to 15 cards: 15 cards for 6 players, 13 for 8 players. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.39; Manual p.39; Manual p.39 · Key: formats.draft.cube-traditional</sub>

<a id="r902.7a"></a>**902.7a** Each player looks at their pack, takes one card from it and passes the rest to their neighbour, until the pack is empty. This is done three times, once per pack, passing left, then right, then left. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 2, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.39; Manual p.39; Manual p.39; Manual p.39 · Key: formats.draft.cube-traditional.picks</sub>

<a id="r902.7b"></a>**902.7b** From the cards they drafted, each player builds a 30-card deck for the constructed matches that follow. See rule 901. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.39; Manual p.39 · Key: formats.draft.cube-traditional.deck</sub>

<a id="r902.8"></a>**902.8.** In team draft, each team brings a constructed deck of 30 cards for each player on the team, with at most 2 copies of each card. The team live drafts from that deck during the game. See rules 904, 901.3. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Manual p.6; Manual p.6; Manual p.6 · Key: formats.draft.team-draft</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U22-1 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r902.8a"></a>**902.8a** In team draft, a player who has finished drafting passes their pack to the nearest teammate, not clockwise to the nearest player. See rule 503. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.6; Rulebook 2023 p.6 · Key: formats.draft.team-draft.pass</sub>

<a id="r902.8b"></a>**902.8b** In team draft, packs are never refreshed. See rule 409. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.6 · Key: formats.draft.team-draft.no-refresh</sub>

<a id="r902.8c"></a>**902.8c** All the other rules of live draft apply in team draft. See rules 503, 409. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed, round 1, 0 tests run · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.6 · Key: formats.draft.team-draft.other-rules</sub>

<a id="r902.8d"></a>**902.8d** The 2023 Rulebook sizes the team-draft deck differently: the team builds a deck of 100 cards, with at most 2 copies of each card. See rule 901.3. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*
