### Engine-only rules (awaiting the owner's sign-off)

- [103.3b](#r103.3b) In constructed, each player's opening hand is 4 cards. No source gives the constructed opening hand; it is the client's convention.
- [105.4c](#r105.4c) A dormant resource gives no affinity until it is activated.
- [109.9n](#r109.9n) A bounded "When I am trashed" ability is limited for each trashed card, not for each player and card name: two copies of one card trashed in the same turn each trigger.
- [111.3a](#r111.3a) A cost that removes counters from the player's allies, or recalls an ally, likewise uses only the player's own units in the region where the cost is paid.
- [406.4b](#r406.4b) A self-erasing spell that is negated or fails to resolve goes to the bin. Its "Erase me" never happened.
- [602.6j](#r602.6j) After blocks, while the defending formation still holds at least one unit, a unit placed into it may also take the front slot of a blocking column whose blockers have all left it. The unit then blocks that column.
- [603.1c](#r603.1c) Two side-blocking units may stand in the same side-block column, one in its front slot and one in its back slot.
- [606.7](#r606.7) If no attacking unit is left when the block step begins, the block step still takes place: the defending player declares blocks, which may be none, and the battle round continues.
- [713.3a](#r713.3a) Deaths are also checked while an effect is still resolving, not only at safe points. Each time an effect puts counters on a unit, and after each part of an effect made of several parts, units that should be dead die at once, before the rest of the effect happens.
- [723.4e](#r723.4e) Triggered and activated abilities, Viruses, units being cast and Ambushes on the stack are not legal hosts for a Virus.
- [D1.2b](#rD1.2b) The game takes an action for a player only where the battle leaves them nothing to decide: an attacker with no unit able to attack has the empty attack declared for them, and a defender with no unit in the battle region has the empty block declared for them. These forced actions are logged like any other. A player holding full control is not forced: the window is left to them.
- [D2.3](#rD2.3) A player may turn on auto-pass. With it on, the client passes priority for the player only in a window where passing is the only thing they could do. Auto-pass never passes through an open decision.
- [D2.9](#rD2.9) This client has no way to keep priority after acting: when a player puts something on the stack in battle, priority goes to the opponent. A player can still respond to their own spell, once priority comes back to them with it still on the stack.
- [D3.1](#rD3.1) A game may be played with a chess clock, in which each player has a bank of time. The home screen offers three settings: no clock, 45 minutes and 60 minutes.
- [D3.1a](#rD3.1a) Unless the player chooses otherwise, the bank is 45 minutes for a constructed game and 60 minutes for a live draft.
- [D3.1b](#rD3.1b) A game with no clock shows no clocks.
- [D3.1c](#rD3.1c) Choosing a clock setting does not make a game a custom game.
- [D3.1d](#rD3.1d) A player's clock is shown as critical when it is down to a tenth of the game's bank or to one minute, whichever is less.
- [D3.2](#rD3.2) A player's clock runs only while the game is waiting on that player, and only while both players are connected.
- [D3.2a](#rD3.2a) In a step both players take at once, both clocks run; a player's clock stops when that player finishes the step.
- [D3.2b](#rD3.2b) A player's clock does not run in a priority window that their standing pass is answering, and the other player, who has nothing to do there, is not billed either. A real choice is billed even while a standing pass is set. If the client's pass has not arrived within a short backstop, the server passes for the player, and that pass is logged like any other.
- [D3.2c](#rD3.2c) A player watching a recap is off the clock until the playback ends or the server's hold on it lapses. Acting ends the hold.
- [D3.3](#rD3.3) A player whose clock runs out loses the game, and the log says they ran out of time. This happens even if neither player acts.
- [D3.4](#rD3.4) A game is closed when nobody has moved in it for an hour, if fewer than five actions have been taken, or for twelve hours otherwise, and nobody (no player and no watcher) has been connected to it for the five-minute reconnect grace. An open tab keeps an idle game open.
- [D3.4a](#rD3.4a) A connected player or a watcher keeps an idle game open, and an empty game is given a grace period for a player to reconnect.
- [D3.4b](#rD3.4b) A game closed for being idle has no winner, is not rated, and is recorded as unfinished.
- [D4.1a](#rD4.1a) The opponent acting in the same step does not stop a player's undo.
- [D4.1b](#rD4.1b) An undo cannot go back past what the step itself did as it began, such as a payment or an ability that happens at the start of the step.
- [D4.1c](#rD4.1c) Actions taken in battle are not undone. For that reason an irreversible activated ability asks for confirmation in battle, while in deployment it activates on the click and undo is the safety net.
- [D5.1a](#rD5.1a) The recap changes nothing in the game. A game played with recap frames is the same game, action for action, as one without them.
- [D5.1b](#rD5.1b) A frame of the opponent's move shows that move on their side, their hand still face down, and the player's own side as the player left it.
- [D5.1c](#rD5.1c) A move with nothing to show is not given a frame, but its log line is kept.
- [D5.1d](#rD5.1d) The end of turn is played as one frame per trigger, in order.
- [D5.1f](#rD5.1f) Undoing a move inside the step removes that move's frame and keeps the others.
- [D5.3](#rD5.3) The deployment recap pauses after the opponent's moves and again after the end of turn; the haste step's recap pauses the same way. Skip jumps to the next pause, never past it. A quiet end of turn does not pause twice.
- [D5.3b](#rD5.3b) The hand-over to the next turn at the end of a recap pauses longer than a frame. Every recap, live, watched again or in Learn to Play, is paced by the same rule.
- [D5.5c](#rD5.5c) During a recap playback, skipping does not jump to the live state. Skip (the S key, Space, or the Skip button drawn on the play bar) jumps to the next stop, and on a stop it continues the playback.

### Findings: where the engine differs

- <a id="F-U01-1"></a>**F-U01-1** Ownership is lost once a stolen card passes through the thief's hand (CT-233). Rule 102.4. Zones follow control, so a stolen unit that is recalled goes to the thief's hand. The hand holds a bare card name, so when the thief replays it the new unit's owner defaults to the playing seat, and the engine records the thief as owner. The rulings say ownership never moves ("its OWNER's, always, forever"). The verifier's probe measured owner = thief after the replay. Low impact today because zones follow control, but the owner field no longer means what the ruling says it keeps meaning. (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.) Also found as F-U01-3.
- <a id="F-U01-2"></a>**F-U01-2** The stack, bins and cache are regionless, so some effects reach across regions (CT-234). Rule 101.6. The Manual says every effect is specific to its region and never impacts anything in another region, and Caleb says everything in the game is region-specific. The client, by an R-ruling, gives the stack, bins and cache no region, so Frosted Denial, Woodland Warding and Molten Riftbreaker reach across regions. Unit targeting, statics and triggers are region-scoped and agree with print. Pending the owner's answer on D-U01-12; fix nothing until then. (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.) Also found as F-U01-4, F-U01-5.
- <a id="F-U01-3"></a>**F-U01-3** Ownership is lost when a card passes through a hand or bin (CT-233). Rule 102.4. Hands and bins store bare card names, so a stolen unit that is recalled to the thief's hand (R262) and played again becomes a new entity owned by the thief. R250 and R262 say ownership never moves ('its OWNER's, always, forever'; in constructed the owner is whoever brought the card). (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.)
- <a id="F-U01-4"></a>**F-U01-4** Stack, bin and cache effects reach across regions (CT-234). Rule 101.6. Card code that iterates g.s.stack (for example Molten Riftbreaker's 'negate all allied spells') has no region filter. An effect resolving in one region negated a spell on the stack in another region. The designer says everything in the game is region specific; R250 and R265 keep the stack global on purpose, so this is a documented owner-ruling divergence from designer and printed text, not an accident. (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.)
- <a id="F-U01-5"></a>**F-U01-5** The stack, bins and cache are global: an effect in one region reaches a stack item in another (CT-234). Rule 101.6. Cosmic Reversal's stack half (and Molten Riftbreaker, Frosted Denial) iterate the whole stack regardless of region, by owner ruling R250/R265. The designer says everything in the game is region specific and nothing crosses regions except attacking. Probe: Cosmic Reversal resolving in A's home region recalled A's Luminous Arc from the battle region's stack.
- <a id="F-U02-1"></a>**F-U02-1** X-cost test titles still cite R157 §20, which R326 reversed (CT-235). Rule 107.5. Three tests in 133-x-cost-semantics are titled "R157 §20 — …" although R326 reversed §20. Their assertions agree with R326 (X = 3 costs [3], X = 5 costs [5]; no Sentry costs exactly X), and one of them is the guard for RAQ 1359629594512068770#1. The labels point a reader at reversed law. Retitle them to R326 (or to R157 §1 for the no-Sentry cases).
- <a id="F-U02-2"></a>**F-U02-2** R158 section 1 still says Living Vault refuses X cards in hand (CT-236). Rule 107.3a. R158 §1 (current) says Living Vault's printedMana returns null, so an X card in hand is never offered, and calls it the odd one out. Test 39-light-b now asserts the opposite: Living Vault offers an X card in hand at [0]. The ruling text is stale. It should be marked as corrected, or the sentence amended, so the register does not describe a bug that is fixed.
- <a id="F-U02-3"></a>**F-U02-3** A Prismite cannot be exchanged into a Shard, though the printed card says "a non-prismite resource" (CT-237). Rule 106.8d. doExchangePrismite accepts only an element of the game. The printed Prismite reads "Erase me: Create a non-prismite resource, then activate it" and Manual p.18 says active Prismites "may be exchanged for other resources"; a Shard is a non-prismite resource. No ruling forbids the Shard (R299 rules the Prismite-into-Prismite case), and test 308's title asserts the refusal. Low impact: a Shard is never better than an element resource.
- <a id="F-U03-1"></a>**F-U03-1** Wraith test title still calls the self-pick an unconfirmed reading after the owner confirmed it (CT-238). Rule 110.4a. R71 item 4 (owner, 2026-08-21) settled that "an ally" may be the Wraith itself, and R265 (owner, 2026-08-30) made "an ally includes itself" general. The 37-attrs-wight test is still titled "(unconfirmed reading)" with a warning mark. The title states an open question that is closed; retitle it to cite the ruling.
- <a id="F-U03-2"></a>**F-U03-2** Gatekeeper of Souls compels targets chosen outside battle (CT-239). Rule 110.12. Printed: "When a player selects targets for an effect during battle, I must be targeted if able." The engine applies the compulsion by region only, so in deployment a player whose own Gatekeeper stands in their home region can only aim a unit-targeting effect (Overbloom) at the Gatekeeper. Measured by the round-1 verifier's probe. (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.)
- <a id="F-U03-3"></a>**F-U03-3** The R58 Enigmatic Warder test asserts nothing on its main path (CT-240). Rule 110.4c. 49-playtest-round6 'R58: Enigmatic Warder cannot redirect an ENEMY into an ally slot' passes twice and then looks for Fight on the stack; Fight has resolved by then, so the ally-slot assertion inside `if (after)` never runs, and the remaining assertion holds whatever the Warder did. Assert before passing, or drop the guard.
- <a id="F-U03-4"></a>**F-U03-4** RAQ 1354013430805434389#2 (retarget rescues from fizzle) has a guard that shows no rescue (CT-241). Rule 110.9b. The RAQ register guards the claim "retargeting before resolution can rescue an effect from fizzling" with the Gravitational Correction test, whose original target is still legal; it shows a retarget, not a fizzle avoided. No test moves a target off an object that would make the effect fizzle.
- <a id="F-U03-5"></a>**F-U03-5** A deployment graft onto Mohruung is attached before Mohruung's trigger resolves (CT-242). Rule 110.11. The designer: grafting onto Mohruung, "he will trigger first". The engine fires the targeted event, attaches the graft at once, and only then resolves the queued trigger: the round-2 verifier's probe logs "Flame Juggle grafts onto Mohruung" before "Resolving Mohruung: create a Crystal 2". The RAQ guard (393 point 5) asserts only that a Crystal is made, not the order. Pending D-U03-13. (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.)
- <a id="F-U04-1"></a>**F-U04-1** Deferral Drone: a test title and R119 say "this turn"; the printed card says "this phase" (CT-235). Rule 111.10k. Deferral Drone prints "The next card you play this phase costs [3] less." R119 quotes it as "this turn" and lists the charge as cleared in E.startTurn, and a 45-hybrids-ld-b test title says "this turn". Another test in the same file (the ERRATA one) shows the charge already ending at a mid-turn phase boundary, so the engine seems to follow the card. The title and the ruling text assert the superseded wording. Suspected test/register problem; not checked against the engine.
- <a id="F-U04-2"></a>**F-U04-2** An Ambush ignores imposed and "cards" cost modifiers (Arbiter of Armistice, Vengeance), though it is a card played (CT-243). Rule 111.10e. R129 counts an Ambush as a card being played, and Arbiter of Armistice ("Cards played during battle gain [Pay 2 life]") and Vengeance ("Cards your opponents play during battle gain '[Sacrifice a unit]'") print the noun "Cards". Measured by the round-1 verifier: an Ambush played under Arbiter of Armistice pays no life, while a spell card in the same spot is billed 2 life; doAmbush pays only the Ambush line's mana and never consults the card-play cost layer. R122 records the exclusion as an undecided future decision, so this is a divergence from the printed literal, not from a settled ruling. (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.) Also found as F-U04-3, F-U04-4.
- <a id="F-U04-3"></a>**F-U04-3** An Ambush ignores imposed "cards played" costs (Arbiter of Armistice, Vengeance) (CT-243). Rule 111.10e. doAmbush pays only the Ambush line's mana and never consults lifeToPlay/unitsToPlay, so a card played as an Ambush during battle pays no [Pay 2 life] under Arbiter of Armistice and no [Sacrifice a unit] under an opponent's Vengeance, although R129 rules an Ambush is a card being played and both cards print the noun "Cards". R122 records this as a deliberate, still-open decision, so it is a divergence from the printed literal rather than from a settled ruling. (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.)
- <a id="F-U04-4"></a>**F-U04-4** An Ambush escapes imposed costs on "cards played" (Arbiter of Armistice) (CT-243). Rule 111.10e. Arbiter prints "Cards played during battle gain [Pay 2 life]". R129 makes an Ambush a card being played, and Manual p.40 says you "play cards as an ambush". But the Ambush path never consults the cost-mod layer, so an Ambush under Arbiter pays no life (measured). R122 calls this deliberate, pending a future decision.
- <a id="F-U05-1"></a>**F-U05-1** Spells carry power and toughness values in printed.json that the cards do not print (CT-244). Rule 206.2. Spells print no stats (stats mark a unit, Rulebook 2023 p.3), but the oracle transcription has power and toughness fields on spell rows and the extractor copies them: 91 of 138 spells in printed.json have non-zero values (Arc Lightning 1/3, Spectrogenesis 4/5, Interdiction Rift 4/3 in the oracle). Suspected harmless; check that no engine or UI path reads a spell's power or toughness (an "Everything is Deadly" reach onto spells, a copy of a spell, Unaware reading printed stats, a card-stats or search surface). If none does, zero them at extraction so nothing can start to.
- <a id="F-U05-2"></a>**F-U05-2** 393-raq-mods Borrower/Reconfigure test is vacuous: Reconfigure is never castable in its setup (CT-240). Rule 208.5. The test guards the RAQ answer that a Borrower of Forms that copied an [Augment] unit is not a first target of Reconfigure, but wraps every assertion in `if (legalActions(...) offers Reconfigure)`. The verifier measured that branch as never taken with the test own setup (no real [Augment] unit is available as a first target, so Reconfigure is not castable), so the test asserts nothing. Add a real [Augment] unit to the setup and drop the `if`, so the play is required and the refusal is asserted; a verifier probe (not committed) did exactly that and passed.
- <a id="F-U06-1"></a>**F-U06-1** Wake the Dead plays a spell unit out of a bin without casting its spell (CT-245). Rule 303.9. R165 rules that Wake the Dead's "Play up to two units" is a real play, and the Hooba-Pon RAQ says playing a spell unit means its spell part happens and the body arrives only if the spell resolves. R165 itself records, under "Left open", that Wake the Dead spawns a spell unit's body and skips the spell. Nothing later in the register or the ledgers closes it. Suspected still live; a test should play a spell unit (Leaping Lillik, Spawntender) through Wake the Dead and assert that its spell effect happens. The verifier measured it (round 1 probe: Jelly played from a bin by Wake the Dead): the body arrives, no target is asked, no spell-played event fires, and the victim stays 7/5. Affects rule 303.5 and rule 303.6 too. Also found as F-U06-3, F-U06-4, F-U14-3, F-U14-6, F-U14-7.
- <a id="F-U06-2"></a>**F-U06-2** Borrower-of-Forms copy test never runs its Download half (CT-240). Rule 304.6. 393-raq-mods 'RAQ Borrower of Forms: copying a Robot token makes a nontoken unit, which Download cannot take' wraps its Download assertion in if (plays.length). The only token on the board is the defender's own Robot (the attacker is a nontoken spawn('Unit Token')), so Download is never offered (the verifier measured plays.length = 0) and the 'Download cannot take' half is vacuous. The test should give Download a real target token and assert the Borrower is not offered, failing if Download is not playable.
- <a id="F-U06-3"></a>**F-U06-3** Wake the Dead plays a spell unit from a bin without its spell part (CT-245). Rule 303.9. Wake the Dead ('Play up to two units in any bin…') offers spell units (isUnitCard) but spawns their bodies directly: the spell part never happens, nothing goes on the stack, no 'spellPlayed' fires and nothing can negate it. The designer (RAQ Hooba-Pon thread) rules that a spell unit played via 'play a unit' casts its spell and spawns only if it resolves. Probe: Jelly from A's bin, victim stays 7/5, no target asked. digital-rules R165 lists it as 'Left open, and filed rather than fixed'.
- <a id="F-U06-4"></a>**F-U06-4** A spell unit played by Wake the Dead skips its spell part and is not a played spell (CT-245). Rule 303.9. Wake the Dead 'plays' units from a bin via spawnUnit(asPlay) inline: a spell unit (Jelly) arrives with no stack item, no target, no spell effect and no spellPlayed event, so Origon/Riftbreaker/'play a spell' watchers never see it. Designer (Hooba-Pon RAQ) and Manual p.43 say a played spell unit casts its spell and is a spell. Already filed as open in R165 (known; engineDiffers F-U06-1). Measured by probe u06-r2-probes.test.ts.
- <a id="F-U07-1"></a>**F-U07-1** Biomass Devourer test title and comments still assert a stolen unit dies to its OWNER's bin (CT-235). Rule 405.3. R250 reversed this: a dying unit goes to its controller's bin. The 26-metal-a test is titled and commented for the owner's bin, but its assertions pass either way: the thief's bin ends with one copy and the owner's with none whichever bin received the dead card. So the title states superseded law and the test cannot tell the two apart. Retitle it and assert that the controller's bin received the dead copy.
- <a id="F-U07-2"></a>**F-U07-2** Two test titles disagree about a token being cached (CT-235). Rule 410.5c. 36-cache-prophecy says a token cached from play "is erased, not cached". 35-rot-debt-trash (R69) says it "visits the cache and is erased out of it". Both assert the same end state, so neither can fail on the visit, but the 36 title states the pre-R69 model.
- <a id="F-U07-3"></a>**F-U07-3** Abyssal Evocation timing test is still titled OPEN after R157 §12 ruled it (CT-238). Rule 405.9. R96 left open whether a bin-played card obeys its printed timing. R157 §12 (owner) answered: a bin-play grant does not waive printed timing ("Already correct — Abyssal Evocation, Writhing Host."). The test and its comment still call the question open and say the assertion "flips" if the owner rules otherwise. Also found as F-U14-4, F-U21-1.
- <a id="F-U07-4"></a>**F-U07-4** Two R208 test titles assert law that R219 reversed (cost-erased mods and the erased pile) (CT-235). Rule 407.2. R219 rules that a mod erased off a living host goes to the erased pile (Slag Spewer's cost, Suppression Field). The 178 test titles still say "Q3 is OPEN" and "the pile is untouched". The assertions may have been updated without the titles; check them. Also found as F-U16-1.
- <a id="F-U07-5"></a>**F-U07-5** Glossary Glimpse row says an expired glimpse card is still moddable; R303 says it is not (CT-231). Rule 403.5. Our Glimpse row ends "public, targetable, and still moddable out of the zone at full price". R303 refuses grafting and augmenting from an expired glimpse ("an expired glimpse is not a graft, not an augment, not anything"), and the Cache row of the same glossary agrees with R303. Test 177 does not catch it. Fix the Glimpse row. Also found as F-U18-2.
- <a id="F-U07-6"></a>**F-U07-6** Engine trashes a dying {Unstable} body via the bin; print and Caleb say it never enters the bin (CT-246). Rule 405.5. Per R137 the engine pushes a dying {Unstable} card into the bin, trashes it there, then sweeps it to the erased pile. The printed reminder ("If they would enter a bin, erase them instead.") and Caleb's glossary line in R145 make it a replacement for entering the bin, which would mean no trash. Under the authority order rule 405.5 states the printed reading. A divergence, not necessarily a bug: it is open as D-U07-3 and depends on the owner's answer there. Also found as F-U07-10, F-U07-11, F-U18-1, F-U18-3.
- <a id="F-U07-7"></a>**F-U07-7** A stolen unit erased from play is filed on its OWNER's erased pile, not its controller's (CT-229). Rule 400.4. R262 ("All four follow control") corrected R172 item 3, and every other route (bin, hand, cache, a mod erased off a host, an {Unstable} death's sweep) files the card under the controller. Erasing a unit from play still emits the erased event with the owner's seat, so a stolen unit erased by Banishment or Celestial Purge lands on its owner's erased pile. Measured by the round-1 verifier probe; test 246 covers only the mod route. (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.) Also found as F-U07-9, F-REG-1.
- <a id="F-U07-8"></a>**F-U07-8** The R296 §5 recycle test is titled for constructed but never builds a constructed game (CT-241). Rule 408.2e. The title says "constructed gives each seat its own pile; shared and draft share one". The body asserts the harness is NOT constructed and checks only the shared pile, so the per-seat constructed pile is untested by the suite. Add a constructed case (the round-1 verifier probe shows one).
- <a id="F-U07-9"></a>**F-U07-9** eraseFromPlay files a stolen unit on its OWNER's erased pile (CT-229). Rule 400.4. E.eraseFromPlay emits the erased event with seat: u.owner, so a stolen unit erased from play (Banishment, Celestial Purge) is recorded on its owner's erased pile. R262 ("All four follow control") superseded R172 item 3; every other route (bin, hand, cache, eraseMod, an Unstable death's sweep) uses the controller. (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.)
- <a id="F-U07-10"></a>**F-U07-10** Unstable card dying from play is binned and trashed before erasure (documented owner divergence from the designer) (CT-246). Rule 405.5. R137 has an Unstable unit that dies enter the bin, be trashed, then be erased; Caleb (2025-04-08) and the printed reminder say it is erased INSTEAD of entering the bin. Recorded on purpose in R137, so not a regression — listed because the brief asks for any engine/designer contradiction.
- <a id="F-U07-11"></a>**F-U07-11** A dying {Unstable} card enters the bin and is trashed before being erased (CT-246). Rule 405.5. disposeToBin pushes an Unstable card into the bin, fires died(to:'bin') and noteTrashed, then sweeps it to the erased pile. The printed reminder ('If they would enter a bin, erase them instead.') and Caleb 2025-04-08 ('they just get erased instead of ending up in the bin') say it never enters the bin, so no trash should happen. This is a deliberate, recorded owner divergence (R137, still current); listed because the engine contradicts print and the designer.
- <a id="F-U08-1"></a>**F-U08-1** Resource, haste and deployment steps run simultaneously and hidden instead of initiative player first, then non-initiative player (CT-247). Rule 501.4. Print (Manual p.27 legend for 1v1, Rulebook 2023 p.5, Manual p.20) has the initiative player take the resource step and the haste step (and deployment) first and the non-initiative player after, seeing what was done. The engine runs these as hidden simultaneous segments: both seats act at once, interleaved, and the non-initiative player never gets the information print gives them. The verifier measured it: the non-initiative seat activated a resource, finished the resource step and played a haste card before the initiative seat acted. Initiative-first order holds in battle only. The draft-step sync is the separate finding F-U08-4. (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.) Also found as F-U09-3.
- <a id="F-U08-2"></a>**F-U08-2** Prophecy timing test title says prophesying is illegal in the haste step without the R277 exception (CT-235). Rule 504.9. 36-cache-prophecy's title states that prophesying is illegal in planning, the haste step and battle, unqualified. R277 later made a banner whose condition ends in [Haste] prophesiable in the haste step. The test uses an unmarked banner, so its assertions still hold, but the title states the pre-R277 law. Retitle it "an UNMARKED banner…" and point at 257.
- <a id="F-U08-3"></a>**F-U08-3** Test comments and assertion messages still say the haste step opens only when someone holds a haste card (CT-235). Rule 504.5. R224/R228 made the haste step open every turn and deleted the predicate that skipped it. Several test comments and assertion messages still say the step opens because a seat holds a payable haste card, and util.ts documents skipHasteStep with the reversed R18 rule. The assertions pass either way (the step is always open), so the messages mislead readers about current law. Reword them.
- <a id="F-U08-4"></a>**F-U08-4** Planning steps do not sync: a seat that has drafted starts its resource step while the other still drafts (CT-248). Rule 501.4a. Print says turns sync up at the end of each step and the draft step is complete once all players have passed their pack. The engine gates the resource step on the acting seat's own draft (and, in constructed, its own recycle of 2) only, so a seat that has committed its draft may activate, recycle and even finish its resource step while the other seat is still drafting. The verifier measured it in a live draft. The hidden plan segment keeps the early start out of the other seat's view, so the observable effect may be nil; either sync the step or ratify the early start as a digital convention. (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.)
- <a id="F-U09-1"></a>**F-U09-1** 35-rot test title asserts that deployment has no priority, which R286 amended (CT-235). Rule 507.5. The test is named 'deployment opens no priority window' and asserts priority === null, which is R38's clause. R286 gives each seat priority over its own deployment stack, so the test pins the unbuilt state (CT-185) under a title that reads as current law. The rot half (rot cannot be responded to) is still right. Retitle it to the rot claim, or tie it to CT-185 so it flips when the deployment stop is built.
- <a id="F-U09-2"></a>**F-U09-2** The R11 regroup test claims an exact sequence but asserts only the end state (CT-241). Rule 506.2. 05-rulings 'R11: regroup runs its exact sequence' checks that each of the five regroup effects happened, after regroup. It never observes their order, so a reordering of startRegroup would stay green. Either drop 'exact sequence' from the title, or add an observation that can tell the orders apart, such as a trigger that reads damage or formation membership mid-regroup.
- <a id="F-U09-3"></a>**F-U09-3** Deployment is simultaneous in the engine; the printed rules have the initiative team deploy first (CT-247). Rule 507.3. The printed rule (Manual p.38, Rulebook 2023 p.5) has the initiative team deploy first and the non-initiative team after it. Measured: at the start of deployment, before the initiative player is done, the non-initiative player is offered playCard and doneDeploying, and the play is accepted. This is the deliberate house rule (simultaneous hidden deployment) recorded as D-U09-1; filed so the owner decides which side is law, not as a request to change the engine. (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.)
- <a id="F-U10-1"></a>**F-U10-1** R27 counts 'my formation' by OWNER, not by control (CT-236). Rule 602.6h. R27 words Embermaw Fledgling's X ('the number of attacking units in my formation') as the surviving units its controller OWNS in the battle columns. A unit its controller controls but does not own (raised from the enemy bin by Wake the Dead, or lent by Uglk; R250 makes such units ordinary allies) attacks in the same formation and should be counted. If the engine counts by owner, it undercounts. Suspected from the ruling's wording only; a probe should attack with a borrowed unit beside Embermaw Fledgling and read X. Re-checked: the engine counts by control (Embermaw Fledgling reads u.controller === self.controller), so nothing undercounts; what stands is the ruling text saying "owns", filed with the stale register text.
- <a id="F-U10-2"></a>**F-U10-2** Throwing Boulder's 'adjacent enemy' test cannot show what its title claims (CT-241). Rule 603.2a. 18-earth-c 'R77: an ALLY is required — an adjacent enemy does not unlock it' sets up the enemy as a blocker facing the Boulder. Under R75 adjacency (the three positions inside the unit's own formation) a facing blocker is not adjacent at all, so the Boulder has no adjacent unit of any kind and the test passes whether or not the gate checks that the neighbour is an ALLY. Either the test is vacuous, or the engine treats the facing enemy as adjacent, which R75 does not allow. A real guard needs an enemy unit inside the Boulder's own formation, for example a unit stolen into it, or a probe of the adjacency query with a facing blocker.
- <a id="F-U10-3"></a>**F-U10-3** Defending formation adjacency ignores unblocked columns between blockers (CT-249). Rule 603.2. adjacentInFormation builds the defender grid from the sorted block keys, so blockers on attacking columns 1 and 3 (column 2 unblocked) are treated as left/right neighbours. Inspiration then buffs across the gap (round-1 verifier probe on rule 603.2). The Manual makes blocking position matter for adjacency, and a blocking column is keyed to the attacking column it faces, so the unblocked column is a gap. The engine's own comment calls its reading an approximation. (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.) Also found as F-U11-3, F-U11-4.
- <a id="F-U10-6"></a>**F-U10-6** A lone Hooba-Lin killed under its attack trigger makes its 1/1 outside the formation (CT-250). Rule 602.6f. Hooba-Lin attacks alone and is killed with its attack trigger on the stack, before blocks. Its column collapses away, the attacker is offered no position, and the 1/1 is created outside any formation. The designer's [Solved] answer names Hooba-Lin among the effects that 'will remember they were in formation and will work fine', with no exception for a lone attacker; rule 602.6f states that and 602.6k excepts it. The engine applies R75's 'no living unit, no slots' instead. It may be an unruled edge rather than a bug (D-U10-6). (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.) Also found as F-U10-7.
- <a id="F-U10-7"></a>**F-U10-7** A source that left play places nothing when its remembered formation is now empty (CT-250). Rule 602.6f. R325/RAQ: Hooba-Lin killed with its attack trigger on the stack "will remember [it was] in formation and will work fine". With a lone Hooba-Lin attacking, formationSeatOf returns its last-known seat but formationSlots returns no slot for a grid with no living unit, so the 1/1 is created outside the formation ("no open position in the formation"). Applies to every R75 placer reading a dead source (Hooba-Bot, Hooba-Pon, Hooba-Lin).
- <a id="F-U11-1"></a>**F-U11-1** R72 still says the client's block build is not re-seeded when the attack line closes, but rekeyBuild and its tests exist (CT-236). Rule 605.1c. R72's section '⚠ The client's in-progress block assignment is index-keyed too' ends 'the client should re-seed its preview when b.columns.length changes, and it does not yet'. The client now has rekeyBuild (client/ui/formation.ts), and client/ui/test/55-ui-formation.test.ts pins it ('rekeyBuild: a collapse to the LEFT drags the block along with its attacker'). The ⚠ looks resolved and the ruling text is stale. A register fix (mark the ⚠ resolved), not an engine bug; suspected only, since the drafter did not run the tests. Also found as F-U24-2.
- <a id="F-U11-2"></a>**F-U11-2** R87's open client item (no reachability row for a counterattack with spell tokens) appears done (CT-236). Rule 606.5a. R87's '⚠ Open for the client' says 75-ui-reachability's facetsOf does not tell a declareBlocks that carries spell tokens from one that does not, so the rider has no reachability row, and asks for a declareBlocks:spellTokens facet and ledger entry. client/ui/test/75-ui-reachability.test.ts now has both. The ⚠ in the register is stale. A register fix, not an engine bug.
- <a id="F-U11-3"></a>**F-U11-3** Blocking-formation adjacency ignores empty blocking columns (CT-249). Rule 606.1f. E.adjacentInFormation builds the defender's grid from the block keys sorted and compressed, so two blockers with an unblocked (empty) blocking column between them read as neighbours. R75 defines adjacency by grid position and the Manual makes the defending formation's empty columns real. Measured by the verifier's probe: blocks {0:[d0], 2:[d2]} gives adjacentInFormation(d0) = [d2]. The engine comment flags it as an approximation.
- <a id="F-U11-4"></a>**F-U11-4** Blockers either side of an empty blocking column are read as adjacent (CT-249). Rule 606.1f. formationGrid(defender) compacts the sorted block keys, so adjacentInFormation/adjacentSlots treat blockers on columns 1 and 3 (column 2 unblocked) as neighbours. The printed definition (adjacent to left/right neighbours, formations locked in position, side-blocks placed 'for adjacency matters cards') puts an empty slot between them. The code comment admits the approximation. Already flagged by the rule as engineDiffers F-U11-3.
- <a id="F-U12-1"></a>**F-U12-1** A redirected Piercing leftover is offered to other replacement holders (CT-228). Rule 608.8c. The designer: Piercing combat damage redirected into Oorblak is dealt to Oorblak up to its lethal damage and the leftover goes to the player, because 'replacement effects only apply once in an effect'; the register states the claim as 'not redirected again'. The pilot verifier measured that the engine stops only the SAME replacement from applying again: a second Oorblak or a Blightsea Polyp in the region takes the leftover, and only a holder with a higher entity id sees it (a lower-id Polyp consumes the whole hit first). The rule states the ruling (no further redirection). Also found as F-U15-3, F-U15-5, F-U20-6.
- <a id="F-U12-2"></a>**F-U12-2** 02-combat test title asserts the superseded no-priority-between-sub-steps law (CT-230). Rule 608.3b. 02-combat.test.ts 'R3/Swift: swift column deals damage first, no priority between sub-steps' names R3's second clause, which R295 amended: a split damage step opens a priority window between sub-steps. The pilot verifier's probe found this test's own board stops at that window (damageSubs Swift and normal, step damageWindow); its assertions are made there and prove only the Swift strike. Retitle it. Also found as F-U12-3.
- <a id="F-U12-3"></a>**F-U12-3** 239 'R3 STILL STANDS' asserts at the Swift window, before the normal sub-step runs (CT-230). Rule 608.3e. 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts 'R3 STILL STANDS' claims the Swift-killed Sprite dealt nothing in the normal sub-step and that only the trigger queue waits. Its board is a split step (a Swift blocker against a normal attacker), so after pass/pass/answerElections it is paused at the Swift/normal window: the 'dealt NOTHING in the normal sub-step' assertion is taken before the normal sub-step runs, and in a split step the trigger queue resolves at that window rather than waiting until after combat (R295). The test does not assert its title.
- <a id="F-U13-1"></a>**F-U13-1** R36 (a lone sent counterattacker auto-forms) is unmarked, but its guard was flipped to assert the opposite (CT-251). Rule 610.4e. R36 says that when a round-2 counterattack pool holds exactly one unit and no ridable spell token, the only-unit formation is auto-declared as a forced action. On 2026-08-24 (a decisions-for-the-player audit) test 32 was flipped: its comment says the auto-declare branch is deleted, and it asserts forcedAction is null and that both attacking and declining are legal. No ruling records the reversal, and R36's heading carries no reversal mark, so the register still presents R36 as current. Register fix: write the reversing ruling (or mark R36) and point R36's heading at it. Also found as F-U23-4, F-U23-7, F-U23-8.
- <a id="F-U13-2"></a>**F-U13-2** 21-fixes test title claims round 2 is restricted to sent counterattackers but only tests the no-send case (CT-241). Rule 610.4b. The test 'round 2 after a real round-1 battle still restricts to the sent counterattackers' declares blocks with no send and asserts only that the battle is over (no round 2). It never reaches a round 2 in which a unit that stayed home is refused as an attacker, so the restriction its title names is not asserted by it. The restriction is shown elsewhere only indirectly (test 32 asserts the attacker pool equals the sent unit). A guard that tries to attack in round 2 with a unit that was not sent would make the title true.
- <a id="F-U14-1"></a>**F-U14-1** A graft trigger with no legal target goes on the stack and fizzles instead of not being put on the stack (CT-252). Rule 702.8b. The designer says a graft composite whose targeted part has no legal target cannot be put on the stack. The RAQ register's own note says the engine reaches the same visible result (no Poison) by putting the item on the stack and fizzling it under R86. Then the opponent gets a priority window, and the item can be taxed or negated, though it should never exist. Suspected; not checked against the engine. Also found as F-U17-7, F-U17-9.
- <a id="F-U14-2"></a>**F-U14-2** The engine appears to pass priority to the other player after every action, so a player cannot hold priority (CT-253). Rule 703.2a. The Manual says a player who acts may keep priority and take further actions before passing. R250 and R198 describe the engine handing priority to the other seat whenever an item is pushed. If so, a player can never stack two of their own actions before the opponent may respond (the Manual names Burst as the usual exception, and Burst is handled separately). Suspected from ruling text only; Annex D may record a digital convention that settles it. Measured by the U14 tester: after a battle cast of Luminous Arc, priority is on the other seat, not the caster (pushItem hands it to other(controller)). (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.)
- <a id="F-U14-3"></a>**F-U14-3** Units played by Wake the Dead and The Bonesculptor spawn in place, never on the stack, and a spell unit they play skips its spell (CT-245). Rule 701.4. R198 rules that a card played during a resolution is played and goes on the stack, where it can be responded to. R207 records that the spawn route used for cards that print "play" (Wake the Dead, The Bonesculptor) predates R198 and still spawns the unit in place, so nobody can answer it. R165 records that a spell unit raised by Wake the Dead does not cast its spell, though a played spell unit's spell part should happen (RAQ, Hooba-Pon). Suspected still open. Verifier probe (U14 round 1): a unit Wake the Dead plays in battle is in play at once and never on the stack. Affects rule 703.5 too. Round 2 probe: onStack=false, inPlay=true; the Wake the Dead comment calls this "the standing playInline approximation", but playInline itself now pushes in battle. (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.)
- <a id="F-U14-4"></a>**F-U14-4** A test title still marks as OPEN whether a bin-played card obeys its printed timing (CT-238). Rule 702.2a. R96 shipped the restrictive answer (printed timing applies) and flagged the question OPEN. R157 §12 later answered it the same way ("Already correct — Abyssal Evocation"). The test title and R96 heading still present it as open.
- <a id="F-U14-5"></a>**F-U14-5** Bloomcaster does not hear its own play (CT-254). Rule 701.1e. R26 (current) says Bloomcaster's "Whenever you play a unit" fires on its own arrival when played normally. The verifier measured no 1/1 when Bloomcaster is played from hand: the card listens on cardPlayed from holders in play, and Bloomcaster is on the stack when its own play fires. Either the engine regressed when Bloomcaster moved to cardPlayed (R129/R165), or R26 is stale and should be superseded (D-U14-11). (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.) Also found as F-U14-8.
- <a id="F-U14-6"></a>**F-U14-6** Wake the Dead / The Bonesculptor plays never reach the stack (CT-245). Rule 703.5. R198 rules that a card played mid-resolution is played and goes on the stack, respondable. Wake the Dead ({Battle}, "Play up to two units ... now") spawns its units with spawnUnit(asPlay) inside its own resolution: no stack item, no window, not negatable (probe: unit in play immediately).
- <a id="F-U14-7"></a>**F-U14-7** Wake the Dead and The Bonesculptor play units mid-resolution with no stack item (CT-245). Rule 703.5. R198 (and the designer on Tides) says a card played during a resolution goes on the stack and is respondable once the resolution finishes. Wake the Dead and The Bonesculptor still spawn the played unit in place (spawnUnit asPlay), so nobody can respond to or negate it. Probe: onStack=false, inPlay=true. The Wake the Dead comment calls this "the standing playInline approximation", but playInline itself now pushes in battle.
- <a id="F-U14-8"></a>**F-U14-8** Bloomcaster does not trigger on its own play (contradicts R26) (CT-254). Rule 701.1e. R26 says Bloomcaster's "Whenever you play a unit" fires on its own arrival. The trigger listens on cardPlayed, which fires at commit while Bloomcaster is on the stack, so it never hears itself. Probe measured 0 tokens. The card file comment still claims "playing Bloomcaster itself still makes a 1/1".
- <a id="F-U14-9"></a>**F-U14-9** Cards that re-check their target restriction by hand let an earlier part make a later part’s target illegal mid-resolution (CT-232). Rule 704.5a. The rule (R324’s encoding) says target legality is judged once, as the item begins to resolve, so an earlier part of the same item cannot make a later part’s target illegal. markIllegalTargets does judge once, but Minor Kraken (and, by the same pattern, Throw off a Cliff and Leave None Pure) re-checks its printed restriction inside its own run. Measured by the U14 tester: a composite whose first part puts 11 +1/+1 counters on a 0/2 and whose second part is Minor Kraken’s recall does not recall it (control without the counters: recalled). (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.)
- <a id="F-U15-1"></a>**F-U15-1** The Bonesculptor's bin-play permission is built as an activated ability, so it reaches the stack and can be negated (CT-255). Rule 707.10. R165 and R168 both say "You may play one unit with no abilities from your bin each deployment" is a standing permission that no one should be able to answer, and both record that the engine builds it as a free bounded activated ability that reaches the stack, where Containment Protocol can negate it. Both left it open ("filed rather than fixed"). The round-1 verifier's probe confirmed it still resolves as an activated item. Also found as F-U15-4.
- <a id="F-U15-2"></a>**F-U15-2** A RAQ register note still warns that the Wispweaver Nectar Ridge guard may be green for the wrong reason (CT-236). Rule 707.4a. The RAQ register note on claim 1355633589890584636#1 says the Infernal Wispweaver guard is "green partly for the wrong reason given the Sandstone defect" and should be re-checked when the Sandstone case is fixed. The note on #0 says the Sandstone case was a fixture error and the engine was already right, so the warning is stale or the re-check is still owed. A test-and-register problem, not an engine bug.
- <a id="F-U15-3"></a>**F-U15-3** Two Oorblaks both redirect one combat hit (CT-228). Rule 708.4a. replaceCombatDamage offers the damage to every holder in turn; with Piercing, the leftover the first Oorblak lets through is redirected again by a second Oorblak. The round-1 verifier's probe: 10 Piercing into two 2/4 Oorblaks, the player loses 2 and both die. Designer: 'replacement effects only apply once in an effect'; R104: a thing can only be replaced once. Expected: one Oorblak absorbs 4, the player loses 6. Same defect as F-U12-1 (there with a Blightsea Polyp); merge when ticketing.
- <a id="F-U15-4"></a>**F-U15-4** The Bonesculptor's permission is an activated ability (CT-255). Rule 707.10. 'You may play one unit with no abilities from your bin each deployment' is built as a free bounded activated ability and resolves as an activated item (probe), where R165/R168 say a permission should simply be true and not reach the stack. Already filed in R165 'Left open'.
- <a id="F-U15-5"></a>**F-U15-5** A second combat-damage redirect absorbs what the first passed through (two Oorblaks) (CT-228). Rule 708.4a. replaceCombatDamage offers the leftover of one holder's replacement to the next holder, so two Oorblaks both absorb a single Piercing hit (D at 28, both die) where the designer says a replacement applies once per event (D at 24, one dies). Already flagged by the rule as engineDiffers.
- <a id="F-U16-1"></a>**F-U16-1** Two R208 test titles assert the erased-pile behaviour R219 reversed (CT-235). Rule 712.1c. In 178-played-item-and-erased-mods, the Slag Spewer test is titled "an erase paid as a COST still announces itself with info — Q3 is OPEN" and the Suppression Field test "... and the pile is untouched". Both titles state R208's held behaviour (a mod erased off a living host files nothing on the erased pile), which R219 reversed. Both bodies now assert the R219 behaviour: the erased mod is on the pile. The titles say the opposite of what the tests check.
- <a id="F-U16-2"></a>**F-U16-2** A copy-layer test title still calls stripping a veto (CT-235). Rule 712.7. The 44-hybrids-ld-a test "R118: R62 suppression is a veto ABOVE copy" and its message "R62 sits ABOVE layer 0" describe R62's veto, which R328 reversed (stripping is applied in timestamp order). The test strips after the copy is made, so its assertions still hold under R328, but no test pins a copy that begins after a strip (see D-U16-6), and the title asserts superseded law.
- <a id="F-U16-3"></a>**F-U16-3** A unit stripped by a continuous effect (Monke, Transmogrifant) keeps applying its own static abilities (CT-256). Rule 712.1a. Transmogrifant and Monke make other units "lose all attributes and abilities", and R62 says a static is an ability, but static-vs-static resolves in one pass that skips only a holder with the one-time stamp. The verifier's probe measured a 1/1 token at 3/5 with Sandstone Defender under Transmogrifant, where the printed text gives 3/3. R62 justifies the one pass only by the mutual case (two Monkes); the one-sided case falls out of the same shortcut. (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.) Also found as F-U16-5, F-U16-7.
- <a id="F-U16-4"></a>**F-U16-4** Tough augmented onto a printed-Balanced unit: the engine balances first, the Manual's "augmented onto" sentence doubles first (CT-257). Rule 709.4b. Manual p.42: "if Tough is augmented onto a Balanced unit ... it will have its defense doubled, then its stats balanced." The engine (R19's own call: printed attributes before mod attributes) gives the reverse: the verifier's probe measured Child of Aether (2/0 Balanced) with a Tough augment at 2/4, where that sentence gives 2/2. The same answer's last sentence ("applied to") gives balanced, then doubled, so this waits on the owner's reading (D-U16-1). Also found as F-U16-6, F-U19-5.
- <a id="F-U16-5"></a>**F-U16-5** A unit silenced by a continuous stripper (Monke, Transmogrifant) keeps radiating its own static abilities (CT-256). Rule 712.1a. Measured by the U16 probe u16-probes.test.ts (Transmogrifant case). Printed Monke/Transmogrifant make other units "lose all attributes and abilities", and R62 itself says "a static is an ability", but E.staticsFor only skips a holder whose own entity stamp is set (textStrippedShallow). So a Sandstone Defender under Transmogrifant still gives +0/+2: probe measured a 1/1 token at 3/5 instead of 3/3. R62 justifies one-pass resolution only for the mutual case (two Monkes); the non-mutual case falls out of the same shortcut.
- <a id="F-U16-6"></a>**F-U16-6** Tough augmented onto a printed-Balanced unit: engine balances first, the Manual p.42 first clause doubles first (CT-257). Rule 709.4b. Manual p.42: "if Tough is augmented onto a Balanced unit ... it will have its defense doubled, then its stats balanced." The engine (R19 ⚠ engine call: printed attrs before mod attrs) gives the reverse: Child of Aether (2/0 Balanced) augmented with Rampart Guardian reads 2/4, where the Manual clause gives 2/2. The same Manual answer then says "applied to" gives balanced-then-doubled, so the printed text contradicts itself; it needs an owner/designer call. Not in the R register.
- <a id="F-U16-7"></a>**F-U16-7** A unit stripped of abilities by a continuous static keeps radiating its own statics (CT-256). Rule 712.1a. Transmogrifant prints that your other units 'lose all attributes and abilities', but the engine's static walks (staticsFor/textStrippedShallow) read only the entity's own suppressed stamp. So Sandstone Defender under Transmogrifant still gives +0/+2: a 1/1 token measures 3/5, not 3/3. This contradicts the printed text, not a current R-ruling (R62/R328 describe the one-pass behaviour), so it is an engine-vs-printed divergence. The rule records it as F-U16-3. (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.)
- <a id="F-U17-1"></a>**F-U17-1** Return to Nature files each erased mod on its OWNER's erased pile; R262 says the erased pile follows control (CT-258). Rule 720.9. R262 (the owner: "All four follow control") moved the erased pile of a mod erased off a living host from mod.owner to mod.controller, and a mod's controller is its host's controller (R244). The 17-earth-b test puts the opponent's mod on P's host, runs Return to Nature, and asserts the mod lands on the OPPONENT's (owner's) pile; the 178 test's message says the same. Either Return to Nature does not go through the controller-filing path, or the test asserts superseded law. Measured by the round-1 verifier: Return to Nature groups its erased mods byOwner and files under m.owner (alreadyFiled), so a mod owned by D on a host controlled by A was filed on D's pile, while E.eraseMod files under mod.controller. (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.) Also found as F-U17-5, F-U17-8.
- <a id="F-U17-2"></a>**F-U17-2** Glossary Graft row says a cached card can be grafted only under a fulfilled prophecy, omitting a live glimpse (CT-231). Rule 720.5a. R303 (and R311) let a cached card be grafted or augmented under a live glimpse as well as a fulfilled prophecy, at the card's mana ignoring affinity. The Graft row of ui/glossary.ts says "or from cache, if a fulfilled prophecy paid for it", which omits the glimpse. Under R206 an omission is a wrong row. Fix the row's text; cite R303.
- <a id="F-U17-3"></a>**F-U17-3** 04-mods 'mods move with a stolen unit' test hand-assigns the controller and never checks the mods (CT-241). Rule 720.6e. The test claims the unit's controller controls its mods, but it changes control by assigning u.controller directly (which R148 says is a bug: a control change is E.giveControl), and asserts only that the host still has Flying, which is true whoever controls the mod. Its comment says no pool card changes control, which R112 and R148 list seven cards doing. Rewrite it through E.giveControl and assert the mod entity's controller.
- <a id="F-U17-4"></a>**F-U17-4** Return to Nature files TOKEN mods on the erased pile; R219 says a token mod erased off a living host is not filed (CT-259). Rule 720.9a. R219: "A token mod is not filed. R133: a token is not a card, and R65's pile is a list of cards." E.eraseMod (the cost route) honours it and files nothing for a token mod. Return to Nature files its own grouped erased line for every mod it erases off hosts that stay in play, token mods included; its own comment says so. Measured by the round-1 verifier: a Wraith token mod erased by Return to Nature is recorded on the erased pile. (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.) Also found as F-U17-6.
- <a id="F-U17-5"></a>**F-U17-5** Return to Nature files erased mods under the mod OWNER, not its controller (CT-258). Rule 720.9. R262 moved the R65 erased pile to follow control ('All four follow control — one rule, no seam'), and E.eraseMod files { seat: mod.controller }. Return to Nature files its own grouped 'erased' line byOwner (m.owner) and passes alreadyFiled, so on a stolen host the erased mod goes to the original owner's pile. Probe: mod owned by D, controlled by A → filed under D. (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.)
- <a id="F-U17-6"></a>**F-U17-6** Return to Nature files TOKEN mods on the erased pile (CT-259). Rule 720.9a. R219: 'A token mod is not filed. R133: a token is not a card, and R65's pile is a list of cards.' E.eraseMod honours it; Return to Nature's grouped line files every erased mod, token mods included. Probe: a Wraith token mod erased by Return to Nature is recorded on the erased pile.
- <a id="F-U17-7"></a>**F-U17-7** A graft trigger whose required target has no legal candidate still goes on the stack (CT-252). Rule 722.4e. Designer (RAQ 1410252965276684418#2): the composite 'can't be put on the stack unless you target such unit in your bin.' The engine pushes it ('→ stack') and lets it fizzle under R86, so it can be responded to and taxed while it sits there. The no-Poison outcome matches; the mechanism does not. Low severity. (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.)
- <a id="F-U17-8"></a>**F-U17-8** Return to Nature files erased mods under the mod OWNER, not the controller (CT-258). Rule 720.9. R262 moved the erased pile to follow control (eraseMod uses mod.controller), but Return to Nature files its own grouped erased line by m.owner and calls eraseMod with alreadyFiled, so a mod on a stolen host goes to the owner's pile.
- <a id="F-U17-9"></a>**F-U17-9** A graft composite with an untargetable required part is stacked and fizzles instead of never being stacked (CT-252). Rule 722.4e. Designer (RAQ 1410252965276684418#2): such a composite cannot be put on the stack. The engine pushes it (probe: 1 item on attack) and it fizzles whole under R86 — same final board, but an opponent gets a priority window and can respond to/negate an item that should not exist.
- <a id="F-U18-1"></a>**F-U18-1** Engine trashes a dying {Unstable} card in the bin; the printed reminder erases it instead of binning it (CT-246). Rule 801.2h. Under R137 the engine pushes a dying {Unstable} card into the bin, trashes it there (firing "when I am trashed" and the trash watchers, and raising the per-battle count), then sweeps it to the erased pile. The printed reminder replaces the bin entry with an erase, so under the authority order the card is never trashed. The same divergence as F-U07-6, seen from the trash rule; merge them in Stage D. A divergence pending the owner's answer to D-U18-1 / D-U07-3, not necessarily a bug.
- <a id="F-U18-2"></a>**F-U18-2** Glossary Glimpse row still says an expired glimpse card is moddable at full price (CT-231). Rule 801.9i. The player-facing Glimpse reminder in client/ui/glossary.ts ends "public, targetable, and still moddable out of the zone at full price". R303 (2026-09-20) made an expired glimpse refuse every verb, mods included, and the Cache row in the same file already says "once it lapses the card is inert". The two rows contradict each other on screen. A text fix in ours, not an engine change; test 177 cannot see it because the row cites R45/R190, which are live.
- <a id="F-U18-3"></a>**F-U18-3** A dying {Unstable} card is trashed before it is erased (CT-246). Rule 801.2h. The engine bins and trashes a printed- or granted-Unstable card that dies in play, then sweeps it to the erased pile (R137, a deliberate owner divergence). The printed reminder and a direct Caleb ruling put it in no bin, so no trash.
- <a id="F-U19-1"></a>**F-U19-1** Tough, Balanced and Inverted stay on in an interaction with a Pure card, against Pure's printed "ignore all other attributes" (CT-260). Rule 802.1n. R289 (and R61, as R289 reads it) keep the stat attributes Tough, Balanced and Inverted applying in a Pure pairing because "they are stat layers". Pure's printed reminder ignores all other attributes, and the Manual lists Tough as an attribute. Under the authority order the printed text wins (rule 802.1n; D-U19-2). Suspected engine behaviour: a Pure blocker facing a Tough unit is priced against the doubled defense. Measured by the round-1 verifier: a Pure source dealing 5 to Rampart Guardian leaves it alive as a Tough 0/8. Measured by the round-2 verifier: a Balanced 4/1 dealt 3 by a Pure source survives as a 4/4. (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.) Also found as F-U19-2.
- <a id="F-U19-2"></a>**F-U19-2** The combat Unaware collapse is said to survive Pure, while noncombat Pure switches Unaware off (CT-260). Rule 802.1n. R106 says the Unaware collapse of a combat exchange "survives {Pure}", because Unaware is a stat layer. R289 switches a Pure pairing's Unaware off outside combat, and Pure's printed reminder ignores all other attributes. The engine therefore appears to treat Unaware + Pure differently in combat and outside it, and the combat half contradicts the printed text (rule 802.1n; D-U19-2).
- <a id="F-U19-3"></a>**F-U19-3** Oorblak's combat-damage redirect doubles damage onto a Pure Vulnerable Oorblak (CT-227). Rule 802.11e. The pilot's round-2 probe (P5) gave Oorblak Pure and Vulnerable and redirected a non-Pure 3-power unblocked column into it: Oorblak was dealt 6 and died. R61 and R289 say a Pure recipient's own Vulnerable is off. The redirect is a damage commit in card code (R237 calls it "the fourth site") and appears not to read Pure. Exotic but reachable (Just a Unit is a Virus).
- <a id="F-U19-4"></a>**F-U19-4** 290 test titled for a Pure recipient's own Vulnerable makes the source Pure instead (CT-241). Rule 802.11e. 290-pure-outside-combat §2's title says "a Pure recipient's own Vulnerable is off too", but the test makes the SOURCE Pure and hits a non-Pure Vulnerable unit. No test guards a Pure recipient's own Vulnerable, which is the half F-U19-3 shows to fail on the Oorblak path.
- <a id="F-U19-5"></a>**F-U19-5** The engine balances a printed-Balanced unit before doubling an augment's Tough, against Manual p.42 (CT-257). Rule 802.1m. Manual p.42: Tough augmented onto a Balanced unit has its defense doubled, then its stats balanced. The engine follows R19's engine call (own printed attributes first, then augment-granted ones), so it balances first. Measured by the round-1 verifier: Child of Aether (printed Balanced, 2/0) augmented with Rampart Guardian (Tough) is a 2/4; the Manual makes it a 2/2. R19's premise that the Manual does not specify printed-vs-granted order is wrong for this pair. No test guards the printed-host case (rule 802.1m; D-U19-1). (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.)
- <a id="F-U20-1"></a>**F-U20-1** The Electric path is asked of the effect's controller, not the Electric source's controller (CT-226). Rule 802.17c. R4 (and R317) give the choice of the Electric path to the Electric source's controller. The orchestrator's known-divergence list and the pilot verifier record that the engine asks the effect's controller. Every Electric source in the pool today is a spell or a spell effect, so the two players coincide in every test; 05-rulings asserts the source's controller only in that coinciding case. The rule states the ruling. Round-1 verifier measured it: dealEffectDamageAll raises the electricPath decision for ctx.controller, while the Piercing split beside it already uses the source unit's controller (the probe for rule 802.17c). Also found as F-U20-5.
- <a id="F-U20-2"></a>**F-U20-2** Afflicting test title says the OWNER of the killed unit gains the rot; the card says its controller (CT-235). Rule 802.23a. Umbral Decay prints "those units' controllers gain a rot". The 42-dark-b test is titled "rots the owner of what it kills". In the test the owner and the controller are the same player, so it passes either way, and no test covers a stolen unit killed by an Afflicting source. Retitle the test, and add a case where controller and owner differ.
- <a id="F-U20-3"></a>**F-U20-3** Modular would be shared through a column if a unit ever printed it (CT-261). Rule 802.26h. The owner ruling (Caleb's "Modular is also special", in R294) is that Modular is not a column-shared attribute. R294 itself records that Modular is in the engine's shared attribute set and is harmless only because the one card that prints it is a spell. The round-1 verifier confirmed colAttrs would union it. Latent: no unit prints Modular today; 298 §5c guards the premise, not the non-sharing.
- <a id="F-U20-4"></a>**F-U20-4** Reaping never loses Reaping after drawing (printed second sentence not built) (CT-173). Rule 802.21c. Reaping's reminder says the source loses Reaping until regroup after drawing. R283 §2 says this is deliberately not built because every Reaping printer is a one-shot spell; the round-1 verifier confirmed nothing removes Reaping after a draw. Latent: becomes live the day a unit can carry Reaping. 263 §4 guards the premise. Re-checked: already open as CT-173, which records the clause as measured and deliberately not built (unreachable today).
- <a id="F-U20-5"></a>**F-U20-5** Electric path asked of the effect's controller, not the source's controller (CT-226). Rule 802.17c. dealEffectDamageAll raises the electricPath decision for ctx.controller. R4 and R317 give the choice to the Electric source's controller. They differ when a spell makes an opponent's unit the source (Battle, Fight). Measured by the probe for rule 802.17c. The Piercing split beside it already uses dealerSeat (the source unit's controller).
- <a id="F-U20-6"></a>**F-U20-6** Piercing excess redirected again by a second Oorblak (CT-228). Rule 802.16p. replaceCombatDamage offers each holder's leftover to the next replaceCombatDamageToPlayer holder. With two Oorblaks, 10 Piercing combat damage kills both and only 2 reach the player. The designer says 4 go into Oorblak and the other 6 reach the player, because a replacement applies only once. Measured by the probe for rule 802.16p.
- <a id="F-U21-1"></a>**F-U21-1** Test title still labels the bin-play timing question OPEN after a ruling answered it (CT-238). Rule 803.8c. A 12-fire-a test title marks "a bin-played card obeys its PRINTED timing" as an open question. R197 records that R157 §12 ruled a bin-play grant does not waive printed timing, which is what the test asserts. The behaviour is settled; only the title (and R96's own "OPEN" heading) still reads as undecided. A test-title fix, not an engine bug.
- <a id="F-U21-2"></a>**F-U21-2** Three test titles claim more than their tests assert (CT-241). Rule 803.8d. Each title names a behaviour the body never checks. The 12-fire-a Abyssal Evocation test says "until regroup" ends the stamp but never reaches regroup. The 403 R336 test says the Borrower dies to the bin but never kills it (26-metal-a's R336 test does). The R43 "One Battle Passes" title says both battles tick, but the test counts only one round. Each needs an assertion added or its title narrowed. These are test problems, not engine bugs: the round-1 verifier measured the engine and it agrees.
- <a id="F-U23-1"></a>**F-U23-1** Holding full control does not stop the deployment stack from resolving itself (CT-185). Rule D2.7a. R287 rules that while full control (Ctrl) is held, nothing resolves automatically, 'even during deployment'. R287 records that clause as not built: the deployment stack drains inside settle(), and the engine has no flag for the hold. Already filed by R287 as CT-185 (owner's call); listed here so the export's marker has a target. The verifier confirmed: the engine has no full-control flag, and CT-185 (a holdStack action) is still open. Also found as F-U23-6. Re-checked: already open as CT-185 (the holdStack action); no new ticket.
- <a id="F-U23-2"></a>**F-U23-2** The automatic pass is latched per state counter, which R245(b) rules out (CT-262). Rule D2.4. R245(b) rules that an automatic answer (it names the haste-step ready and the automatic pass) is latched by being unanswered, never by a state counter, because states keep arriving while an intent is outstanding. R258 says the automatic pass is latched once per actionCount via takeAutoPass, and test 70 [59] asserts that a new state number re-opens the latch. If a state with a new actionCount reaches a seat while its automatic pass is still outstanding, a second pass could go out and come back refused. The verifier confirmed it in the client: the haste ready was converted (hasteAutoOut), but the automatic pass still goes through takeAutoPass, keyed on actionCount. Also found as F-U23-5.
- <a id="F-U23-3"></a>**F-U23-3** The live action counter tells the opponent when you act inside every hidden simultaneous segment (CT-106). Rule D2.5e. A hidden simultaneous segment is meant to show nobody the other side's plays until everyone is done (R18). R236 measured that GameState.actionCount is served live to both seats and rises on every action, so a modified client sees when its opponent acts in the resource step, the haste step and deployment. The shipped client renders nothing from it. R236 names the fix (a per-seat action counter in the engine or rooms.ts) and leaves it as the owner's call. Pinned by 205 §3d. Also found as F-U24-3. Re-checked: already decided: CT-106 is wontfix by the owner (2026-08-29, "I am not worried about this"); no new ticket.
- <a id="F-U23-4"></a>**F-U23-4** R36 still stands in the register, but the engine removed the one-unit round-2 auto-declare (CT-251). Rule D1.2c. R36 rules that a round-2 counterattack pool of exactly one unit, with no spell token that could ride along, is auto-declared as a forced action. The verifier found that apply.ts forcedAction removed that branch on 2026-08-24 (decisions-for-the-player audit), because declining is a real choice. R36's heading carries no reversed or superseded marker, so the register and the engine disagree. Either R36 gets a reversal mark (if the audit was the owner's call) or the engine is wrong.
- <a id="F-U23-5"></a>**F-U23-5** The automatic pass is latched on actionCount, which R245(b) forbids (CT-262). Rule D2.4. R245(b) says an automatic answer (the haste ready AND the automatic pass) is latched by the fact of being unanswered, never by a state counter. The haste ready was converted (hasteAutoOut); the automatic pass still goes through takeAutoPass, keyed on actionCount.
- <a id="F-U23-6"></a>**F-U23-6** R287's deployment clause (full control holds the deployment stack) is not built (CT-185). Rule D2.7a. The owner ruled that while Control is held nothing resolves automatically even in deployment. The engine drains the deployment stack inside settle() and has no full-control flag; CT-185 (a holdStack action) is still open.
- <a id="F-U23-7"></a>**F-U23-7** Lone round-2 counterattacker is not auto-formed, against R36 (CT-251). Rule D1.2c. R36 (no amendment in the register) says a round-2 counterattack pool of exactly one unit and no ridable spell token auto-declares the one-unit formation. forcedAction's branch for it was removed 2026-08-24 and the engine offers decline/attack as a choice. Either R36 should be amended in the register or the engine restored. Already flagged by the rule as F-U23-4.
- <a id="F-U23-8"></a>**F-U23-8** R36 still registers a forced lone-counterattacker formation the engine deleted (CT-251). Rule D1.2b. R36 (unamended, no reversal marker) says a round-2 pool of exactly one sent unit with no ridable token auto-declares its attack as a forced action. forcedAction's branch was removed 2026-08-24 in the decisions-for-the-player audit and 32-cast-costs asserts it is NOT forced. Either R36 needs an amendment entry or the engine contradicts a current ruling.
- <a id="F-U24-1"></a>**F-U24-1** The in-game inspector states a type-line attribute's reminder twice on cards with an empty text box (CT-236). Rule D6.10. R282 put a card's type-line attribute reminders into its text box when the printed box is empty (21 cards). The card browser was changed to stop repeating them, but R282 says the in-game inspector still prints its own Attributes (printed) section under the box, so on those cards it states the reminder twice. R282 says the one-condition fix in inspectorHtml should be made before the ruling counts as closed. Suspected still open; not checked against the client. Re-checked: the client already drops the inspector rows the text box states (ui/main.ts inBox filter), so nothing is printed twice; what stands is the ruling's open warning, filed with the stale register text.
- <a id="F-U24-2"></a>**F-U24-2** The client's in-progress block assignment may not be re-seeded when attack columns close ranks (CT-236). Rule D6.13. R72's note says the defender's half-built block assignment in the client is keyed by attack-column index, and that a spell killing an attacker during the blocks step shifts those indices under it. The engine refuses a stale key, so the worst case is a rejected declaration, but R72 says the client should re-seed its preview when the number of columns changes and does not yet. Suspected; the note may be stale (the board has been rebuilt since) and was not checked against the client.
- <a id="F-U24-3"></a>**F-U24-3** A modified client can still see when its opponent acts inside a hidden simultaneous step (CT-106). Rule D6.1. R236 hid the opponent's haste readiness but names a residual it did not close: the state's action count is served live to both seats and rises on every action, so a modified client can tell that, and when, the opponent did something inside any hidden step (resource, haste, deployment). The shipped client draws nothing from it. Recorded so the hidden-step rule is not read as airtight; not checked against the server.
- <a id="F-U24-4"></a>**F-U24-4** Announcements of a loss the player paid for are still shown only in the game log (CT-236). Rule D7.4. R266 requires an announcement the player acts on or has lost something by to reach a surface other than the log. The verifier measured the client's own derived inventory in 244-log-is-not-the-only-surface: 39 announcements are log-only, 21 of them tier 1 (spells fizzling, costs that cannot be paid, declined costs, life not gained or not lost, nothing lured). R266 records nineteen and the test asserts 21, so the ruling's count is also stale. Re-checked: the cost-toast tier (CT-142, done; 256-cost-toasts passes) gives every tier-1 announcement a toast, so none is log-only; what stands is the ruling's "Nineteen ... remain log-only" sentence, filed with the stale register text.
- <a id="F-U24-5"></a>**F-U24-5** Looking at your own hand tells the other player nothing, not even that a hand was looked at (CT-263). Rule D6.5a. The rule says that when an effect lets a player look at a hand, the other players log says only that the hand was looked at. The U24 tester measured Thought Extraction aimed at the caster own hand: the other player log has no look line at all (it goes from Resolving straight to the discard). Aimed at the other player hand, that player log does say "looks at". Four look-at sites skip the public line when the looker owns the hand (if (who !== ctx.controller) g.revealHandTo(...)). Either the rule should say the line is written only when looking at another player hand, or the engine should write it for both. (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.)
- <a id="F-REG-1"></a>**F-REG-1** eraseFromPlay files an erased unit under its owner, but zones follow control (CT-229). Ruling register. E.eraseFromPlay emits its 'erased' event with seat: u.owner, so a stolen unit erased from play (e.g. as a cost) is filed on its OWNER's erased pile. R262 rules that zones follow control in all four per-seat destinations, and supersession.json corrects R172 §2 item 3 (the erased-from-play seat) by R262 accordingly. The Unstable-death erase route already uses the controller (binSeat = opts.binTo ?? u.controller), so only this route differs. Found in Stage B4.
- <a id="F-REG-2"></a>**F-REG-2** The Electric glossary row still says excess is lost at the end of the chain (CT-231). Ruling register. ui/glossary.ts's {Electric} row (cites R4 only) says each unit absorbs only enough to die and 'When the chain runs out the excess is lost'. R317 (amending R4) rules each hop optional (excess may stay on the current unit) and a dead-end remainder is dealt to the last unit, never lost; R340 makes the Piercing dead end elective. The row's text states superseded law; its text was left alone (B3 changes headings only).

- R180: the [Augment] box and the trigger fixtures: 218 unchecked printed promises down to 52
- R181: a check that never ran is worse than no check, because the config is what everyone reads as proof

- R199: The card was already in the battle. Nothing was waiting for it there.

- R215: a ruling number cited in the code must resolve to a ruling
- R217: two readings of the same text that agree are not two pieces of evidence
